tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\edmem\.claude\skills\hyperframes

# HyperFrames entry point

HyperFrames **renders video from HTML** — a composition is an HTML file whose DOM declares timing with `data-*` attributes, whose animation runtime is seekable, and whose media playback is owned by the framework. The full authoring contract lives in `/hyperframes-core`; read it before writing composition HTML.

## 1. Start from project state

Apply the first matching row; do not evaluate lower state rows:

| State                                                                                                                         | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Explicit port of existing Remotion source to HyperFrames                                                                      | Read `references/routes/remotion-to-hyperframes.md`, then route directly to that workflow. Skip the intent layer.                                                                                           |
| Specific operation on an existing HyperFrames project: inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, render, publish, or batch-render | Perform only that operation. Skip intent and workflow routing; load `/hyperframes-cli` and any required domain skills.                                                                                      |
| Specific edit to an existing project                                                                                          | Make the edit. Do not run the intent layer.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BRIEF.md` exists                                                                                                             | Read `workflow` and `flow`. Execute that workflow; `flow: companion` always executes in `/general-video`. Ask no brief questions.                                                                           |
| No brief, but `hyperframes.json` or `STORYBOARD.md` exists                                                                    | Resume from project files and recorded preferences. Infer the owning workflow from existing artifacts. If it cannot be determined uniquely, ask one routing-only question; do not run the intent interview. |
| Fresh creation                                                                                                                | Run the intent layer — `references/intent-interview.md` — then route once using § 2's table.                                                                                                                |

If a fresh request does not identify the subject or input, ask what the video is about before routing. Check preferences and recipes before asking anything (`references/intent-interview.md`, step 1). A `figma.com` input or a named recipe changes intake, not routing — the interview's "Adapt orthogonal inputs" section handles both.

### Keep the project's CLI current

A scaffolded project pins `hyperframes@<version>` in its `package.json` scripts so renders stay reproducible; the pin never advances on its own, and a pinned run of an older CLI prints no warning about it. When resuming a project whose scripts carry a pin, probe once before the first render-affecting command:

```bash
npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check
```

The probe is read-only and reports the pin against the latest release; keep the explicit `.` — on older CLI releases a bare `--project` followed by another flag consumes that flag as its directory value. When it reports the project behind — or any CLI output already shows it (the stderr notice `This project pins hyperframes@… (latest …)`, or `_meta.updateAvailable: true` in a `--json` result from a pinned script) — apply with `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .`, then verify with `npx hyperframes check`. A passing check confirms the project's compositions still validate on the new version — not that rendered output is frame-identical to the old pin — so a successful bump is never silent: name the old and new version in the run's summary. A project with no composition yet needs no verification. If the check fails, revert the `package.json` change, continue on the pinned version, and report which version the project stays on and why. Act on the signal rather than relaying it to the user; never leave a bumped pin unverified.

## 2. Route fresh creation

Use the first matching row. Match the requested **deliverable**, not a word or file type mentioned in passing.

| Priority | Request                                                                                                            | Workflow                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| 1        | Explicitly port an existing Remotion source                                                                        | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` |
| 2        | Author a presentation, pitch deck, or navigable interactive deck                                                   | `/slideshow`               |
| 3        | Add plain captions or subtitles to existing talking-head footage without changing it                               | `/embedded-captions`       |
| 4        | Add designed graphic overlays to existing talking-head, interview, or podcast footage without changing the footage | `/talking-head-recut`      |
| 5        | Build a beat-synced video from a music track, with no narration or website capture                                 | `/music-to-video`          |
| 6        | Create an explicitly short, unnarrated, motion-first unit, typically under 10s                                     | `/motion-graphics`         |
| 7        | Explain a GitHub pull request or code change from a PR reference                                                   | `/pr-to-video`             |
| 8        | Market or showcase a website, product site, app, or company from a URL or site-specific brief                      | `/product-launch-video`    |
| 9        | Explain a topic, article, or notes with invented visuals and no product or site capture                            | `/faceless-explainer`      |
| 10       | Any other custom video or composition                                                                              | `/general-video`           |

Before finalizing the route, read `references/routes/<workflow>.md` — one small file per route: the canonical input/output/trigger contract (available before lazy-installed workflow skills are present) plus that route's interview entry. If the candidate does not satisfy its contract, continue routing instead of forcing the match. Read only the matched route's file.

### Resolve common ambiguities

- A short animated title, logo sting, stat hit, chart hit, map hit, or standalone lower-third is `/motion-graphics` when it is unnarrated and motion is the message. A static title card, narrated sequence, longer montage, or custom loop is `/general-video`.
- An explicitly short motion graphic may use a URL, tweet, article, or screenshot as source material. A generic "make a video from this site" request is `/product-launch-video`.
- Existing footage with captions routes to `/embedded-captions`; footage with designed information cards routes to `/talking-head-recut`. Retiming, reordering, recoloring, reframing, or remixing footage is a custom edit and falls through to `/general-video`.
- A music file selects `/music-to-video` only when its beat grid drives the piece. Music used as a bed does not override the subject-matched route.
- "I want a storyboard" changes the review process, not the workflow. With no other routing signal, use `/general-video`. A confirmed sketched board may itself be the requested deliverable; the review loop defines that stop point.
- Specialized narrative workflows support up to about 3 minutes and are strongest around 30–90s. Route a clearly longer piece to `/general-video`. Length never overrides an explicit port, deck, caption, overlay, or music-driven deliverable.

## 3. Route once, then leave

For fresh creation the intent layer (`references/intent-interview.md`) runs the full conversation — memory, triage, pitch round, must-haves, run-shape, hand-off — and **ends by writing `BRIEF.md`. The brief is the only routing artifact the workflow reads**; nothing later re-opens this skill or the interview. Answer every later "what did the route require?" from `BRIEF.md`.

## 4. Install and enter the workflow

Before reading the selected workflow, install or refresh it and the core domain skills:

```bash
npx hyperframes skills update <workflow-name>
```

Use the bare name without `/`. If the command fails, surface the error; do not reconstruct the workflow from memory. Everything else about installation — the core-vs-lazy split, what `init` refreshes, diagnosis, CI opt-out, and the no-CLI fallback — lives in `references/skill-lifecycle.md`.

## 5. Load domain skills on demand

| Need                                                                                                                | Skill                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Composition structure, timing attributes, tracks, variables, determinism                                            | `/hyperframes-core`      |
| Motion rules, scene blueprints, transitions, runtime adapters                                                       | `/hyperframes-animation` |
| Seek-safe GSAP, CSS, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG, 3D keyframes, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics | `/hyperframes-keyframes` |
| Design specs, concept, palette, typography, narration, beat planning                                                | `/hyperframes-creative`  |
| Images, icons, logos, audio, captions, grades, LUTs, reusable media                                                 | `/media-use`             |
| Voiceover carve, audio effect chains, or automation envelopes on a track                                            | `/hyperframes-audio`     |
| Init, lint, check, snapshots, compare, batch render, Studio, render, publish, or diagnostics                        | `/hyperframes-cli`       |
| Registry blocks and components                                                                                      | `/hyperframes-registry`  |
| Figma assets, tokens, components, or storyboard frames as reconstructed motion                                      | `/figma`                 |

Creator edit phrases are cross-domain requests. Load every skill named in the matching row:

| Creator request                                                                                   | Required domains                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| “cut this footage”, hard cut, trim, splice, reorder, or use a source range                        | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core`; core owns `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-media-start`, and track layout.                                                            |
| zoom in here, punch-in / punch-out, smooth multi-state zoom or reframe, Ken Burns, or camera move | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-keyframes`; animate the inner visual/crop wrapper, not the timed clip.                                                     |
| match cut or whip pan camera transition                                                           | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-animation` + `/hyperframes-keyframes` + `/hyperframes-registry`; search/install a transition primitive before hand-authoring.                    |
| fade, crossfade, track gain/volume, automation, duck/carve, or audio effects                      | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-audio`; core places clips, audio mixes placed tracks.                                                                      |
| picture and sound edits that combine cuts with camera motion or mixing                            | `/general-video` + `/hyperframes-core` + `/hyperframes-keyframes` when there is visual motion + `/hyperframes-audio` when sound is faded, mixed, ducked, automated, or processed. |
| source or generate media, or preprocess an unsupported speed ramp/mid-source freeze               | `/media-use`; sourcing/generation/preprocessing only, never placed-track mixing.                                                                                                  |

Constant `data-playback-rate` is render-safe for picture and pitch-preserved
sound. It does not make source speed ramps keyframeable; preprocess ramps.
For copyable edit contracts, load `/hyperframes-core` → `references/creator-editing-recipes.md`.

Broad feedback about how photographic media looks or behaves also routes to
`/media-use`, even when the user never says “color grading” or “effect”: fix
dark/flat/boring footage, stylize a clip, hide a face, or improve a media
reveal. Read `../media-use/references/media-treatments.md` before editing a
treatment; it governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used.
Do not substitute a generic LUT, CSS filter/overlay, or opacity tween for an
existing canonical treatment primitive. Keep text/layout/motion-only edits in
their owning domain.
During a build with important photographic media, include one grounded
media-polish scan in the final quality pass; leaving suitable media unchanged is
a valid result.

Domain skills never take ownership of the end-to-end deliverable. Load only what the active workflow needs.

  ## Automated Minecraft meme-edit pipeline: tool research (Oct 2026), tuned for a PC with no NVIDIA GPU
  
  **What I checked:** I searched the web and read official pages (GitHub, PyPI, npm, the Gemini changelog, AMD ROCm docs). Anything I couldn't confirm is marked **[unverified]**.
  
  **Hardware and Python 3.14:**
  - **Hardware:** Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with Radeon 890M integrated graphics (gfx1150). AMD's Windows ROCm support tables list the HX 370 for PyTorch on ROCm 6.4.4 and 7.x. That support is preview-grade, only works on Python 3.12, and iGPU performance is modest. Plan on CPU, ONNX Runtime (CPU or DirectML), Vulkan (whisper.cpp, llama.cpp) and cloud APIs. Treat ROCm as an optional speed-up.
  - **Python 3.14:** CTranslate2 4.8.2 (the engine behind faster-whisper and WhisperX) has no Windows wheel for 3.14; its Windows wheels stop at 3.13. ROCm PyTorch wheels need 3.12. Use `uv venv --python 3.12` for every ML tool. Keep 3.14 only for glue scripts.
  
  ### 1. Programmatic composition
  - **Primary: HyperFrames** (HeyGen). Apache-2.0, npm `hyperframes` v0.8.136 (current), open-sourced 17 Apr 2026, about 57k stars. You write HTML/CSS/GSAP/Lottie and it renders MP4 through headless Chrome and FFmpeg. It needs Node 22+, which the PC has. It runs on CPU, is built for agents, and HyperFrames skills are already installed in this Claude Code session. Use it for zooms, captions, meme cards and motion graphics. `npx hyperframes init`. https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes
  - **Alternative: Remotion 4.0.533** (React). Free, including commercial use, for individuals and companies with up to 3 employees. The Company License starts at $100/month for 4+ people. v5.0 is announced but not released, and its migration notes mention a small license change. CPU rendering. https://remotion.dev/license
  - **Others:**
    - Motion Canvas and Revideo (its fork) are both MIT. Revideo has slow momentum; I couldn't confirm its latest release **[unverified]**.
    - MoviePy 2.2.1 (May 2025, no newer release found) is fine for simple Python assembly but slow.
    - **FFmpeg filtergraphs** (ffmpeg 9.0 is installed) should do the heavy lifting: cuts, concat, chromakey, loudnorm, sidechain ducking, `zoompan`/`crop` punch-ins, and burning in ASS subtitles.
  - **"video-use", identified:** https://github.com/browser-use/video-use, by the Browser Use team. MIT, about 28k stars, launched around July 2026. It is a **Claude Code skill**, not a browser agent. You drop footage in a folder and get `final.mp4`. It transcribes with ElevenLabs Scribe (an API key is required), packs the transcript into about 12 KB of markdown, has the LLM write an EDL, renders with ffmpeg, then checks its own cut points. It also does filler and dead-air removal, color grading and burned-in subtitles, and builds overlays with HyperFrames, Remotion, Manim or PIL. Install is `uv sync` plus ffmpeg. Windows isn't documented **[unverified]**. It's a strong reference architecture to fork.
  - **MCP servers:**
    - DaVinci Resolve MCP (samuelgursky): MIT, v2.60.0 (6 Jul 2026), covers the full scripting API. The free Resolve has limited external scripting support **[unverified for 20.x]**.
    - Premiere MCPs: ayushozha/AdobePremiereProMCP and others.
    - CapCut MCPs: community projects, fragile.
    - ffmpeg MCPs: KyaniteLabs/mcp-video (ffmpeg plus HyperFrames rendering), Kush36Agrawal/Video_Editor_MCP.
    - Recommendation: skip NLE MCPs. Calling the ffmpeg and HyperFrames CLIs directly is more deterministic.
  
  ### 2. Transcription and word-level timestamps
  - **Primary: faster-whisper large-v3-turbo, int8 on CPU**, via WhisperX 3.8.6 (14 Aug 2026; includes pyannote community-1 diarization and wav2vec2 word alignment). Install with `pip install whisperx` in a Python 3.12 venv. Diarization needs a free Hugging Face token. On a 12-core CPU, expect roughly real time or somewhat faster with turbo int8 **[estimate]**.
  - **Alternative: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3** through `pip install onnx-asr[cpu,hub]`. It gives native word timestamps and 25 European languages, and runs at about RTFx 36 on a desktop CPU, so it's very fast. Use **whisper.cpp v1.9.x with Vulkan** (1.8.3 added a large iGPU speed-up) if you want the 890M to help.
  - **Cloud fallbacks:** ElevenLabs Scribe (what video-use uses), and `gemini-3.5-transcribe` (GA 26 Aug 2026). Canary-Qwen 2.5B is the most accurate open model but needs NeMo and a GPU, so skip it here.
  
  ### 3. Highlight and moment detection
  - **Primary: Gemini API video understanding.** Agentic video mode shipped 1 Sep 2026 on Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite. It finds moments down to fractions of a second and uses up to 88% fewer tokens. Combine it with cheap local signals:
    - loudness and peaks with ffmpeg `ebur128`/`astats`;
    - laughter, screams and explosions from AudioSet taggers: PANNs CNN14 on CPU, or the ChuckleNet laughter models on Hugging Face (new, small, **[unverified quality]**);
    - **PySceneDetect 0.7.1** (22 Jul 2026, `pip install scenedetect`, CPU).
  - **Alternatives:**
    - Qwen3-VL 4B/8B run locally (it has timestamp-grounded video features). Running it on llama.cpp Vulkan is slow on an iGPU **[GGUF video support unverified]**.
    - Twelve Labs Marengo 3.0 / Pegasus 1.5 (API, also on Bedrock).
    - Open auto-clippers: autoclip (MIT, has MCP), SupoClip. I could not confirm that ClipsAI is still maintained; it looks dormant **[unverified]**.
  
  ### 4. Silence removal and jump cuts
  - **Primary: auto-editor 29.3.1** (Nov 2025; `pip install auto-editor`; prebuilt binary, CPU). It cuts on audio threshold or motion and can export Resolve, Premiere or FCP timelines.
  - **Alternative:** your own EDL built from word timestamps plus Silero VAD (ONNX, CPU). This also removes filler words such as "um" and "uh", which is the video-use approach.
  
  ### 5. Asset retrieval (SFX and meme library)
  - **Primary:**
    - **LAION-CLAP** for text-to-SFX search (`pip install laion-clap`, CPU fine for indexing). Research shows it best matches human judgement of what sounds and effects sound like.
    - **SigLIP 2** (via `transformers`, or ONNX for fixed-resolution variants) for meme clips and keyframes.
    - **sqlite-vec** as a single-file vector store (`pip install sqlite-vec`).
  - **Alternatives:** MS-CLAP 2023; PANNs or BEATs tags as metadata filters; LanceDB (handles multimodal data well) or Chroma. Library versions not checked **[unverified]**.
  
  ### 6. Green screen
  - **Primary:** ffmpeg `chromakey`/`colorkey` + `despill`. Meme green-screen assets key cleanly, and it runs in real time on CPU.
  - **Alternative** (for cutting yourself or the facecam out of a normal background): rembg with BiRefNet ONNX (CPU or DirectML) or RobustVideoMatting ONNX (works well on video, DirectML). SAM 2 is too heavy without a CUDA card.
  
  ### 7. Audio
  - **Loudness:** ffmpeg `loudnorm` two-pass, targeting -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP for YouTube.
  - **Ducking:** ffmpeg `sidechaincompress` with the mic as the key.
  - **Noise:**
    - Primary: DeepFilterNet3. Original wheels are outdated; the community `deepfilternet-slim` wheel bundles the C runtime **[test on Windows]**.
    - Alternative: ffmpeg `arnndn` (RNNoise, built into ffmpeg) or `afftdn`. Both CPU-only and trivial.
  - **Voice enhancement:** a simple EQ and compression chain in ffmpeg. Resemble-Enhance needs a GPU.
  
  ### 8. Generative extras (prefer hosted APIs)
  - **Music:**
    - Primary: ACE-Step 1.5 (Feb 2026; XL 4B version Apr 2026). Open source, and AMD supports it in ComfyUI with ROCm on Windows, Ryzen AI included. Slow but workable.
    - Alternative: Lyria 3.5 via the Gemini API (GA 3 Sep 2026).
  - **SFX:** ElevenLabs Sound Effects v2 API (Jan 2026, about $0.02 per effect, up to 30 s). MMAudio needs a GPU, so skip it locally.
  - **TTS:** `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (GA 22 Sep 2026) or ElevenLabs. Kokoro-82M is a CPU-friendly local option **[not re-verified this session]**.
  - **B-roll video:** use hosted models, e.g. `gemini-omni-1.1-flash` (GA 27 Aug 2026) or Veo. LTX-2 (open weights, Jan 2026) and Wan 2.2 need large NVIDIA GPUs, and Wan 2.5/2.6 never released weights.
  - **Thumbnails:** hosted image models (Gemini image, gpt-image) composited with HyperFrames or PIL **[current model IDs unverified]**.
  
  ### 9. Agentic projects and skills
  - **video-use** (above): the closest match to this goal.
  - **OpenMontage** (calesthio): about 32k stars, many pipelines and skills, turns Claude Code into a studio; aimed at generated and stock content.
  - **HyperFrames skills** (already installed here, including media-use for transcription and background removal).
  - **Remotion Skills** (Jan 2026).
  
  ### Recommended stack
  | Stage | Pick | Runs on | Install |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Orchestration | Claude Code + a fork of the video-use skill pattern | n/a | git clone |
  | Transcription | WhisperX (turbo, int8) / Parakeet onnx-asr | CPU | uv Python 3.12, pip |
  | Diarization | pyannote community-1 | CPU | via WhisperX |
  | Dead air | auto-editor 29.3.1 + Silero VAD | CPU | pip |
  | Moments | Gemini agentic video + ffmpeg ebur128 + PANNs + PySceneDetect 0.7.1 | API + CPU | pip |

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = ["numpy>=2.1", "pillow>=11"]
# ///
"""
Scan the Editing Pack and build the technical layer of the asset catalog.

    uv run studio/catalog/build_catalog.py            # incremental (skips unchanged files)
    uv run studio/catalog/build_catalog.py --full     # rescan everything

Outputs (all under studio/catalog/):
    scan.json          one record per asset: probe data, audio hit timing, key mode, thumbnails
    thumbs/<id>.jpg    per-asset thumbnail / 4-frame strip / font specimen
    sheets/<cat>_NN.jpg labelled contact sheets used by the tagging pass

Semantic tags live separately in tags/*.json and are merged by merge_catalog.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]          # .../Minecraft Channel
PACK = ROOT / "Editing Pack"
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
THUMBS = OUT / "thumbs"
SHEETS = OUT / "sheets"

AUDIO_EXT = {".mp3", ".wav", ".m4a", ".flac", ".ogg", ".aac"}
VIDEO_EXT = {".mp4", ".mov", ".webm", ".wmv", ".avi", ".mkv"}
IMAGE_EXT = {".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".webp", ".gif"}
FONT_EXT = {".ttf", ".otf"}
SKIP_EXT = {".sfk"}
SKIP_DIRS = {".data"}

# top-level folder (or folder/subfolder) -> category
CATEGORY_RULES = [
    ("Gaming Sound Effects", "sfx_meme"),
    ("MLG Sound Effects", "sfx_mlg"),
    ("Laughs", "sfx_laugh"),
    ("SFX (Sound Effects)/Minecraft", "sfx_minecraft"),
    ("SFX (Sound Effects)", "sfx_ui"),
    ("Background Music", "music"),
    ("Non-Copyright Music", "music"),
    ("Meme Videos", "meme_video"),
    ("Green Screen", "green_screen"),
    ("Transitions", "transition"),
    ("Animations", "animation"),
    ("Backgrounds", "background"),
    ("Images & Png", "image"),
    ("Images", "image"),
    ("Fonts", "font"),
]


def run(cmd: list[str], **kw) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, **kw)


def slugify(s: str) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"\(\s*\d+kbps\s*\)|\(HD\)|\[Mpgun\.com\]|- Sound Effect|Sound Effect|Gaming|\bHD\b", "", s, flags=re.I)
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", s).strip("-").lower()
    return s[:60] or "asset"


def clean_title(stem: str) -> str:
    t = re.sub(r"\(\s*\d+\s*kbps\s*\)|\(HD\)|\[Mpgun\.com\]|\(\d+k\)|\(128 kbps\)", "", stem, flags=re.I)
    t = re.sub(r"[-–]\s*(Gaming |MLG |Comical )?Sound Effects?( for editing)?\s*$", "", t.strip(), flags=re.I)
    t = t.replace("_", "'") if "_s " in t or "_m " in t or "_t " in t else t.replace("_", " ")
    return re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", t).strip(" -")


def categorize(rel: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
    rel_s = rel.as_posix()
    for prefix, cat in CATEGORY_RULES:
        if rel_s.startswith(prefix + "/"):
            sub = rel.parent.as_posix()
            return cat, sub
    return "reference", rel.parent.as_posix()


def quick_hash(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    size = p.stat().st_size
    h.update(str(size).encode())
    with p.open("rb") as f:
        h.update(f.read(65536))
        if size > 131072:
            f.seek(-65536, os.SEEK_END)
            h.update(f.read(65536))
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def ffprobe(p: Path) -> dict:
    r = run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-print_format", "json", "-show_format", "-show_streams", str(p)])
    try:
        return json.loads(r.stdout or b"{}")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}


def parse_fps(s: str | None) -> float | None:
    if not s or s == "0/0":
        return None
    n, _, d = s.partition("/")
    try:
        return round(float(n) / float(d or 1), 3)
    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- audio analysis
SR = 8000
WIN = 80  # 10 ms windows at 8 kHz


def analyse_audio(p: Path, max_seconds: float | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """Decode to 8 kHz mono and derive levels + timing landmarks.

    onset_s : first moment the sound is audible (> peak-30 dB) -> trim point
    peak_s  : loudest 10 ms window -> the 'hit' to align with the visual event
    tail_s  : last audible moment -> effective end (ignores trailing silence)
    """
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(p)]
    if max_seconds:
        cmd += ["-t", str(max_seconds)]
    cmd += ["-ac", "1", "-ar", str(SR), "-f", "s16le", "-"]
    r = run(cmd)
    if not r.stdout:
        return None
    x = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
    if x.size < WIN:
        return None
    n = x.size // WIN
    frames = x[: n * WIN].reshape(n, WIN)
    rms = np.sqrt((frames**2).mean(axis=1) + 1e-12)
    db = 20 * np.log10(rms)
    peak_idx = int(db.argmax())
    peak_db = float(db[peak_idx])
    audible = np.where(db > peak_db - 30)[0]
    onset = int(audible[0]) if audible.size else 0
    tail = int(audible[-1]) if audible.size else n - 1
    active = db[onset : tail + 1]
    return {
        "peak_dbfs": round(float(20 * np.log10(np.abs(x).max() + 1e-9)), 1),
        "rms_dbfs": round(float(20 * np.log10(np.sqrt((x**2).mean()) + 1e-12)), 1),
        "active_rms_dbfs": round(float(np.mean(active)), 1) if active.size else None,
        "onset_s": round(onset * WIN / SR, 3),
        "peak_s": round(peak_idx * WIN / SR, 3),
        "tail_s": round((tail + 1) * WIN / SR, 3),
        # crude punchiness: how far the loudest moment sits above the median -> high = transient hit
        "punch_db": round(peak_db - float(np.median(active)), 1) if active.size else None,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- video analysis
def grab_frame(p: Path, t: float, w: int = 96, h: int = 54, alpha: bool = False) -> np.ndarray | None:
    pix = "rgba" if alpha else "rgb24"
    ch = 4 if alpha else 3
    r = run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{t:.3f}", "-i", str(p), "-frames:v", "1",
             "-vf", f"scale={w}:{h}", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", pix, "-"])
    if len(r.stdout) < w * h * ch:
        return None
    return np.frombuffer(r.stdout[: w * h * ch], dtype=np.uint8).reshape(h, w, ch)


def detect_key_mode(p: Path, duration: float, has_alpha: bool) -> dict:
    ts = [duration * f for f in (0.2, 0.5, 0.8)] if duration > 0.3 else [0]
    stats = {"green": [], "blue": [], "black": [], "white": [], "transparent": []}
    for t in ts:
        fr = grab_frame(p, t, alpha=has_alpha)
        if fr is None:
            continue
        rgb = fr[..., :3].astype(np.int16)
        r_, g_, b_ = rgb[..., 0], rgb[..., 1], rgb[..., 2]
        stats["green"].append(float(((g_ > 90) & (g_ > r_ * 1.35) & (g_ > b_ * 1.35)).mean()))
        stats["blue"].append(float(((b_ > 90) & (b_ > r_ * 1.4) & (b_ > g_ * 1.15)).mean()))
        stats["black"].append(float((rgb.max(axis=2) < 22).mean()))
        stats["white"].append(float((rgb.min(axis=2) > 235).mean()))
        if has_alpha:
            stats["transparent"].append(float((fr[..., 3] < 16).mean()))
    avg = {k: round(sum(v) / len(v), 3) if v else 0.0 for k, v in stats.items()}
    if has_alpha and avg["transparent"] > 0.15:
        mode = "alpha"
    elif avg["green"] > 0.25:
        mode = "green"
    elif avg["blue"] > 0.35:
        mode = "blue"
    elif avg["black"] > 0.45:
        mode = "black_screen"
    elif avg["white"] > 0.55:
        mode = "white_multiply"
    else:
        mode = "none"
    return {"key_mode": mode, "key_stats": avg}


def video_strip(p: Path, duration: float, dest: Path) -> None:
    """4 frames side by side, 240px each, checkerboard behind alpha."""
    tiles = []
    for f in (0.1, 0.35, 0.6, 0.85):
        fr = grab_frame(p, max(0.0, duration * f), 240, 135, alpha=True)
        if fr is None:
            continue
        im = Image.fromarray(fr, "RGBA")
        bg = checkerboard(240, 135)
        bg.alpha_composite(im)
        tiles.append(bg.convert("RGB"))
    if not tiles:
        return
    strip = Image.new("RGB", (240 * len(tiles), 135))
    for i, t in enumerate(tiles):
        strip.paste(t, (240 * i, 0))
    strip.save(dest, quality=80)


def checkerboard(w: int, h: int, s: int = 12) -> Image.Image:
    im = Image.new("RGBA", (w, h), (200, 200, 200, 255))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    for y in range(0, h, s):
        for x in range(0, w, s):
            if (x // s + y // s) % 2:
                d.rectangle([x, y, x + s - 1, y + s - 1], fill=(150, 150, 150, 255))
    return im


def image_thumb(p: Path, dest: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        with Image.open(p) as im:
            info = {"width": im.width, "height": im.height,
                    "animated": bool(getattr(im, "is_animated", False)),
                    "frames": int(getattr(im, "n_frames", 1))}
            im.seek(0)
            rgba = im.convert("RGBA")
            a = np.asarray(rgba)[..., 3]
            info["has_alpha"] = bool((a < 250).mean() > 0.02)
            rgba.thumbnail((240, 240))
            bg = checkerboard(240, 240)
            bg.alpha_composite(rgba, ((240 - rgba.width) // 2, (240 - rgba.height) // 2))
            bg.convert("RGB").save(dest, quality=80)
            return info
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"error": str(e)}


def font_specimen(p: Path, dest: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        f_big = ImageFont.truetype(str(p), 44)
        f_small = ImageFont.truetype(str(p), 24)
        im = Image.new("RGB", (720, 130), (24, 24, 28))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
        d.text((14, 8), "WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!", font=f_big, fill=(255, 230, 60), stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0))
        d.text((14, 80), "Creeper aw man 0123456789", font=f_small, fill=(240, 240, 240))
        im.save(dest, quality=85)
        name = f_big.getname()
        return {"family": name[0], "style": name[1]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"error": str(e)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-file
def scan_file(p: Path) -> dict:
    rel = p.relative_to(PACK)
    ext = p.suffix.lower()
    cat, sub = categorize(rel)
    rec: dict = {
        "path": rel.as_posix(),
        "category": cat,
        "subfolder": sub,
        "filename": p.name,
        "title": clean_title(p.stem),
        "ext": ext,
        "size_bytes": p.stat().st_size,
        "mtime": int(p.stat().st_mtime),
        "hash": quick_hash(p),
    }
    rec["id"] = f"{cat}.{slugify(p.stem)}"
    thumb = THUMBS / f"{rec['hash']}.jpg"

    if ext in AUDIO_EXT or ext in VIDEO_EXT:
        pr = ffprobe(p)
        fmt = pr.get("format", {})
        vs = next((s for s in pr.get("streams", []) if s.get("codec_type") == "video"
                   and not s.get("disposition", {}).get("attached_pic")), None)
        aus = next((s for s in pr.get("streams", []) if s.get("codec_type") == "audio"), None)
        dur = float(fmt.get("duration") or 0)
        rec["duration_s"] = round(dur, 3)
        rec["has_audio"] = aus is not None
        if aus:
            rec["audio"] = {"codec": aus.get("codec_name"), "sample_rate": int(aus.get("sample_rate", 0) or 0),
                            "channels": aus.get("channels")}
        if ext in VIDEO_EXT and vs:
            rec["kind"] = "video"
            pix = vs.get("pix_fmt", "") or ""
            alpha_tag = (vs.get("tags", {}) or {}).get("alpha_mode") == "1"
            has_alpha = alpha_tag or any(k in pix for k in ("yuva", "rgba", "argb", "bgra", "gbrap", "ya"))
            if ext == ".webm" and not has_alpha:
                # vp8/vp9 alpha lives in side data; decode with libvpx to check
                has_alpha = alpha_tag
            rec["video"] = {"codec": vs.get("codec_name"), "width": vs.get("width"), "height": vs.get("height"),
                            "fps": parse_fps(vs.get("avg_frame_rate") or vs.get("r_frame_rate")),
                            "pix_fmt": pix, "has_alpha": bool(has_alpha)}
            rec.update(detect_key_mode(p, dur, bool(has_alpha)))
            video_strip(p, dur, thumb)
        else:
            rec["kind"] = "audio"
        if aus:
            # music: only analyse the first 4 minutes, it's plenty for levels
            a = analyse_audio(p, max_seconds=240 if dur > 240 else None)
            if a:
                rec["audio_analysis"] = a
    elif ext in IMAGE_EXT:
        rec["kind"] = "image"
        rec["image"] = image_thumb(p, thumb)
    elif ext in FONT_EXT:
        rec["kind"] = "font"
        rec["font"] = font_specimen(p, thumb)
    else:
        rec["kind"] = "other"
        rec["category"] = "reference"
        if ext == ".txt" and rec["size_bytes"] < 4096:
            rec["text"] = p.read_text(errors="replace").strip()
    if thumb.exists():
        rec["thumb"] = thumb.relative_to(OUT).as_posix()
    return rec


def iter_pack():
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(PACK):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        for fn in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / fn
            if p.suffix.lower() in SKIP_EXT:
                continue
            yield p


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- contact sheets
def build_sheets(records: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Labelled contact sheets per category so a vision model can tag visuals in bulk."""
    for old in SHEETS.glob("*.jpg"):
        old.unlink()
    try:
        label_font = ImageFont.truetype("arial.ttf", 15)
    except OSError:
        label_font = ImageFont.load_default()
    by_cat: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in records:
        if r.get("thumb") and not r.get("duplicate_of"):
            by_cat.setdefault(r["category"], []).append(r)
    for cat, recs in by_cat.items():
        recs.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"])
        wide = recs[0]["kind"] == "video" or cat == "font"
        per = 8 if wide else 20
        for n in range(0, len(recs), per):
            chunk = recs[n : n + per]
            if wide:
                cell_w, cell_h, cols = 960 if cat != "font" else 720, 160, 1
            else:
                cell_w, cell_h, cols = 240, 270, 5
            rows = (len(chunk) + cols - 1) // cols
            sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cell_w * cols, cell_h * rows), (16, 16, 16))
            d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
            for i, r in enumerate(chunk):
                x, y = (i % cols) * cell_w, (i // cols) * cell_h
                with Image.open(OUT / r["thumb"]) as t:
                    t = t.copy()
                t.thumbnail((cell_w, cell_h - 22))
                sheet.paste(t, (x, y + 22))
                label = f"{r['id']}"
                if r.get("duration_s"):
                    label += f"  {r['duration_s']:.1f}s"
                if r.get("key_mode") and r["key_mode"] != "none":
                    label += f"  [{r['key_mode']}]"
                d.text((x + 4, y + 3), label[: (cell_w // 8)], font=label_font, fill=(255, 220, 80))
            sheet.save(SHEETS / f"{cat}_{n // per:02d}.jpg", quality=82)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--full", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=min(12, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    THUMBS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    SHEETS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    scan_path = OUT / "scan.json"
    prev = {}
    if scan_path.exists() and not args.full:
        prev = {r["path"]: r for r in json.loads(scan_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}

    files = list(iter_pack())
    todo, records = [], []
    for p in files:
        rel = p.relative_to(PACK).as_posix()
        old = prev.get(rel)
        if old and old.get("mtime") == int(p.stat().st_mtime) and old.get("size_bytes") == p.stat().st_size:
            records.append(old)
        else:
            todo.append(p)
    print(f"{len(files)} files, {len(todo)} to scan", flush=True)

    done = 0
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as ex:
        for rec in ex.map(scan_file, todo):
            records.append(rec)
            done += 1
            if done % 50 == 0:
                print(f"  {done}/{len(todo)}", flush=True)

    # stable unique ids + duplicate detection
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"])
    seen_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
    first_by_hash: dict[str, str] = {}
    for r in records:
        r.pop("duplicate_of", None)
        base = r["id"].rsplit("~", 1)[0]
        k = seen_ids.get(base, 0)
        r["id"] = base if k == 0 else f"{base}~{k + 1}"
        seen_ids[base] = k + 1
        if r["hash"] in first_by_hash:
            r["duplicate_of"] = first_by_hash[r["hash"]]
        else:
            first_by_hash[r["hash"]] = r["id"]

    scan_path.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    build_sheets(records)
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter(r["category"] for r in records if not r.get("duplicate_of"))
    print("categories:", dict(c))
    print("duplicates:", sum(1 for r in records if r.get("duplicate_of")))
    print("key modes:", dict(Counter(r.get("key_mode") for r in records if r.get("kind") == "video")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def analyse_audio(p: Path, max_seconds: float | None = None) -> dict | None:

            im.seek(0)

            a = np.asarray(rgba)[..., 3]
            info["has_alpha"] = bool((a < 250).mean() > 0.02)

            bg.alpha_composite(rgba, ((240 - rgba.width) // 2, (240 - rgba.height) // 2))

        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
        d.text((14, 8), "WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!", font=f_big, fill=(255, 230, 60), stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0))

            chunk = recs[n : n + per]

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--full", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=min(12, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    THUMBS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    SHEETS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    scan_path = OUT / "scan.json"
    prev = {}
    if scan_path.exists() and not args.full:
        prev = {r["path"]: r for r in json.loads(scan_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}

    files = list(iter_pack())
    todo, records = [], []
    for p in files:
        rel = p.relative_to(PACK).as_posix()
        old = prev.get(rel)
        if old and old.get("mtime") == int(p.stat().st_mtime) and old.get("size_bytes") == p.stat().st_size:
            records.append(old)
        else:
            todo.append(p)
    print(f"{len(files)} files, {len(todo)} to scan", flush=True)

    done = 0
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as ex:
        for rec in ex.map(scan_file, todo):
            records.append(rec)
            done += 1
            if done % 50 == 0:
                print(f"  {done}/{len(todo)}", flush=True)

    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"])
    seen_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
    first_by_hash: dict[str, str] = {}
    for r in records:
        r.pop("duplicate_of", None)
        base = r["id"].rsplit("~", 1)[0]
        k = seen_ids.get(base, 0)
        r["id"] = base if k == 0 else f"{base}~{k + 1}"
        seen_ids[base] = k + 1
        if r["hash"] in first_by_hash:
            r["duplicate_of"] = first_by_hash[r["hash"]]
        else:
            first_by_hash[r["hash"]] = r["id"]

    scan_path.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    build_sheets(records)
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter(r["category"] for r in records if not r.get("duplicate_of"))
    print("categories:", dict(c))
    print("duplicates:", sum(1 for r in records if r.get("duplicate_of")))
    print("key modes:", dict(Counter(r.get("key_mode") for r in records if r.get("kind") == "video")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def video_strip(p: Path, duration: float, dest: Path) -> None:
    """4 frames side by side, 240px each, checkerboard behind alpha."""
    tiles = []
    for f in (0.1, 0.35, 0.6, 0.85):
        fr = grab_frame(p, max(0.0, duration * f), 240, 135, alpha=True)
        if fr is None:
            continue
        im = Image.fromarray(fr, "RGBA")
        bg = checkerboard(240, 135)
        bg.alpha_composite(im)
        tiles.append(bg.convert("RGB"))
    if not tiles:
        return
    strip = Image.new("RGB", (240 * len(tiles), 135))
    for i, t in enumerate(tiles):
        strip.paste(t, (240 * i, 0))
    strip.save(dest, quality=80)


def checkerboard(w: int, h: int, s: int = 12) -> Image.Image:
    im = Image.new("RGBA", (w, h), (200, 200, 200, 255))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    for y in range(0, h, s):
        for x in range(0, w, s):
            if (x // s + y // s) % 2:
                d.rectangle([x, y, x + s - 1, y + s - 1], fill=(150, 150, 150, 255))
    return im


def image_thumb(p: Path, dest: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        with Image.open(p) as im:
            info = {"width": im.width, "height": im.height,
                    "animated": bool(getattr(im, "is_animated", False)),
                    "frames": int(getattr(im, "n_frames", 1))}
            im.seek(0)
            rgba = im.convert("RGBA")
            a = np.asarray(rgba)[..., 3]
            info["has_alpha"] = bool((a < 250).mean() > 0.02)
            rgba.thumbnail((240, 240))
            bg = checkerboard(240, 240)
            bg.alpha_composite(rgba, ((240 - rgba.width) // 2, (240 - rgba.height) // 2))
            bg.convert("RGB").save(dest, quality=80)
            return info
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"error": str(e)}


def font_specimen(p: Path, dest: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        f_big = ImageFont.truetype(str(p), 44)
        f_small = ImageFont.truetype(str(p), 24)
        im = Image.new("RGB", (720, 130), (24, 24, 28))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
        d.text((14, 8), "WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!", font=f_big, fill=(255, 230, 60), stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0))
        d.text((14, 80), "Creeper aw man 0123456789", font=f_small, fill=(240, 240, 240))
        im.save(dest, quality=85)
        name = f_big.getname()
        return {"family": name[0], "style": name[1]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"error": str(e)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-file
def scan_file(p: Path) -> dict:
    rel = p.relative_to(PACK)
    ext = p.suffix.lower()
    cat, sub = categorize(rel)
    rec: dict = {
        "path": rel.as_posix(),
        "category": cat,
        "subfolder": sub,
        "filename": p.name,
        "title": clean_title(p.stem),
        "ext": ext,
        "size_bytes": p.stat().st_size,
        "mtime": int(p.stat().st_mtime),
        "hash": quick_hash(p),
    }
    rec["id"] = f"{cat}.{slugify(p.stem)}"
    thumb = THUMBS / f"{rec['hash']}.jpg"

    if ext in AUDIO_EXT or ext in VIDEO_EXT:
        pr = ffprobe(p)
        fmt = pr.get("format", {})
        vs = next((s for s in pr.get("streams", []) if s.get("codec_type") == "video"
                   and not s.get("disposition", {}).get("attached_pic")), None)
        aus = next((s for s in pr.get("streams", []) if s.get("codec_type") == "audio"), None)
        dur = float(fmt.get("duration") or 0)
        rec["duration_s"] = round(dur, 3)
        rec["has_audio"] = aus is not None
        if aus:
            rec["audio"] = {"codec": aus.get("codec_name"), "sample_rate": int(aus.get("sample_rate", 0) or 0),
                            "channels": aus.get("channels")}
        if ext in VIDEO_EXT and vs:
            rec["kind"] = "video"
            pix = vs.get("pix_fmt", "") or ""
            alpha_tag = (vs.get("tags", {}) or {}).get("alpha_mode") == "1"
            has_alpha = alpha_tag or any(k in pix for k in ("yuva", "rgba", "argb", "bgra", "gbrap", "ya"))
            if ext == ".webm" and not has_alpha:
                # vp8/vp9 alpha lives in side data; decode with libvpx to check
                has_alpha = alpha_tag
            rec["video"] = {"codec": vs.get("codec_name"), "width": vs.get("width"), "height": vs.get("height"),
                            "fps": parse_fps(vs.get("avg_frame_rate") or vs.get("r_frame_rate")),
                            "pix_fmt": pix, "has_alpha": bool(has_alpha)}
            rec.update(detect_key_mode(p, dur, bool(has_alpha)))
            video_strip(p, dur, thumb)
        else:
            rec["kind"] = "audio"
        if aus:
            # music: only analyse the first 4 minutes, it's plenty for levels
            a = analyse_audio(p, max_seconds=240 if dur > 240 else None)
            if a:
                rec["audio_analysis"] = a
    elif ext in IMAGE_EXT:
        rec["kind"] = "image"
        rec["image"] = image_thumb(p, thumb)
    elif ext in FONT_EXT:
        rec["kind"] = "font"
        rec["font"] = font_specimen(p, thumb)
    else:
        rec["kind"] = "other"
        rec["category"] = "reference"
        if ext == ".txt" and rec["size_bytes"] < 4096:
            rec["text"] = p.read_text(errors="replace").strip()
    if thumb.exists():
        rec["thumb"] = thumb.relative_to(OUT).as_posix()
    return rec


def iter_pack():
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(PACK):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS]
        for fn in filenames:
            p = Path(dirpath) / fn
            if p.suffix.lower() in SKIP_EXT:
                continue
            yield p


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- contact sheets
def build_sheets(records: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Labelled contact sheets per category so a vision model can tag visuals in bulk."""
    for old in SHEETS.glob("*.jpg"):
        old.unlink()
    try:
        label_font = ImageFont.truetype("arial.ttf", 15)
    except OSError:
        label_font = ImageFont.load_default()
    by_cat: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for r in records:
        if r.get("thumb") and not r.get("duplicate_of"):
            by_cat.setdefault(r["category"], []).append(r)
    for cat, recs in by_cat.items():
        recs.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"])
        wide = recs[0]["kind"] == "video" or cat == "font"
        per = 8 if wide else 20
        for n in range(0, len(recs), per):
            chunk = recs[n : n + per]
            if wide:
                cell_w, cell_h, cols = 960 if cat != "font" else 720, 160, 1
            else:
                cell_w, cell_h, cols = 240, 270, 5
            rows = (len(chunk) + cols - 1) // cols
            sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cell_w * cols, cell_h * rows), (16, 16, 16))
            d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
            for i, r in enumerate(chunk):
                x, y = (i % cols) * cell_w, (i // cols) * cell_h
                with Image.open(OUT / r["thumb"]) as t:
                    t = t.copy()
                t.thumbnail((cell_w, cell_h - 22))
                sheet.paste(t, (x, y + 22))
                label = f"{r['id']}"
                if r.get("duration_s"):
                    label += f"  {r['duration_s']:.1f}s"
                if r.get("key_mode") and r["key_mode"] != "none":
                    label += f"  [{r['key_mode']}]"
                d.text((x + 4, y + 3), label[: (cell_w // 8)], font=label_font, fill=(255, 220, 80))
            sheet.save(SHEETS / f"{cat}_{n // per:02d}.jpg", quality=82)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--full", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=min(12, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    THUMBS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    SHEETS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    scan_path = OUT / "scan.json"
    prev = {}
    if scan_path.exists() and not args.full:
        prev = {r["path"]: r for r in json.loads(scan_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}

    files = list(iter_pack())
    todo, records = [], []
    for p in files:
        rel = p.relative_to(PACK).as_posix()
        old = prev.get(rel)
        if old and old.get("mtime") == int(p.stat().st_mtime) and old.get("size_bytes") == p.stat().st_size:
            records.append(old)
        else:
            todo.append(p)
    print(f"{len(files)} files, {len(todo)} to scan", flush=True)

    done = 0
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as ex:
        for rec in ex.map(scan_file, todo):
            records.append(rec)
            done += 1
            if done % 50 == 0:
                print(f"  {done}/{len(todo)}", flush=True)

    # stable unique ids + duplicate detection
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["path"])
    seen_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
    first_by_hash: dict[str, str] = {}
    for r in records:
        r.pop("duplicate_of", None)
        base = r["id"].rsplit("~", 1)[0]
        k = seen_ids.get(base, 0)
        r["id"] = base if k == 0 else f"{base}~{k + 1}"
        seen_ids[base] = k + 1
        if r["hash"] in first_by_hash:
            r["duplicate_of"] = first_by_hash[r["hash"]]
        else:
            first_by_hash[r["hash"]] = r["id"]

    scan_path.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    build_sheets(records)
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter(r["category"] for r in records if not r.get("duplicate_of"))
    print("categories:", dict(c))
    print("duplicates:", sum(1 for r in records if r.get("duplicate_of")))
    print("key modes:", dict(Counter(r.get("key_mode") for r in records if r.get("kind") == "video")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    - CapCut MCPs: community projects, fragile.
    - ffmpeg MCPs: KyaniteLabs/mcp-video (ffmpeg plus HyperFrames rendering), Kush36Agrawal/Video_Editor_MCP.
    - Recommendation: skip NLE MCPs. Calling the ffmpeg and HyperFrames CLIs directly is more deterministic.
  
  ### 2. Transcription and word-level timestamps
  - **Primary: faster-whisper large-v3-turbo, int8 on CPU**, via WhisperX 3.8.6 (14 Aug 2026; includes pyannote community-1 diarization and wav2vec2 word alignment). Install with `pip install whisperx` in a Python 3.12 venv. Diarization needs a free Hugging Face token. On a 12-core CPU, expect roughly real time or somewhat faster with turbo int8 **[estimate]**.
  - **Alternative: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3** through `pip install onnx-asr[cpu,hub]`. It gives native word timestamps and 25 European languages, and runs at about RTFx 36 on a desktop CPU, so it's very fast. Use **whisper.cpp v1.9.x with Vulkan** (1.8.3 added a large iGPU speed-up) if you want the 890M to help.
  - **Cloud fallbacks:** ElevenLabs Scribe (what video-use uses), and `gemini-3.5-transcribe` (GA 26 Aug 2026). Canary-Qwen 2.5B is the most accurate open model but needs NeMo and a GPU, so skip it here.
  
  ### 3. Highlight and moment detection
  - **Primary: Gemini API video understanding.** Agentic video mode shipped 1 Sep 2026 on Gemini 3.7 Flash, 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite. It finds moments down to fractions of a second and uses up to 88% fewer tokens. Combine it with cheap local signals:
    - loudness and peaks with ffmpeg `ebur128`/`astats`;
    - laughter, screams and explosions from AudioSet taggers: PANNs CNN14 on CPU, or the ChuckleNet laughter models on Hugging Face (new, small, **[unverified quality]**);
    - **PySceneDetect 0.7.1** (22 Jul 2026, `pip install scenedetect`, CPU).
  - **Alternatives:**
    - Qwen3-VL 4B/8B run locally (it has timestamp-grounded video features). Running it on llama.cpp Vulkan is slow on an iGPU **[GGUF video support unverified]**.
    - Twelve Labs Marengo 3.0 / Pegasus 1.5 (API, also on Bedrock).
    - Open auto-clippers: autoclip (MIT, has MCP), SupoClip. I could not confirm that ClipsAI is still maintained; it looks dormant **[unverified]**.
  
  ### 4. Silence removal and jump cuts
  - **Primary: auto-editor 29.3.1** (Nov 2025; `pip install auto-editor`; prebuilt binary, CPU). It cuts on audio threshold or motion and can export Resolve, Premiere or FCP timelines.
  - **Alternative:** your own EDL built from word timestamps plus Silero VAD (ONNX, CPU). This also removes filler words such as "um" and "uh", which is the video-use approach.
  
  ### 5. Asset retrieval (SFX and meme library)
  - **Primary:**
    - **LAION-CLAP** for text-to-SFX search (`pip install laion-clap`, CPU fine for indexing). Research shows it best matches human judgement of what sounds and effects sound like.
    - **SigLIP 2** (via `transformers`, or ONNX for fixed-resolution variants) for meme clips and keyframes.
    - **sqlite-vec** as a single-file vector store (`pip install sqlite-vec`).
  - **Alternatives:** MS-CLAP 2023; PANNs or BEATs tags as metadata filters; LanceDB (handles multimodal data well) or Chroma. Library versions not checked **[unverified]**.
  
  ### 6. Green screen
  - **Primary:** ffmpeg `chromakey`/`colorkey` + `despill`. Meme green-screen assets key cleanly, and it runs in real time on CPU.
  - **Alternative** (for cutting yourself or the facecam out of a normal background): rembg with BiRefNet ONNX (CPU or DirectML) or RobustVideoMatting ONNX (works well on video, DirectML). SAM 2 is too heavy without a CUDA card.
  
  ### 7. Audio
  - **Loudness:** ffmpeg `loudnorm` two-pass, targeting -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP for YouTube.
  - **Ducking:** ffmpeg `sidechaincompress` with the mic as the key.
  - **Noise:**
    - Primary: DeepFilterNet3. Original wheels are outdated; the community `deepfilternet-slim` wheel bundles the C runtime **[test on Windows]**.
    - Alternative: ffmpeg `arnndn` (RNNoise, built into ffmpeg) or `afftdn`. Both CPU-only and trivial.
  - **Voice enhancement:** a simple EQ and compression chain in ffmpeg. Resemble-Enhance needs a GPU.
  
  ### 8. Generative extras (prefer hosted APIs)
  - **Music:**
    - Primary: ACE-Step 1.5 (Feb 2026; XL 4B version Apr 2026). Open source, and AMD supports it in ComfyUI with ROCm on Windows, Ryzen AI included. Slow but workable.
    - Alternative: Lyria 3.5 via the Gemini API (GA 3 Sep 2026).
  - **SFX:** ElevenLabs Sound Effects v2 API (Jan 2026, about $0.02 per effect, up to 30 s). MMAudio needs a GPU, so skip it locally.
  - **TTS:** `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (GA 22 Sep 2026) or ElevenLabs. Kokoro-82M is a CPU-friendly local option **[not re-verified this session]**.
  - **B-roll video:** use hosted models, e.g. `gemini-omni-1.1-flash` (GA 27 Aug 2026) or Veo. LTX-2 (open weights, Jan 2026) and Wan 2.2 need large NVIDIA GPUs, and Wan 2.5/2.6 never released weights.
  - **Thumbnails:** hosted image models (Gemini image, gpt-image) composited with HyperFrames or PIL **[current model IDs unverified]**.
  
  ### 9. Agentic projects and skills
  - **video-use** (above): the closest match to this goal.
  - **OpenMontage** (calesthio): about 32k stars, many pipelines and skills, turns Claude Code into a studio; aimed at generated and stock content.
  - **HyperFrames skills** (already installed here, including media-use for transcription and background removal).
  - **Remotion Skills** (Jan 2026).
  
  ### Recommended stack
  | Stage | Pick | Runs on | Install |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Orchestration | Claude Code + a fork of the video-use skill pattern | n/a | git clone |
  | Transcription | WhisperX (turbo, int8) / Parakeet onnx-asr | CPU | uv Python 3.12, pip |
  | Diarization | pyannote community-1 | CPU | via WhisperX |
  | Dead air | auto-editor 29.3.1 + Silero VAD | CPU | pip |
  | Moments | Gemini agentic video + ffmpeg ebur128 + PANNs + PySceneDetect 0.7.1 | API + CPU | pip |
  | Asset search | LAION-CLAP + SigLIP 2 + sqlite-vec | CPU | pip |
  | Composition | HyperFrames 0.8.x (Remotion as backup) | CPU/Chrome | npx |
  | Cuts and final mux | FFmpeg 9 filtergraphs | CPU (AMF encode) | installed |
  | Green screen | ffmpeg chromakey; RVM/BiRefNet ONNX | CPU/DirectML | pip |
  | Audio | loudnorm, sidechaincompress, arnndn / DeepFilterNet | CPU | ffmpeg / pip |
  | Generation | ElevenLabs SFX v2, Gemini TTS, Lyria 3.5 / ACE-Step 1.5, hosted video | API (ROCm optional) | API keys |

"""Split scan.json into compact manifests for the semantic tagging pass.

    python studio/catalog/make_tag_batches.py

Writes studio/catalog/tag_batches/<batch>.json. Each tagger writes tags/<batch>.json.
Only assets without an existing tag entry are included, so re-running after adding
new files to the Editing Pack yields small top-up batches.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
scan = json.loads((OUT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

tagged: set[str] = set()
for f in (OUT / "tags").glob("*.json"):
    tagged |= {t["id"] for t in json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}

BATCHES = {
    "sfx_meme_a": lambda r: r["category"] == "sfx_meme" and r["filename"][0].upper() < "M",
    "sfx_meme_b": lambda r: r["category"] == "sfx_meme" and r["filename"][0].upper() >= "M",
    "sfx_other": lambda r: r["category"] in ("sfx_mlg", "sfx_laugh", "sfx_ui", "sfx_minecraft"),
    "music": lambda r: r["category"] == "music",
    "memes_greenscreen": lambda r: r["category"] in ("meme_video", "green_screen"),
    "motion": lambda r: r["category"] in ("transition", "animation", "background"),
    "images_fonts": lambda r: r["category"] in ("image", "font"),
}


def compact(r: dict) -> dict:
    c = {k: r[k] for k in ("id", "path", "title", "kind") if k in r}
    for k in ("duration_s", "key_mode", "key_color", "has_audio"):
        if k in r:
            c[k] = r[k]
    if a := r.get("audio_analysis"):
        c["audio"] = {k: a[k] for k in ("onset_s", "peak_s", "tail_s", "active_rms_dbfs", "punch_db")}
    if v := r.get("video"):
        c["res"] = f"{v['width']}x{v['height']}@{v['fps']}"
    if im := r.get("image"):
        c["res"] = f"{im.get('width')}x{im.get('height')}"
        c["alpha"] = im.get("has_alpha")
        c["animated"] = im.get("animated")
    return c


(OUT / "tag_batches").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(OUT / "tags").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
live = [r for r in scan if not r.get("duplicate_of") and r["category"] != "reference" and r["id"] not in tagged]
for name, pred in BATCHES.items():
    recs = [compact(r) for r in live if pred(r)]
    if not recs:
        continue
    cats = sorted({r["category"] for r in scan if pred(r)})
    sheets = sorted(p.name for p in (OUT / "sheets").glob("*.jpg") if p.name.rsplit("_", 1)[0] in cats)
    (OUT / "tag_batches" / f"{name}.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"batch": name, "sheets": sheets, "assets": recs}, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{name:20s} {len(recs):4d} assets, {len(sheets)} sheets")

# Asset tagging instructions

You are tagging assets from a Minecraft YouTube editing pack so an automated editor can pick the
right sound / clip / graphic for each moment of a funny, fast-paced Minecraft gameplay video.

**Inputs**
- `studio/catalog/tag_batches/<batch>.json`: the assets to tag, with technical data:
  - `duration_s`
  - `audio.onset_s`: when sound starts
  - `audio.peak_s`: the loudest "hit" moment
  - `audio.tail_s`: when the sound ends
  - `audio.punch_db`: a high value means a sharp transient
  - `key_mode` and `key_color`: auto-detected green, blue, black, or alpha background
- `studio/catalog/sheets/*.jpg`: labelled contact sheets showing thumbnails or 4-frame strips. The label is the asset id. **Look at every sheet for visual batches.**
- `studio/catalog/taxonomy.json`: the ONLY allowed values for `moments`, `roles`, `placement`, `key_mode`, `content_rating`, `copyright_risk`.

**Output.** Write `studio/catalog/tags/<batch>.json`: a JSON array with exactly one object per asset in the batch.

```json
{
  "id": "sfx_meme.bruh",                      // copy exactly
  "description": "Deadpan male 'bruh' voice line",  // what it IS + what it sounds/looks like, 1 sentence
  "moments": ["fail", "awkward", "confusion"],  // 1-5 from taxonomy.moments, best first
  "roles": ["voice_line", "reaction"],          // 1-3 from taxonomy.roles
  "tags": ["bruh", "deadpan", "male voice"],    // free-form search keywords (quotes said, characters, objects)
  "quote": "bruh",                              // spoken words if any, else null
  "mood": "deadpan",                            // one or two words
  "energy": 2,                                  // 1 calm .. 5 chaos
  "content_rating": "clean",                    // clean | mild | explicit | banned
  "copyright_risk": "low",                      // low | medium | high
  "placement": "audio_only",                    // from taxonomy.placement
  "key_mode": "none",                           // confirm or correct the auto-detected value
  "use_window": null,                           // [in_s, out_s] best sub-range if only part is useful, else null
  "volume_db": 0,                               // suggested gain vs. normal SFX (-6 if very loud, +3 if quiet)
  "frequency": "common",                        // how often an editor may reuse it: signature | common | rare | once_per_video
  "notes": null                                 // anything an editor must know (e.g. "has its own sound", "starts with 1s silence", "watermark")
}
```

**Rules**
- `content_rating` must be honest. It protects monetization.
  - `banned`: any racial slur, including the n-word and spelled variants; homophobic jokes ("ha gay"); sexual phrases; harassment of real private people; mocking disability ("retarded"). Ban the asset if its file name or likely audio contains these.
  - `explicit`: f-word or b-word, but otherwise fine.
  - `mild`: damn, hell, ass, crude humour.
  - When unsure, rate it more strictly.
- `copyright_risk`:
  - `high`: commercial songs, Nintendo / game OST tracks, film scores, and long clips from movies or TV.
  - `medium`: brief TV, film, or game sound bites.
  - `low`: generic and royalty-free material, and the pack's "Non-Copyright Music" folder. Kevin MacLeod tracks are `low` but need credit; put "credit: Kevin MacLeod (CC-BY)" in `notes`.
- Pick `moments` by how a funny Minecraft editor would actually use the asset. For example:
  - Sad violin: `sad`, `fail`, `irony`.
  - Vine boom: `emphasis`, `shock`, `punchline`.
  - Bonk: `combat`, `fail`, `emphasis`.
  - SpongeBob time card: `time_skip`.
- For music, also set `tags` to include tempo feel (slow / mid / fast), genre, and the vibe it suits, e.g. "sneaky", "building montage", "boss fight", "comedic tension". Numbered files (`2.mp3`) have no info in the name. Use the loudness data, mark `description` "unidentified track", and keep the moments generic (`exploring`, `building`). Never invent a song identity.
- For visuals, describe what appears on screen and when (e.g. "confetti bursts in first 2s, clears by 10s"). Correct `key_mode` from the sheet if the auto-detect was wrong. For example, blue skies or blueprint backgrounds are `none`, not `blue`.
- Validate before finishing: the output must parse as JSON, have the same count as the batch, include every id, and use only taxonomy values. Run a quick Python check to confirm.
