"""Tagging batches for Editing Pack/_Incoming (new archives), plus auto-tags for Minecraft item icons.

    python studio/catalog/make_incoming_batches.py

* Minecraft item icons are tagged from their file names (no vision needed) -> tags/incoming_items.json
* everything else is split into themed batches with batch-specific labelled contact sheets:
  tag_batches/incoming_<name>.json  +  sheets/incoming_<name>_NN.jpg
"""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
scan = json.loads((OUT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
aliases = json.loads((OUT / "aliases.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if (OUT / "aliases.json").exists() else {}
inc = [r for r in scan if r["path"].startswith("_Incoming/") and not r.get("duplicate_of") and r["kind"] != "other"]

ITEM_MOMENTS = [
    (r"diamond", ["loot", "flex"]), (r"netherite|emerald|gold|treasure|totem|enchanted", ["loot", "small_win"]),
    (r"sword|axe|bow|crossbow|trident|mace|shield", ["combat"]), (r"tnt|fire_charge|end_crystal", ["explosion"]),
    (r"apple|bread|beef|pork|chicken|mutton|cod|salmon|potato|carrot|cake|cookie|pie|stew|soup|melon|berries",
     ["eat_drink"]), (r"potion|bottle|bucket", ["eat_drink", "small_win"]), (r"pickaxe|shovel|hoe", ["building"]),
    (r"elytra|firework|ender_pearl", ["speed", "flex"]), (r"spawn_egg", ["jumpscare"]), (r"bed\b|_bed$", ["time_skip"]),
    (r"clock|compass|map", ["exploring", "time_skip"]), (r"music_disc", ["intro"]),
]


def item_tags(r: dict) -> dict:
    stem = PurePosixPath(r["path"]).stem
    words = stem.replace("_", " ")
    moments = next((m for rx, m in ITEM_MOMENTS if re.search(rx, stem)), ["building"])
    al = [a.replace("_", " ") for a in aliases.get(stem, [])]
    return {"id": r["id"], "description": f"Minecraft {words} icon (official texture render)",
            "moments": moments, "roles": ["sticker"], "tags": ["minecraft", "item", words, *al],
            "quote": None, "mood": "neutral", "energy": 1, "content_rating": "clean", "copyright_risk": "medium",
            "placement": "overlay_any", "key_mode": "alpha" if (r.get("image") or {}).get("has_alpha") else "none",
            "use_window": None, "volume_db": 0, "frequency": "common",
            "notes": ("same texture as: " + ", ".join(al)) if al else None,
            "category": "image", "folder": "Images/Minecraft Items", "clean_name": None}


items = [r for r in inc if "/Minecraft_Items_latest_AllVisible/" in r["path"]]
(OUT / "tags").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(OUT / "tags" / "incoming_items.json").write_text(json.dumps([item_tags(r) for r in items], indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"auto-tagged {len(items)} Minecraft item icons")

rest = [r for r in inc if r not in items]
sub = lambda r: "/".join(PurePosixPath(r["path"]).parts[2:4])   # noqa: E731
BATCHES = {
    "sfxlib_a": lambda r: r["kind"] == "audio" and "/SFX (2)/" in r["path"] and sub(r) < "SFX (2)/M",
    "sfxlib_b": lambda r: r["kind"] == "audio" and "/SFX (2)/" in r["path"],
    "sfx_misc": lambda r: r["kind"] == "audio" and re.search(r"/SFX \((1|3)\)/|/My Favorite Ones/|ZenitsuLord", r["path"]),
    "meme_sfx_drive": lambda r: r["kind"] == "audio" and "drive-download" in r["path"] and "/Meme Sound Effects/" in r["path"],
    "meme_sfx_pack_music": lambda r: r["kind"] == "audio",
    "vfx_overlays": lambda r: r["kind"] == "video" and re.search(r"/VFX|/OVERLAYS", r["path"]),
    "videos_memes_bg": lambda r: r["kind"] == "video",
    "images": lambda r: r["kind"] in ("image", "font"),
}
try:
    font = ImageFont.truetype("arial.ttf", 15)
except OSError:
    font = ImageFont.load_default()


def compact(r: dict) -> dict:
    c = {k: r[k] for k in ("id", "path", "title", "kind", "duration_s", "key_mode", "key_color", "has_audio") if k in r}
    if a := r.get("audio_analysis"):
        c["audio"] = {k: a.get(k) for k in ("onset_s", "peak_s", "tail_s", "loud_db", "punch_db")}
    if v := r.get("video"):
        c["res"] = f"{v['width']}x{v['height']}@{v['fps']}"
    if im := r.get("image"):
        c["res"] = f"{im.get('width')}x{im.get('height')}"
        c["alpha"] = im.get("has_alpha")
    return c


def sheets(name: str, recs: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    vis = [r for r in recs if r.get("thumb")]
    out = []
    wide = any(r["kind"] == "video" for r in vis)
    per, cw, ch, cols = (8, 960, 160, 1) if wide else (20, 240, 270, 5)
    for n in range(0, len(vis), per):
        chunk = vis[n:n + per]
        rows = (len(chunk) + cols - 1) // cols
        sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cw * cols, ch * rows), (16, 16, 16))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
        for i, r in enumerate(chunk):
            x, y = (i % cols) * cw, (i // cols) * ch
            with Image.open(OUT / r["thumb"]) as t:
                t = t.copy()
            t.thumbnail((cw, ch - 22))
            sheet.paste(t, (x, y + 22))
            lab = r["id"] + (f"  {r['duration_s']:.1f}s" if r.get("duration_s") else "") + \
                (f"  [{r['key_mode']}]" if r.get("key_mode") not in (None, "none") else "")
            d.text((x + 4, y + 3), lab[: cw // 8], font=font, fill=(255, 220, 80))
        fn = f"incoming_{name}_{n // per:02d}.jpg"
        sheet.save(OUT / "sheets" / fn, quality=82)
        out.append(fn)
    return out


claimed: set[str] = set()
for name, pred in BATCHES.items():
    recs = [r for r in rest if pred(r) and r["id"] not in claimed]
    claimed |= {r["id"] for r in recs}
    if not recs:
        continue
    sh = sheets(name, recs)
    (OUT / "tag_batches" / f"incoming_{name}.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"batch": f"incoming_{name}", "sheets": sh, "assets": [compact(r) for r in recs]},
                   indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"incoming_{name:22s} {len(recs):4d} assets, {len(sh)} sheets")
print("unclaimed:", len([r for r in rest if r["id"] not in claimed]))

input.command:
cd "/c/Users/edmem/OneDrive/Desktop/Minecraft Channel/.claude/skills/mc-edit" && python - <<'PYEOF'
p='SKILL.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old='''## Pipeline
'''
new='''## One click (default path)

```
uv run mcs make <slug> --game rec.mkv [--mic mic.wav] [--facecam cam.mp4] --title "..." --context "what happens"
uv run mcs auto <slug> [--final]          # existing project: transcribe -> analyze -> autoplan -> render -> 3 shorts
```

`autoplan` is a deterministic creative pass (no LLM). Your job in a Claude pass is to **beat it**. Start from its
edit.json (generator: autoplan) or write your own; keep `"generator"` out of hand-made edits so `auto` won't overwrite them.

## Pipeline
'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
old2='''## Rules
'''
new2='''## The toolbox (read references/edl.md for exact fields)

- **Modes** (`studio/modes.json`): per-segment `"mode"` — funny (default), exciting, happy, sad, angry, scary, serious,
  narration (talking avatar), pov ("POV:" header via `header_text`), flashback, broll. Each sets grade, captions,
  text style, music & SFX palette, zoom/shake intensity, avatar face. Switch modes with the story, ~3 s minimum.
- **Looks** (`studio/looks.json`): subtle always-on polish under the mode grade: clean (default), vivid, warm, cool,
  cinematic, shader, none. Per video `"look"`, per segment `"look"`.
- **Shorts**: `mcs shorts <slug>` cuts 9:16 sub-projects from the edit (segment-anchored events travel along, hook
  banner added, captions raised). Hint the picks with `"shorts": [{"from","to","hook"}]` in the main edit.
- **Facecam**: `sources.facecam` + `"facecam": {"layout": "corner"|"stack"}`; `"facecam": false` on a segment hides it
  (do that for jumpscares/full-screen gags).
- **Narration avatar** ("Blocky", `studio/brand/avatar/`): automatic in narration mode, or `"avatar": true` per segment;
  expression follows the mode (`avatar_mood` to override). Creator's own skin: `mcs avatar build --skin <png>`.
- **Motion graphics** (`studio/motion/`, HyperFrames): overlays `{"type":"motion","template":"time_card","vars":{"text":"3 HOURS LATER"}}`,
  cards `{"type":"card","template":"title_card","vars":{...}}`. Templates: title_card, chapter, time_card, lower_third,
  subscribe, counter, hook_banner, end_screen, mode_stinger (cut under it at 0.29 s).
- **Stock / B-roll**: the creator's `Stock Library/` is in the same database (`--category broll stock`). Use B-roll as
  full-frame `video` overlays with `"audio": false` while the voice continues.
- **Engagement**: `mcs engage <slug>` adds attention zooms (punch-ins on stressed words, 1.0x/1.1x jump-cut reframes)
  so something changes every few seconds; auto zooms are marked `"auto": true` and replaced on re-run.

## Cutting the voice (creator feedback: never clip words)
- ASR timestamps end early. Leave >= 0.2 s after the last word of a segment; the renderer's **cut guard** also extends
  outs to the real end of speech (and ins to the onset) using the audio, and logs it in render_report.json.
  Mark a segment `"exact": true` only when you need a hard cut mid-sound on purpose.
- Every cut gets 12 ms audio fades automatically.

## Memes & SFX: use the funny part, not the whole thing (creator guidance)
- A meme cutaway is usually 1.2–3 s: the reaction/punchline, not the full clip. Short clips can play in full. Vary it.
- Long SFX/stingers: trim to the useful part (`"dur"`); the renderer fades any sound cut before its natural end.
- Levels are automatic (voice-relative). Never "fix" loudness with volume_db; only nudge taste ±2–3 dB.

## Rules
'''
assert old2 in s; s=s.replace(old2,new2,1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p='references/edl.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
s=s.replace('''## Top level
''','''## Anchors (pick one per event)
- `"src_at": 312.4`: source seconds (ambiguous if the footage appears twice, e.g. cold opens).
- `"seg": "s012", "src_at": 312.4`: source time **inside that segment**. Preferred. Shorts carry these along.
- `"seg": "s012", "rel": 0.5`: seconds after that segment starts (negative is allowed, e.g. -0.29 for a stinger).
- `"at": 61.2`: output seconds. Avoid it, because it breaks when the cut changes.

## Top level
''')

  "format": "landscape",             // or "vertical" (1080x1920 shorts)
  "mode": "funny",                   // default mode for segments without one (studio/modes.json)
  "look": "clean",                   // base colour polish (studio/looks.json)
  "facecam": {"layout": "corner"},   // needs sources.facecam; vertical defaults to "stack"
  "avatar": {"always": false},       // narration avatar; also on automatically in narration mode
  "watermark": {"text": "@NAME", "opacity": 0.55},
  "guard_cuts": true,                // render-time protection against clipped words
  "shorts": [{"from": "s010", "to": "s014", "hook": "HE TRIED..."}],   // optional hints for mcs shorts''')
s=s.replace('''| `source` | `in`, `out` (source s) | `speed` (0.25–4; atempo keeps pitch), `zoom[]`, `shake[]`, `effects[]`, `freeze_end` (s), `mute_game`, `mute_mic`, `game_db`, `mic_db` |''','''| `source` | `in`, `out` (source s) | `speed` (0.25–4; atempo keeps pitch), `zoom[]`, `shake[]`, `effects[]`, `freeze_end` (s), `mute_game`, `mute_mic`, `game_db`, `mic_db`, `mode`, `look`, `exact`, `facecam` (false hides), `avatar`, `avatar_mood`, `header_text` (pov), `frame_x` (vertical crop pan 0..1) |''')
s=s.replace('''| `card` | `file` (pre-rendered mp4/mov), `dur` | `effects[]` |''','''| `card` | `file` (pre-rendered mp4/mov) + `dur`, **or** `template` + `vars` (channel motion graphic, rendered opaque) | `effects[]` |''')
s=s.replace('''| `motion` | Your own HyperFrames render (`file: overlays/x.mov`). |''','''| `motion` | `template` + `vars` from the channel motion library (rendered and cached automatically), or `file` for your own HyperFrames .mov. |''')

Asset ids are content-stable (`catalog/identity.json`), so files can move without breaking tags or edits. - `Stock Library/`: the creator's own footage (B-roll, stock, memes, music). Index it with `uv run mcs library scan`, then tag.''')
s=s.replace('''- `.claude/skills/mc-edit/`: the editing skill. **Use it for any editing request.**''','''- `studio/modes.json` (mood modes), `studio/looks.json` (colour presets), `studio/brand/` (channel identity + narrator avatar), `studio/motion/` (HyperFrames motion-graphics templates).
- `.claude/skills/mc-edit/`: the editing skill. **Use it for any editing request.**''')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s); print("CLAUDE.md updated")

    ("## Pipeline\n", """## One click (default path)

```
uv run mcs make <slug> --game rec.mkv [--mic mic.wav] [--facecam cam.mp4] --title "..." --context "what happens"
uv run mcs auto <slug> [--final]          # existing project: transcribe -> analyze -> autoplan -> render -> 3 shorts
```

`autoplan` is a deterministic creative pass with no LLM involved. In a Claude pass, your job is to **beat it**. You can
start from its edit.json (which has `"generator": "autoplan"`) or write your own. Leave `"generator"` out of hand-made
edits so that `auto` will not overwrite them.

## Pipeline
"""),
    ("## Rules\n", """## The toolbox (exact fields are in references/edl.md)

- **Modes** (`studio/modes.json`): set `"mode"` per segment. Each mode sets the grade, captions, text style, music
  and SFX palette, zoom/shake intensity and the avatar's face. Switch modes with the story, holding each for about 3 s
  at minimum.
  - Available modes: funny (default), exciting, happy, sad, angry, scary, serious, narration (talking avatar),
    pov ("POV:" header via `header_text`), flashback, broll.
- **Looks** (`studio/looks.json`): subtle always-on polish applied under the mode grade. Set `"look"` per video or per
  segment.
  - Available looks: clean (default), vivid, warm, cool, cinematic, shader, none.
- **Shorts**: `mcs shorts <slug>` cuts 9:16 sub-projects from the edit.
  - Segment-anchored events travel along, a hook banner is added, and captions are raised.
  - Steer the picks with `"shorts": [{"from", "to", "hook"}]` in the main edit.
- **Facecam**: add `sources.facecam` plus `"facecam": {"layout": "corner"|"stack"}`.
  - Set `"facecam": false` on a segment to hide it there. Do that for jumpscares and full-screen gags.
- **Narration avatar** ("Blocky", in `studio/brand/avatar/`): appears automatically in narration mode, or set
  `"avatar": true` per segment.
  - The expression follows the mode; override it with `avatar_mood`.
  - To use the creator's own skin: `mcs avatar build --skin <png>`.
- **Motion graphics** (`studio/motion/`, built with HyperFrames):
  - Overlay: `{"type":"motion","template":"time_card","vars":{"text":"3 HOURS LATER"}}`
  - Card: `{"type":"card","template":"title_card","vars":{...}}`
  - Templates: title_card, chapter, time_card, lower_third, subscribe, counter, hook_banner, end_screen, mode_stinger.
  - For mode_stinger, cut the footage underneath at 0.29 s.
- **Stock and B-roll**: the creator's `Stock Library/` is in the same database (`--category broll stock`).
  - Use B-roll as full-frame `video` overlays with `"audio": false` while the voice continues.
- **Engagement**: `mcs engage <slug>` adds attention zooms (punch-ins on stressed words, 1.0x/1.1x reframes across
  jump cuts) so something changes every few seconds.
  - Auto zooms are marked `"auto": true` and are replaced on each re-run.

## Cutting the voice (creator feedback: never clip words)
- ASR word end times are early. Leave at least 0.2 s after the last word of a segment.
- The renderer's **cut guard** also uses the audio to extend each out-point to the real end of speech, and each
  in-point back to the onset. It logs every change in render_report.json.
- Mark a segment `"exact": true` only when you deliberately need a hard cut in the middle of a sound.
- Every cut gets 12 ms audio fades automatically.

## Memes and SFX: use the funny part, not the whole thing (creator guidance)
- A meme cutaway is usually 1.2–3 s: just the reaction or punchline, not the full clip. Short clips can play in full.
  Vary it.
- Trim long SFX and stingers to the useful part with `"dur"`. The renderer fades any sound that is cut before its
  natural end.
- Levels are set automatically, relative to the voice. Never use volume_db to fix loudness; use it only to nudge taste
  by ±2–3 dB.

## Rules
"""),
])

1	# Minecraft Channel: automated editing studio
2	
3	This folder contains:
4	- `Editing Pack/`: the unified asset pack. It combines the original pack with the v2 archives, deduplicated and organised into `Sound Effects/`, `Music/`, `Meme Videos/`, `Green Screen/`, `Overlays & VFX/`, `Transitions/`, `Animations/`, `Backgrounds/`, `Images/`, `Fonts/` and a few more (the full tree is in `catalog/taxonomy.json` → `folders`).
5	  - Asset ids are content-stable (`catalog/identity.json`), so files can move without breaking tags or edits.
6	  - Ids of merged-away duplicates are mapped in `catalog/redirects.json`.
7	  - Every move is logged in `catalog/moves.jsonl`; undo with `python studio/catalog/organize.py undo`.
8	  - Quarantined duplicates sit in `_Duplicates (review, then delete)/`.
9	- `Stock Library/`: the creator's own footage (B-roll, stock, memes, music). Index it with `uv run mcs library scan`, then tag it.
10	- `studio/`: the editing assembly line (Python package `mcstudio`, CLI `mcs`, uv project pinned to Python 3.12).
11	  - `catalog/`: the asset database pipeline. `build_catalog.py` (technical scan) → `tags/*.json` (LLM semantic tags, see `TAGGING.md`) → `merge_catalog.py` → `assets.db`. The vocabulary lives in `taxonomy.json`. Hand corrections go in `overrides.json` (`{"<asset id>": {field: value}}`), and they win over the tags.
12	  - `projects/<slug>/`: one folder per episode. `project.json` (sources), `edit.json` (the EDL), `work/` (transcript, signals, renders cache), `out/` (videos).
13	  - `style.json`: channel look (caption font and colours, text styles, audio levels, pacing targets, encoders).
14	  - `docs/TOOLS.md`: tool research and roadmap.
15	  - `ui/` + `mcstudio/server.py`: the local web UI (`uv run mcs ui`).
16	- `studio/modes.json` (mood modes), `studio/looks.json` (colour presets), `studio/brand/` (channel identity and narrator avatar), `studio/motion/` (HyperFrames motion-graphics templates).
17	- `.claude/skills/mc-edit/`: the editing skill. **Use it for any editing request.**
18	
19	Conventions:
20	- Run commands from `studio/` with `uv run mcs ...`. ffmpeg 9 is on PATH.
21	- No NVIDIA GPU: keep heavy ML on CPU (int8) or hosted APIs.
22	- Never auto-use assets rated `banned`. The finder and `mcs check` enforce this.
23	- Image/GIF overlays must go through the `movie=` source filter (looped image inputs deadlock ffmpeg 9's scheduler). render.py already does this.

input.command:
cd "/c/Users/edmem/OneDrive/Desktop/Minecraft Channel/studio" && uv run python - <<'PYEOF'
import json, subprocess
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from mcstudio.edl import build_spans, resolve_time, load
from mcstudio import assets as A
e=load("projects/auto-dig/edit.json"); sp=build_spans(e, lambda i:A.get(i))
times=[]
for o in e["overlays"]:
    t=resolve_time(o, sp, [], "o")
    name=o.get("template") or o.get("asset","")[:20]
    off={"title_card":1.3,"time_card":0.9,"subscribe":1.8,"mode_stinger":0.28}.get(name,0.8)
    times.append((name, t+off))
tiles=[]
for name,t in times:
    r=subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-ss",f"{t:.2f}","-i","projects/auto-dig/out/auto-dig_preview.mp4","-frames:v","1","-vf","scale=480:270","-f","rawvideo","-pix_fmt","rgb24","-"],capture_output=True)
    im=Image.frombytes("RGB",(480,270),r.stdout[:480*270*3]); d=ImageDraw.Draw(im); d.rectangle([0,0,200,16],fill=(0,0,0)); d.text((4,2),f"{t:.1f}s {name}",fill=(255,230,0)); tiles.append(im)
s=Image.new("RGB",(960,270*3))
for i,t in enumerate(tiles): s.paste(t,((i%2)*480,(i//2)*270))
s.save("projects/auto-dig/out/motion_check.jpg",quality=85)
print(times)
PYEOF

file.content:
def hook_text(edl: dict, segs: list[dict], pj: dict, n: int) -> str:
    """A hook must promise the payoff. First short: the episode title; others: a strong on-screen line
    from inside the window, else a tease matched to how the window ends."""
    title = (pj.get("title") or "").upper()
    if n == 1 and title:
        return title[:34] + ("..." if not title.endswith(("!", "?", "...")) else "")
    ids = {s["id"] for s in segs}
    texts = [t["text"] for t in edl.get("text", []) if t.get("seg") in ids and len(t["text"]) <= 22
             and t.get("style") != "label" and not BORING.search(t["text"])]
    if texts:
        return texts[0]
    end_mode = segs[-1].get("mode") or edl.get("mode", "funny")
    return TEASES.get(end_mode, TEASES["funny"])


def make_short(slug: str, n: int, win: dict, edl: dict, pj: dict) -> str:
    main_segs = [s for s in edl["segments"] if not s["id"].startswith("cold")]
    segs = [dict(s) for s in main_segs[win["from"]: win["to"] + 1]]
    ids = {s["id"] for s in segs}
    keep = lambda e: e.get("seg") in ids or ("src_at" in e and "seg" not in e and "at" not in e)  # noqa: E731
    skip_text = {"label"}                                # intro titles / speed labels stay in the long video
    texts = [dict(t) for t in edl.get("text", []) if keep(t)
             and not (t.get("style") in skip_text and "SPEED" not in t["text"])
             and not re.search(r"EARLIER|LATER", t["text"], re.I)]      # cold-open segues mean nothing in a short
    hook = win.get("hook") or hook_text(edl, segs, pj, n)
    hook_overlay = {"type": "motion", "template": "hook_banner", "vars": {"text": hook}, "seg": segs[0]["id"],
                    "rel": 0.0, "dur": 3.2}
    overlays = [dict(o) for o in edl.get("overlays", []) if keep(o) and o.get("type") != "transition"
                and o.get("template") not in ("title_card", "subscribe", "time_card", "end_screen")]
    overlays.insert(0, hook_overlay)
    for o in overlays:                                    # corner overlays read better centred on a phone
        if o.get("x") is not None and o.get("placement") != "fullscreen":
            o["x"], o["scale"] = 0.5, min(0.32, o.get("scale", 0.45))
    sfx = [dict(e) for e in edl.get("audio", {}).get("sfx", []) if keep(e)
           and not (e.get("rel") is not None and e.get("rel") <= 0 and "rewind" in e.get("asset", ""))]

    # music: whatever bed was playing where the short starts, re-timed into the short
    spans_main = build_spans(edl, lambda i: A.get(i))

Add a **favourites** feature to the Minecraft editing studio. Working dir: C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel (Windows; Python via `cd studio && uv run ...`). Read CLAUDE.md first. The creator wants to star assets, especially memes and green screens, so the auto-editor prefers them.

Requirements:
1. Storage: `studio/catalog/favorites.json` with the shape `{"ids": [...]}`. It must survive catalog rebuilds. Asset ids are content-stable (see catalog/identity.json), and `studio/catalog/redirects.json` maps old ids to new ones, so honour redirects.
2. DB: `studio/catalog/merge_catalog.py` adds an `favorite INT` column to the `assets` table, filled from favorites.json, and includes it in assets.jsonl. Keep the existing schema otherwise. The `usage` table must keep being preserved across rebuilds, as it is now.
3. Finder (`studio/mcstudio/assets.py`):
   - `Query.favorites_only: bool = False`.
   - Favourites get a scoring bonus (+1.2) so the planner prefers them.
   - Add `set_favorite(id, on: bool)`, which updates favorites.json AND the DB row directly, with no full rebuild.
   - Add `favorites()` listing.
   - `as_dict` must include `favorite`.
4. CLI (`studio/mcstudio/cli.py`, the `assets` subcommand):
   - New actions `fav <ids...>`, `unfav <ids...>` and `favs` (list).
   - A `--favorites` flag on `find`.
   - Keep all existing behaviour.
5. Server (`studio/mcstudio/server.py`):
   - `POST /api/assets/{id}/favorite` with body `{"on": true|false}` returns the updated asset.
   - The `/api/assets` list gets a `favorites: bool = False` filter.
   - Asset dicts carry `favorite`.
6. UI (`studio/ui/app.js` + `style.css`):
   - A star toggle on every asset card in the grid, top-right of the thumbnail. It must not open the drawer when clicked.
   - A "★ Favourite" toggle button in the asset drawer.
   - A "★ Favourites" filter chip in the library filter bar, persisted in the existing LIB localStorage state.
   - Favourited cards get a gold star and a subtle gold border.
   - Match the existing code style; the UI is vanilla JS with no build step.
7. Autoplan (`studio/mcstudio/autoplan.py`): no changes are needed if the finder bonus works. Just confirm the meme cutaway and green screen picks go through `assets.find` and so get the bonus.

Verify:
- Run `python studio/catalog/merge_catalog.py` and confirm the column exists.
- `uv run mcs assets fav <some meme_video id> <some green_screen id>`, then `uv run mcs assets find --moment shock --category meme_video --favorites`.
- Start the server on a spare port (`uv run python -c "from mcstudio.server import serve; serve(port=8799, open_browser=False)"` in the background) and exercise the endpoints with curl or Python, including the toggle on and off, then stop it.
- Syntax-check app.js with node.
- Don't touch the server on port 8765 (the user's UI); just tell me it needs a restart.

Another process may run `merge_catalog.py` concurrently (an asset import is in progress). Keep your merge changes backward compatible and atomic.

input.content:
"""Deep analysis: what is SAID in every clip, and a richer look at every video.

    uv run python catalog/deep_analyze.py [--workers 4] [--model small]

For every asset that can contain speech (meme sounds, laughs, MLG, meme videos, green screens, new incoming):
  speech transcript with word timings + detected language (multilingual faster-whisper, CPU int8)
For every video: an 8-frame strip (thumbs8/<hash>.jpg) so taggers see the whole clip, not 4 moments.
Results: catalog/analysis.json keyed by content hash (incremental; re-runs only do new files).
The transcripts give taggers real quotes, exact punchline windows, and catch swearing/slurs the file
names don't reveal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import wave
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

CAT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = CAT.parents[1]
SPEECH_CATS = {"sfx_meme", "sfx_laugh", "sfx_mlg", "meme_video", "green_screen"}
_model = None


def _init(model_name: str, threads: int):
    global _model
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    _model = WhisperModel(model_name, device="cpu", compute_type="int8", cpu_threads=threads)


def transcribe(job: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    h, path = job
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-t", "30", "-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000",
                            "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True)
        pcm = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
        if pcm.size < 1600 or np.abs(pcm).max() < 0.01:
            return h, {"speech": "", "lang": None, "words": [], "no_audio": True}
        segs, info = _model.transcribe(pcm, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True, beam_size=3,
                                       condition_on_previous_text=False)
        words, texts, nsp = [], [], []
        for s in segs:
            nsp.append(s.no_speech_prob)
            if s.no_speech_prob > 0.6 and s.avg_logprob < -1.0:
                continue                                  # music/noise hallucination
            texts.append(s.text.strip())
            words += [[w.word.strip(), round(w.start, 2), round(w.end, 2)] for w in (s.words or [])]
        speech = " ".join(t for t in texts if t)
        if speech.lower().strip(" .!") in ("thank you", "thanks for watching", "you", "bye", ""):
            speech, words = "", []                         # classic whisper hallucinations on non-speech
        return h, {"speech": speech, "lang": info.language if speech else None,
                   "lang_p": round(info.language_probability, 2), "words": words[:120]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return h, {"error": str(e)}


def strip8(job: tuple[str, str, float]) -> str | None:
    h, path, dur = job
    out = CAT / "thumbs8" / f"{h}.jpg"
    if out.exists():
        return h
    tiles = []
    for k in range(8):
        t = dur * (0.04 + 0.92 * k / 7)
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{t:.2f}", "-i", path, "-frames:v", "1",
                            "-vf", "scale=240:135", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-"], capture_output=True)
        if len(r.stdout) >= 240 * 135 * 3:
            tiles.append(Image.frombytes("RGB", (240, 135), r.stdout[:240 * 135 * 3]))
    if not tiles:
        return None
    im = Image.new("RGB", (240 * 4, 135 * 2), (10, 10, 10))
    for k, t in enumerate(tiles):
        im.paste(t, ((k % 4) * 240, (k // 4) * 135))
    im.save(out, quality=78)
    return h


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="small")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ap_path = CAT / "analysis.json"
    done = json.loads(ap_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if ap_path.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in scan if not r.get("duplicate_of") and not r["path"].startswith("_Duplicates")]
    absp = lambda r: str(ROOT / r.get("root", "Editing Pack") / r["path"])  # noqa: E731
    speech_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r)) for r in live if r.get("has_audio") and r["hash"] not in done
                   and (r["category"] in SPEECH_CATS or r["path"].startswith("_Incoming/"))
                   and (r.get("duration_s") or 0) <= 120]
    video_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r), r.get("duration_s") or 1.0) for r in live if r["kind"] == "video"]
    (CAT / "thumbs8").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    print(f"speech: {len(speech_jobs)} clips to transcribe; video strips: {len(video_jobs)}", flush=True)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as tp:
        strips = tp.map(strip8, video_jobs)
        threads = max(1, 12 // args.workers)
        with ProcessPoolExecutor(args.workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(args.model, threads)) as pp:
            for k, (h, res) in enumerate(pp.map(transcribe, speech_jobs, chunksize=4), 1):
                done[h] = res
                if k % 100 == 0:
                    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
                    print(f"  transcribed {k}/{len(speech_jobs)}", flush=True)
        n_strips = sum(1 for s in strips if s)
    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    talk = sum(1 for v in done.values() if v.get("speech"))
    langs: dict[str, int] = {}
    for v in done.values():
        if v.get("lang"):
            langs[v["lang"]] = langs.get(v["lang"], 0) + 1
    print(f"done: {len(done)} analysed, {talk} contain speech, {n_strips} video strips; languages {langs}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

            words += [[w.word.strip(), round(w.start, 2), round(w.end, 2)] for w in (s.words or [])]
        speech = " ".join(t for t in texts if t)
        if speech.lower().strip(" .!") in ("thank you", "thanks for watching", "you", "bye", ""):
            speech, words = "", []                         # classic whisper hallucinations on non-speech
        return h, {"speech": speech, "lang": info.language if speech else None,
                   "lang_p": round(info.language_probability, 2), "words": words[:120]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return h, {"error": str(e)}


def strip8(job: tuple[str, str, float]) -> str | None:
    h, path, dur = job
    out = CAT / "thumbs8" / f"{h}.jpg"
    if out.exists():
        return h
    tiles = []
    for k in range(8):
        t = dur * (0.04 + 0.92 * k / 7)
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{t:.2f}", "-i", path, "-frames:v", "1",
                            "-vf", "scale=240:135", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-"], capture_output=True)
        if len(r.stdout) >= 240 * 135 * 3:
            tiles.append(Image.frombytes("RGB", (240, 135), r.stdout[:240 * 135 * 3]))
    if not tiles:
        return None
    im = Image.new("RGB", (240 * 4, 135 * 2), (10, 10, 10))
    for k, t in enumerate(tiles):
        im.paste(t, ((k % 4) * 240, (k // 4) * 135))
    im.save(out, quality=78)
    return h


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="small")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ap_path = CAT / "analysis.json"
    done = json.loads(ap_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if ap_path.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in scan if not r.get("duplicate_of") and not r["path"].startswith("_Duplicates")]
    absp = lambda r: str(ROOT / r.get("root", "Editing Pack") / r["path"])  # noqa: E731
    speech_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r)) for r in live if r.get("has_audio") and r["hash"] not in done
                   and (r["category"] in SPEECH_CATS or r["path"].startswith("_Incoming/"))
                   and (r.get("duration_s") or 0) <= 120]
    video_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r), r.get("duration_s") or 1.0) for r in live if r["kind"] == "video"]
    (CAT / "thumbs8").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    print(f"speech: {len(speech_jobs)} clips to transcribe; video strips: {len(video_jobs)}", flush=True)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as tp:
        strips = tp.map(strip8, video_jobs)
        threads = max(1, 12 // args.workers)
        with ProcessPoolExecutor(args.workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(args.model, threads)) as pp:
            for k, (h, res) in enumerate(pp.map(transcribe, speech_jobs, chunksize=4), 1):
                done[h] = res
                if k % 100 == 0:
                    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
                    print(f"  transcribed {k}/{len(speech_jobs)}", flush=True)
        n_strips = sum(1 for s in strips if s)
    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    talk = sum(1 for v in done.values() if v.get("speech"))
    langs: dict[str, int] = {}
    for v in done.values():
        if v.get("lang"):
            langs[v["lang"]] = langs.get(v["lang"], 0) + 1
    print(f"done: {len(done)} analysed, {talk} contain speech, {n_strips} video strips; languages {langs}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Full re-review of the library with real evidence (not just file names).

    uv run python catalog/make_review_batches.py [--size 420]

Each asset in a batch carries:
  prev        its current tags (refine, don't throw away)
  speech      what is said (deep_analyze.py transcript) + language + word timings  -> real quotes, punchline window
  sound       measured audio descriptors: brightness, noisiness, attack/decay, tempo & energy curve for music
  sheet       8-frame strip of every video (sheets/review_<batch>_NN.jpg)
Batches: review_speech_* (anything with speech + all memes/green screens), review_video_* (other videos),
review_sfx_* (non-speech sounds), review_music_*. Reviewers write tags/zz_review_<batch>.json (sorted last =
overrides older tags).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

CAT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = CAT.parents[1]


def descriptors(path: str, music: bool) -> dict:
    sr = 8000
    args = ["-ss", "20"] if music else []
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", *args, "-i", path, "-t", "40" if music else "8", "-vn", "-ac", "1",
                        "-ar", str(sr), "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True)
    x = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
    if x.size < 400:
        return {}
    n = 256
    frames = x[: (x.size // n) * n].reshape(-1, n) * np.hanning(n)
    spec = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(frames, axis=1)) + 1e-9
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, 1 / sr)
    energy = spec.sum(axis=1)
    w = energy / energy.sum()
    centroid = float((spec @ freqs / spec.sum(axis=1) * w).sum())
    flat = float((np.exp(np.log(spec).mean(axis=1)) / spec.mean(axis=1) * w).sum())
    env = np.sqrt((frames ** 2).mean(axis=1))
    pk = int(env.argmax())
    thr = env[pk] * 0.1
    on = int(np.argmax(env > thr))
    after = np.where(env[pk:] < thr)[0]
    fr = n / sr
    d = {"brightness": "bright" if centroid > 1800 else "mid" if centroid > 900 else "dark",
         "centroid_hz": int(centroid), "noisiness": round(flat, 2),
         "texture": "noisy" if flat > 0.35 else "mixed" if flat > 0.15 else "tonal",
         "attack_s": round((pk - on) * fr, 3), "decay_s": round((after[0] if after.size else len(env) - pk) * fr, 3)}
    if music:
        onset = np.maximum(0, np.diff(env))
        onset -= onset.mean()
        ac = np.correlate(onset, onset, "full")[len(onset) - 1:]
        lags = np.arange(len(ac)) * fr
        band = (lags > 60 / 180) & (lags < 60 / 70)
        if band.any():
            d["tempo_bpm"] = int(round(60 / lags[band][ac[band].argmax()]))
        q = np.array_split(env, 4)
        d["energy_curve"] = [round(float(20 * np.log10(c.mean() + 1e-9)), 1) for c in q]
        d["dynamics_db"] = round(float(20 * np.log10(np.percentile(env, 90) + 1e-9) -
                                       20 * np.log10(np.percentile(env, 20) + 1e-9)), 1)
    return d


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=420)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

"""Rebuild redirects.json: every asset quarantined as a duplicate -> the id of the copy that was kept.

    python studio/catalog/rebuild_redirects.py

Follows moves.jsonl to find where each kept copy lives *now*, then maps ids via scan.json. Run after any
dedupe/organize step (organize.py and the pack importer call it).
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

CAT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = CAT.parents[1]
scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
by_abs = {str(ROOT / r.get("root", "Editing Pack") / r["path"]).lower(): r for r in scan}
moves = [json.loads(line) for line in (CAT / "moves.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
nxt = {m["from"].lower(): m["to"] for m in moves}


def final(p: str) -> str:
    seen = set()
    while p.lower() in nxt and p.lower() not in seen:
        seen.add(p.lower())
        p = nxt[p.lower()]
    return p


red = json.loads((CAT / "redirects.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if (CAT / "redirects.json").exists() else {}
added = 0
for m in moves:
    if not m["why"].startswith("duplicate of "):
        continue
    dup = by_abs.get(final(m["to"]).lower())
    keep = by_abs.get(final(m["why"][len("duplicate of "):]).lower())
    if dup and keep and dup["id"] != keep["id"] and red.get(dup["id"]) != keep["id"]:
        red[dup["id"]] = keep["id"]
        added += 1
live = {r["id"] for r in scan if not r["path"].startswith("_Duplicates")}
red = {k: v for k, v in red.items() if k != v}
(CAT / "redirects.json").write_text(json.dumps(red, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
broken = [k for k, v in red.items() if v not in live]
print(f"{len(red)} redirects ({added} new); {len(broken)} point at missing ids")

new='''def _init(model_name: str, threads: int):
    """Parakeet (onnx, ~9x realtime on this CPU) for words + whisper-tiny for language id only."""
    global _model, _lid
    import os
    os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", str(threads))
    import onnx_asr
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    _model = onnx_asr.load_model("nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3", quantization="int8").with_timestamps()
    _lid = WhisperModel("tiny", device="cpu", compute_type="int8", cpu_threads=threads)


def _words(res) -> list:
    """Parakeet tokens (sentencepiece, '▁'/space = word start) -> [[word, start, end], ...]."""
    out = []
    toks, ts = list(res.tokens or []), list(res.timestamps or [])
    for i, (tok, t) in enumerate(zip(toks, ts)):
        end = ts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(ts) else t + 0.25
        if tok.startswith((" ", "\\u2581")) or not out:
            out.append([tok.strip(" \\u2581"), round(t, 2), round(end, 2)])
        else:
            out[-1][0] += tok
            out[-1][2] = round(end, 2)
    return [w for w in out if w[0]]


def transcribe(job: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    h, path = job
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-t", "30", "-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000",
                            "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True)
        pcm = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
        if pcm.size < 1600 or np.abs(pcm).max() < 0.01:
            return h, {"speech": "", "lang": None, "words": [], "no_audio": True}
        res = _model.recognize(pcm, sample_rate=16000)
        speech = (res.text or "").strip()
        words = _words(res)[:120]
        lang, lp = None, 0.0
        if speech:
            lang, lp, _ = _lid.detect_language(pcm[: 16000 * 15])
        return h, {"speech": speech, "lang": lang, "lang_p": round(float(lp), 2), "words": words,
                   "engine": "parakeet-v3+whisper-tiny-lid"}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return h, {"error": str(e)}

"""Catalog coverage report: how well is each category described for the editor?

    uv run python catalog/coverage.py
"""
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

db = sqlite3.connect(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "assets.db")
q = """SELECT category, COUNT(*), SUM(tagged), SUM(quote IS NOT NULL AND quote != ''), SUM(use_in IS NOT NULL),
       SUM(speech IS NOT NULL), SUM(content_rating IN ('clean','mild')), SUM(content_rating='banned'),
       SUM(moments != '[]')
       FROM assets WHERE substr(path,1,1) != '_' GROUP BY category ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC"""
print(f"{'category':14s} {'total':>6s} {'tagged':>6s} {'moments':>7s} {'quote':>6s} {'window':>6s} {'speech':>6s} {'usable':>6s} {'banned':>6s}")
for row in db.execute(q):
    c, n, t, qt, w, sp, ok, ban, mo = row
    print(f"{c:14s} {n:6d} {t:6d} {mo:7d} {qt:6d} {w:6d} {sp:6d} {ok:6d} {ban:6d}")
left = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assets WHERE path LIKE '_Incoming/%'").fetchone()[0]
removed = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assets WHERE path LIKE '_Removed%'").fetchone()[0]
untagged = db.execute("SELECT path FROM assets WHERE tagged=0 AND substr(path,1,1) != '_' LIMIT 8").fetchall()
print(f"\nstill in _Incoming: {left}   removed (quarantined): {removed}")
print("untagged examples:", [u[0] for u in untagged])

content.text:
The untagged meme videos you saw were the new v3 clips. Their tags were written but hadn't been loaded into the database yet. They're loaded now: every meme video and green screen is tagged. Refresh the library to see it.

**How the editor knows when to use a meme.** Each clip's tags answer "when does this fit?":
- **Moments:** the situations it's for, such as fail, shock, confusion, victory or irony.
- **Quote:** what's actually said, taken from the audio transcript. You can search by quote, so "I can do this all day" finds the Captain America clip.
- **Funny window:** the exact second range of the punchline, so only that part plays.
- **Rating:** whether it's safe to use, so banned or explicit clips never get picked automatically.

When the auto-editor detects a beat in your video ("oh no" is a fail, "oh my god" is shock), it searches for clips tagged with that moment. For example, a fail gets the Naked Gun facepalm and a shock gets iShowSpeed or Eddy Wally's "wow". Your ★ favorites get a boost, and clips already used recently get a penalty so it doesn't repeat itself.

**State of the library now:**
- **Coverage:** every usable asset is tagged. 6,203 of 6,263; the other 60 are readmes, presets and download links. 363 meme videos (192 with real quotes, 218 with a funny window) and 311 green screens are fully described.
- **Asset Pack v3:** all 271 clips are tagged and filed into their proper folders.
- **Indian memes:** 97 moved to `_Removed (review, then delete)`, nothing deleted. I hit and fixed a bug on the way: the first removal got undone because the next reorganizing pass pulled the files back into the pack. That can't happen any more.
- **Copyright:** copyrighted clips are allowed for quick cuts. The checker only flags long uses, such as copyrighted music as a background track.
- **Favorites:** the ★ on cards and in the asset panel works, and the editor prefers starred clips.

**Treat as a strong first pass, not checked by ear:**
- The reviewers couldn't hear the audio. They worked from transcripts, file names and measured sound properties.
- Transcripts of Hindi clips were mostly gibberish, so those clips were judged from their titles and rated strictly.
- Some funny windows on clips without speech were estimated from the frames.
- If any tag looks wrong in the library, open the asset and use "Correct tags"; corrections are kept permanently.

        # ---- cold open: tease the strongest late beat

        if self.cold_open and cands and duration > 40:
            # tease with the creator's own line when there is one ("I'm actually gonna die"), then the death screen
            top = max(cands, key=lambda b: (b["score"], bool(b["phrase"]) and not b.get("death_screen"), b["t"]))

from mcstudio.edl import build_spans, resolve_time
c=Ctx("auto-dig", True); sp=build_spans(c.edl, c.asset_lookup)
print(f"voice_ref (processed voice, p90): {c.voice_ref:.1f} dBFS")
rows=[]
for ev in c.edl["audio"]["sfx"][:40]:
    a=c.asset(ev["asset"]); at=resolve_time(ev,sp,[],"s")
    if at is None: continue
    pl,si,du=sfx_timing(c,ev,at)
    g=c.matched_db(a,c.sfx_rel(a),0)+ev.get("volume_db",0)
    path=c.media_path(ev)
    raw=subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-ss",f"{si:.3f}"]+(["-t",f"{du:.3f}"] if du else [])+["-i",str(path),"-ac","1","-ar","8000","-f","s16le","-"],capture_output=True).stdout
    x=np.frombuffer(raw,np.int16)/32768*10**(g/20)
    n=len(x)//800
    if n<1: continue
    lvl=np.percentile(20*np.log10(np.sqrt((x[:n*800].reshape(n,800)**2).mean(1))+1e-9),90)
    rows.append((round(lvl-c.voice_ref,1), round(c.sfx_rel(a),1), a["roles"][:2], a.get("loud_db"), ev["asset"][:40]))
rows.sort(reverse=True)
for r in rows[:10]: print(r)
print("median placed vs voice:", np.median([r[0] for r in rows]))

content.text:
Here's the re-edit and its 3 shorts. All three problems were real faults in the auto-editor, not demos, and I changed its rules so every future video gets the fixes, not just this one.

**Filters changing every few seconds.** The editor was switching mood (exciting, happy, sad) on almost every beat, about 20 look changes in 1:45. The cave-brightening filter was also toggling on and off between neighboring cuts.
- The look now stays steady.
- A mood change only happens for a real story section of 8+ seconds of scary, or a sad ending. In this video that's just the death at the end.
- Brightening applies to a whole dark stretch, so it only changes where the footage actually goes from outdoors into caves.

**Effects in the wrong places:**
- **"K.O." on "let's go get a pickaxe":** the editor read "let's go" as a victory. Now only a shouted "let's go!" or "let's gooo" counts. Green screens are also only used when their main purpose matches the moment. None qualified in this video, so it has none, which is better than a wrong one.
- **Subscribe button during the drowning panic:** it now only goes in a calm stretch in the middle of the video. Here it's at 0:39.
- **Color-flash stingers:** removed from automatic edits.

**Overuse:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Sound effects | 36 | 28 |
| Zooms | 44 | 28 |

- The same "pop" sound played 8 times; now it's 4 times, and favorite sounds max out at twice per video.
- Zooms are now mostly on strong moments, not filler.

**Sound effect volume.** Every effect is 3 dB quieter than last time, and screams and other high-energy sounds get an extra 2 dB cut. I measured them: hits sit about 9 dB under your voice and meme voice lines about 6 dB under. Your recordings put voice and game on one track, so game noise between your words still adds some loudness that effects can't control. A separate mic track in OBS would fix that.

If effects still feel off in either direction, tell me "quieter" or "louder" and I'll adjust that one setting for every video. I've also saved your feedback so future edits follow it.

3. `location_tag` — location / dimension banner ("THE NETHER", "STRONGHOLD", "DAY 12") with icon square and coordinates line (vars: text, sub, color), ~3s.

5. `progress_tracker` — challenge goal tracker "DIAMONDS 3/10" with a segmented bar that fills by one step (vars: label, from, to, total, icon optional), ~2.5s.
6. `question_card` — "WOULD YOU RATHER" / poll / question card with two options popping in (vars: title, a, b), ~3.5s.

input.description: Build Motion Graphics UI page
input.prompt:
Build a **Motion Graphics library page** in the studio web UI. Working dir: C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel (Windows; Python via `cd studio && uv run ...`). Read CLAUDE.md, studio/motion/README.md, studio/mcstudio/motion.py (template manifests in studio/motion/templates/<name>/template.json, `list_templates()`, `render(name, vars, orientation, preview, opaque, duration)` -> cached .mov with alpha), studio/mcstudio/server.py (FastAPI; there is already a basic `/api/motion` and `/media/studio/{rel}` route that serves files under studio/motion/ and studio/brand/), and studio/ui/app.js + style.css (vanilla JS SPA, hash routes, no build step). Other agents are concurrently ADDING new template folders under studio/motion/templates/ — your code must discover templates dynamically, never hard-code the list.

Deliver:
1. **Previews** — `studio/mcstudio/motion_previews.py` with `make(name, force=False)`: render the template in preview mode (landscape, default vars) via motion.render, composite it over a Minecraft gameplay still (extract a frame once from a source video referenced in studio/projects/test-clip-02/project.json or any project's game file; fall back to a dark checkerboard) into `studio/motion/previews/<name>.mp4` (h264, browser-playable, ~540p, loop-friendly) and `<name>.jpg` poster (mid-frame). Cache by the rendered .mov's name so it only re-renders when the template changes. CLI: `uv run python -m mcstudio.motion_previews [names...]` (all if none), printing progress. Run it for all current templates.
2. **API** in server.py:
   - GET `/api/motion` returns every template: name, description, kind, duration, orientations, vars (from template.json, with defaults resolved incl. brand), preview_mp4 + poster URLs if present.
   - POST `/api/motion/render` {name, vars, orientation, preview} starts a background Job (reuse the existing Job class/JOBS dict pattern) that calls motion.render and records the output path. The job result must expose the output file URL — also make a browser-playable mp4 copy over checkerboard/gameplay for viewing (ProRes .mov doesn't play in browsers) while keeping the .mov path for the editor.
   - Serve outputs via /media/studio/motion/... (already allowed).
3. **UI** — new nav item "Motion graphics" (#/motion) in index.html + app.js:
   - grid of template cards with poster images that play the preview mp4 on hover (muted loop), name, description, duration, orientation badges;
   - clicking opens the drawer: big preview, a form auto-generated from the template's vars (text inputs, number inputs, color pickers for type "color", checkboxes for booleans, select for enum-like options if defined), orientation toggle (landscape/vertical), "Render" button -> shows job progress -> plays the result, offers "Download .mov (alpha)" link and a "Copy EDL snippet" button that copies e.g. `{"type": "motion", "template": "time_card", "vars": {...}, "seg": "<segment id>", "rel": 0.0}`;
   - a "Regenerate previews" button that runs the preview job for templates missing previews.
   - Match existing UI style/patterns (see Library page and drawer); remember `[hidden]{display:none!important}` is already in style.css.
4. Update the Brand page's motion section to link to the new page (keep it simple).

Verify: run previews for all templates; start the server on a spare port (e.g. `uv run python -c "from mcstudio.server import serve; serve(port=8798, open_browser=False)"` in background), exercise /api/motion and a render job end-to-end with curl/python, syntax-check app.js with node, and if you can, open the page in the browser pane to confirm cards/previews/drawer/render work; then stop your server. Do NOT stop or restart the user's server on port 8765 — just tell me it needs a restart. Report concisely what you built.

Four agents are working in parallel:

| Agent | Building |
|---|---|
| Minecraft UI set | **Advancement toast** ("Challenge Complete!"), **boss health bar**, **XP level-up**, **Minecraft chat messages**, **/title-style big title**, **hotbar item select** |

  ## Report: 6 new HyperFrames meme templates
  
  I built all 6 templates, each with landscape and vertical versions. All 12 generated projects pass `npx hyperframes check`. Every one was rendered in preview mode in both orientations. All output is `yuva444p12le`, so the alpha channel is there. I pulled mid-frames out with ffmpeg, put them over a solid green background and looked at each one. I iterated on all of them before calling them done.
  
  I only created files under `studio/motion/templates/{word_slam,callout_arrow,speech_bubble,emoji_burst,versus_card,ranking_number}/`, plus the `landscape/` and `vertical/` projects that `mcs motion build` generates. `shared/`, `motion.py`, the existing templates and the README are untouched. Every template also accepts the standard `opaque` var.
  
  | Template | Length | Vars (default) | Preview render time (landscape / vertical) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `word_slam` | 1.4s | `text` ("BONK", 1–3 words, wraps), `color` (brand gold) | ~12s / 9s |
  | `callout_arrow` | 2.5s, stretchable ≥1.4s | `text` ("LOOK AT THIS"), `x` (0.62), `y` (0.55), `side` (left\|right, label side), `color` (redstone) | ~19s / 15s |
  | `speech_bubble` | 3.0s, stretchable ≥1.6s | `text`, `kind` (speech\|thought), `x` (0.5), `y` (0.3) as bubble centre, `tail` (left\|right) | 21s / 23s |
  | `emoji_burst` | 1.5s | `emoji` ("💀 😂 🔥 heart"), `x` (0.5), `y` (0.55), `count` (16) | 11s / 10s |
  | `versus_card` | 2.5s, stretchable ≥1.6s | `left` ("ME"), `right` ("THE WARDEN"), `left_color` (diamond), `right_color` (redstone), `label` ("VS") | 17s / 16s |
  | `ranking_number` | 2.5s, stretchable ≥1.6s | `number` ("3"), `title`, `accent` (gold) | 15s / 16s |
  
  Render times were measured one at a time. Two or three renders running in parallel take about 20–34s each. I did not run any full 60fps renders.
  
  **What each one does:**
  - **`word_slam`:** the word zooms in from 4x and squashes on impact. A comic burst (brand-colour outer ring, ink centre) pops behind it, with droplets and flying block/triangle shards, plus a decaying shake. It scales out over the last 0.3s.
  - **`callout_arrow`:** a hand-drawn ring draws on around the target, then a curved, outlined arrow draws from the label to the ring and the label pops in. During the hold the arrow pokes toward the target. The label goes above the target when it's low in the frame and below when it's high, and is kept inside safe margins (on vertical it stays clear of the Shorts UI).
  - **`speech_bubble`:**
    - Speech is a single outlined shape with its tail; thought is a cloud of lobes with trailing dots.
    - The bubble pops from the tail tip, the text types in letter by letter, then it bobs gently.
    - The bubble is kept fully on screen.
  - **`emoji_burst`:**
    - A gold starburst flash and a ring, then particles fly out on gravity arcs, spin and pop away.
    - In the `emoji` var, `heart`/`<3` and `star` become pixel-art sprites. Any plain word (e.g. `LOL`) becomes outlined caption text.
    - Emoji typed with no spaces between them are split up correctly.
  - **`versus_card`:** slanted striped panels slam in from opposite sides: left/right on landscape, top/bottom on vertical. The names land with overshoot. A VS burst then smashes into the seam with sparks and a shake, and the panels slide back out. Name colour switches between ink and paper automatically for contrast.
  - **`ranking_number`:** sunburst rays spin up and a block drops in. The "#N" slams onto it with a squash and shake, then the title bar wipes out from behind it. Badge on the left with the bar to the right on landscape; stacked on vertical.

On a machine without that font, emoji would come out wrong. The pixel heart and star sprites don't depend on any font.
  - **Some shapes are allowed to overlap or leave the frame.** Emoji particles and the ranking bar's entrance are marked as intentionally overlapping or off-screen, so the layout checker doesn't flag them.
  - **One small visual quirk:** on vertical, the `word_slam` burst spikes can poke a few pixels past the frame edge. The text itself never does.
  - **README not updated:** `studio/motion/README.md` doesn't list the new templates yet, because I was told to leave existing files alone. The table above can be pasted in as-is.

"""Pull a class of content out of the pack (quarantine, never delete).

    python studio/catalog/remove_content.py indian [--max-keep-s 0] [--dry-run]

indian: meme videos / green screens whose reviewed tags say origin "indian", or whose speech was detected as an
Indian language (hi, bn, ta, te, mr, pa, gu, ml, ur, kn). Clips up to --max-keep-s seconds can be kept
(0 = remove all). Files move to "Editing Pack/_Removed (review, then delete)/<reason>/", logged in moves.jsonl,
and drop out of the finder (that folder is catalogued as reference).
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from organize import PACK, move  # noqa: E402

CAT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
INDIAN = {"hi", "bn", "ta", "te", "mr", "pa", "gu", "ml", "ur", "kn", "ne"}
VIDEO_CATS = {"meme_video", "green_screen"}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("what", choices=["indian"])
    ap.add_argument("--max-keep-s", type=float, default=0.0)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    analysis = json.loads((CAT / "analysis.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if (CAT / "analysis.json").exists() else {}
    tags: dict = {}
    for f in sorted((CAT / "tags").glob("*.json")):
        for t in json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            tags[t["id"]] = t
    sp = CAT / "indian_sweep.json"                     # Hindi-title sweep (see remove_content usage)
    sweep = set(json.loads(sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))) if sp.exists() else set()
    sweep -= {i for i in sweep if "get-out-of-here" in i}  # English clip, false positive
    picked = []
    for r in scan:
        if r.get("duplicate_of") or r["path"].startswith(("_Duplicates", "_Removed")) or r["kind"] != "video":
            continue
        t = tags.get(r["id"], {})
        cat = t.get("category") or r["category"]
        if cat not in VIDEO_CATS:
            continue
        an = analysis.get(r["hash"], {})
        indian = t.get("origin") == "indian" or (an.get("lang") in INDIAN and (an.get("lang_p") or 0) >= 0.5)             or r["id"] in sweep
        if indian and (r.get("duration_s") or 0) > a.max_keep_s:
            picked.append(r)
    print(f"{len(picked)} Indian meme videos / green screens selected")
    for r in picked[:15]:
        print(f"   {r.get('duration_s', 0):5.1f}s  {r['path'][:90]}")
    if a.dry_run:
        return
    for r in picked:
        src = PACK / r["path"]
        if src.exists():
            move(src, PACK / "_Removed (review, then delete)" / "Indian memes" / Path(r["path"]).name,
                 "removed: indian meme (creator request)")
    print("moved. Re-run build_catalog.py + merge_catalog.py to refresh the database.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Deep analysis: what is SAID in every clip, and a richer look at every video.

    uv run python catalog/deep_analyze.py [--workers 4] [--model small]

For every asset that can contain speech (meme sounds, laughs, MLG, meme videos, green screens, new incoming):
  speech transcript with word timings + detected language (multilingual faster-whisper, CPU int8)
For every video: an 8-frame strip (thumbs8/<hash>.jpg) so taggers see the whole clip, not 4 moments.
Results: catalog/analysis.json keyed by content hash (incremental; re-runs only do new files).
The transcripts give taggers real quotes, exact punchline windows, and catch swearing/slurs the file
names don't reveal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import wave
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

CAT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = CAT.parents[1]
SPEECH_CATS = {"sfx_meme", "sfx_laugh", "sfx_mlg", "meme_video", "green_screen"}
_model = None


def _init(model_name: str, threads: int):
    """Parakeet (onnx, ~9x realtime on this CPU) for words + whisper-tiny for language id only."""
    global _model, _lid
    import os
    os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", str(threads))
    import onnx_asr
    from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    _model = onnx_asr.load_model("nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3", quantization="int8").with_timestamps()
    _lid = WhisperModel("tiny", device="cpu", compute_type="int8", cpu_threads=threads)


def _words(res) -> list:
    """Parakeet tokens (sentencepiece, '▁'/space = word start) -> [[word, start, end], ...]."""
    out = []
    toks, ts = list(res.tokens or []), list(res.timestamps or [])
    for i, (tok, t) in enumerate(zip(toks, ts)):
        end = ts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(ts) else t + 0.25
        if tok.startswith((" ", "▁")) or not out:
            out.append([tok.strip(" ▁"), round(t, 2), round(end, 2)])
        else:
            out[-1][0] += tok
            out[-1][2] = round(end, 2)
    return [w for w in out if w[0]]


def transcribe(job: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    h, path = job
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-t", "30", "-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000",
                            "-f", "s16le", "-"], capture_output=True)
        pcm = np.frombuffer(r.stdout, np.int16).astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
        if pcm.size < 1600 or np.abs(pcm).max() < 0.01:
            return h, {"speech": "", "lang": None, "words": [], "no_audio": True}
        res = _model.recognize(pcm, sample_rate=16000)
        speech = (res.text or "").strip()
        words = _words(res)[:120]
        lang, lp = None, 0.0
        if speech:
            lang, lp, _ = _lid.detect_language(pcm[: 16000 * 15])
        return h, {"speech": speech, "lang": lang, "lang_p": round(float(lp), 2), "words": words,
                   "engine": "parakeet-v3+whisper-tiny-lid"}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return h, {"error": str(e)}


def strip8(job: tuple[str, str, float]) -> str | None:
    h, path, dur = job
    out = CAT / "thumbs8" / f"{h}.jpg"
    if out.exists():
        return h
    tiles = []
    for k in range(8):
        t = dur * (0.04 + 0.92 * k / 7)
        r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-ss", f"{t:.2f}", "-i", path, "-frames:v", "1",
                            "-vf", "scale=240:135", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-"], capture_output=True)
        if len(r.stdout) >= 240 * 135 * 3:
            tiles.append(Image.frombytes("RGB", (240, 135), r.stdout[:240 * 135 * 3]))
    if not tiles:
        return None
    im = Image.new("RGB", (240 * 4, 135 * 2), (10, 10, 10))
    for k, t in enumerate(tiles):
        im.paste(t, ((k % 4) * 240, (k // 4) * 135))
    im.save(out, quality=78)
    return h


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="small")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    scan = json.loads((CAT / "scan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ap_path = CAT / "analysis.json"
    done = json.loads(ap_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if ap_path.exists() else {}
    live = [r for r in scan if not r.get("duplicate_of") and not r["path"].startswith("_Duplicates")]
    absp = lambda r: str(ROOT / r.get("root", "Editing Pack") / r["path"])  # noqa: E731
    done = {k: v for k, v in done.items() if v.get("engine")}       # redo anything from the old slow engine
    speech_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r)) for r in live if r.get("has_audio") and r["hash"] not in done
                   and (r["category"] in SPEECH_CATS or r["path"].startswith("_Incoming/"))
                   and (r.get("duration_s") or 0) <= 120]
    video_jobs = [(r["hash"], absp(r), r.get("duration_s") or 1.0) for r in live if r["kind"] == "video"]
    (CAT / "thumbs8").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    print(f"speech: {len(speech_jobs)} clips to transcribe; video strips: {len(video_jobs)}", flush=True)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as tp:
        strips = tp.map(strip8, video_jobs)
        threads = max(1, 12 // args.workers)
        with ProcessPoolExecutor(args.workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(args.model, threads)) as pp:
            for k, (h, res) in enumerate(pp.map(transcribe, speech_jobs, chunksize=4), 1):
                done[h] = res
                if k % 100 == 0:
                    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
                    print(f"  transcribed {k}/{len(speech_jobs)}", flush=True)
        n_strips = sum(1 for s in strips if s)
    ap_path.write_text(json.dumps(done, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    talk = sum(1 for v in done.values() if v.get("speech"))
    langs: dict[str, int] = {}
    for v in done.values():
        if v.get("lang"):
            langs[v["lang"]] = langs.get(v["lang"], 0) + 1
    print(f"done: {len(done)} analysed, {talk} contain speech, {n_strips} video strips; languages {langs}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```
1 mcs new <slug> --game <rec> [--mic <wav> --mic-offset s]   # creates projects/<slug>/project.json
2 mcs transcribe <slug>               # work/transcript.md + .json, word timings, SOURCE seconds
3 mcs analyze <slug>                  # work/signals.md (yells, game booms, scene cuts, silences) + work/sheets/overview_*.jpg
4 mcs scaffold <slug>                 # edit.json v0: dead air removed, music bed, captions on
5 PLAN (you)                          # beat sheet -> query assets -> write the EDL layers
6 mcs check <slug> --timeline         # validation, pacing densities, rating/copyright warnings
7 mcs render <slug> --preview         # 540p30, seconds-fast after the first run (segments cached)
8 VERIFY (you)                        # pull frames at every big beat, look at them, fix, re-render
9 mcs render <slug>                   # 1080p60 final -> out/<slug>.mp4, logs asset usage
```

2. **Write a beat sheet** in `projects/<slug>/BEATS.md`: one line per moment, `src_time | moment (taxonomy) | what happens | planned treatment`. Moments come from `studio/catalog/taxonomy.json` → `moments`. Aim for a beat every 3–8 seconds of kept footage. Mark the 2–3 biggest beats; those get the heaviest treatment.
3. **Pick assets per beat** with the finder. Ask for several and choose the one that fits the *context* (what was said, what happened), not just the top score:

   ```
   uv run mcs assets find --moment fail --role hit voice_line --project <slug> --limit 6
   uv run mcs assets find --text "sad violin" --project <slug>
   uv run mcs assets find --moment death --category green_screen meme_video --project <slug>
   ```
