tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

                s.setdefault("zoom", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "to": round(to, 3), "in": 0.06,
                                                 "hold": max(0.4, b["end"] - b["t"] + 0.3), "out": 0.15})
            if r.get("shake") and mode.get("shake", 1) > 0:
                s.setdefault("shake", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "dur": 0.45,
                                                  "amp": round(r["shake"] * mode.get("shake", 1))})
            if r.get("sfx") and abs(b["t"] - last["sfx"]) > 4.0 and self.n_sfx < self.max_sfx:
                moments, roles = r["sfx"]
                a = self.pick(moments + mode.get("sfx_moments", [])[:1], roles,
                              categories=["sfx_meme", "sfx_ui", "sfx_minecraft", "sfx_mlg", "sfx_laugh"],
                              max_duration=6)
                if a:
                    hit = "hit" in a.get("roles", [])
                    # impacts land on the word; reactions/stingers right AFTER it (never on the punchline)
                    t = b["t"] if hit else b["end"] + 0.1
                    if self.seg_of(segs, t) is s:
                        ev = {"asset": a["id"], "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(t, 3),
                              "align": "peak" if hit else "onset", "_beat": b["moment"]}
                        cap = sfx_cap(a)
                        if cap:
                            ev["dur"] = cap
                        sfx.append(ev)
                        self.n_sfx += 1
                        last["sfx"] = b["t"]
            recent_same = any(t["text"] == b.get("text") and abs(t.get("src_at", -99) - b["t"]) < 30 for t in texts)
            if b.get("text") and abs(b["t"] - last["text"]) > 3.5 and not recent_same:
                texts.append({"text": b["text"], "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(b["t"], 3), "dur": 1.1,
                              "y": 0.32, **({"style": "minecraft"} if b["moment"] == "loot" else {})})
                last["text"] = b["t"]
            if r.get("meme") and meme_budget and b["score"] >= 3 and abs(b["t"] - last["meme"]) > 25 \
                    and s["out"] - b["end"] < 1.5:
                a = self.pick(r["meme"], categories=["meme_video"], max_duration=12, max_rating="clean")
                if a:
                    lo, hi = meme_window(a, self.rng)
                    cutaways.append((s["id"], {"id": f"meme-{len(cutaways) + 1}", "type": "cutaway",
                                               "asset": a["id"], "in": lo, "out": round(hi, 2)}))
                    meme_budget -= 1
                    last["meme"] = b["t"]
            if r.get("greenscreen") and gs_budget and not b.get("death_screen") and abs(b["t"] - last["gs"]) > 30 \
                    and b["score"] >= 4 and b.get("phrase"):
                a = self.pick(r["greenscreen"], categories=["green_screen"], max_duration=10, max_rating="clean")
                if a and (a.get("moments") or [None])[0] not in r["greenscreen"]:
                    a = None                                     # only overlays made FOR this kind of moment
                if a:
                    full = a.get("placement") == "fullscreen"
                    overlays.append({"type": "greenscreen", "asset": a["id"], "seg": s["id"],
                                     "src_at": round(b["end"], 3), "dur": min(3.0, a["duration_s"]),
                                     **({} if full else {"x": 0.78, "y": 0.62, "scale": 0.5})})
                    gs_budget -= 1
                    last["gs"] = b["t"]
            if b["moment"] == "death" and b.get("death_screen"):
                s["freeze_end"] = max(s.get("freeze_end", 0), 1.6)
                s.setdefault("zoom", []).append({"src_at": round(b["t"] + 0.05, 3), "to": 1.35, "in": 1.4,
                                                 "focus": [0.5, 0.22]})
                s["mode"] = "sad"

        # running gag: a content word said 4+ times within 45 s gets a counter ("STICKS x1", "x2", ...)
        for word, times in running_gags(self.words).items():
            for n, (t, seg_t) in enumerate(times, 1):
                s = self.seg_of(segs, t)
                if not s:
                    continue
                last_one = n == len(times)
                texts.append({"text": f"{word.upper()} x{n}", "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(t, 3),
                              "dur": 1.5 if last_one else 0.9, "style": "minecraft", "x": 0.84, "y": 0.22,
                              "size": 120 if last_one else 80})
                if n == 1 or last_one or n % 3 == 0:
                    sfx.append({"asset": "sfx_ui.pop", "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(t, 3), "align": "peak",
                                "volume_db": -4})
                emphasis.add(word)

        for after, cut in cutaways:                          # insert meme cutaways after their beat segment
            k = next(i for i, x in enumerate(segs) if x["id"] == after)
            segs.insert(k + 1, cut)

        # montage labels
        for s in segs:
            if s.get("speed", 1) > 1:
                texts.append({"text": f"x{int(s['speed'])} SPEED", "seg": s["id"], "rel": 0.0, "dur": 1.4,
                              "style": "label", "x": 0.86, "y": 0.1})

        # ---- cold open: tease the strongest late beat
        lead = []
        dur_src = self.pj.get("duration_s") or 0
        cands = [b for b in beats if b["moment"] in ("panic", "death", "shock", "jumpscare", "explosion")
                 and b["t"] > dur_src * 0.4 and b["score"] >= 4]
        if self.cold_open and cands and duration > 40:
            # tease with the creator's own line when there is one ("I'm actually gonna die"), then the death screen
            top = max(cands, key=lambda b: (b["score"], bool(b["phrase"]) and not b.get("death_screen"), b["t"]))
            a = max(0.0, top["t"] - 1.2)
            z = top["end"] + 0.8
            lead.append({"id": "cold-1", "type": "source", "in": round(a, 3), "out": round(z, 3),
                         "zoom": [{"src_at": round(top["t"], 3), "to": 1.3, "in": 0.06, "hold": 0.6, "out": 0.2}]})
            ds = next((d for d in self.sig.get("death_screens", []) if d["t"] > top["t"]), None)
            if ds:
                lead.append({"id": "cold-2", "type": "source", "in": round(ds["t"] - 0.05, 3),
                             "out": round(ds["t"] + 0.9, 3), "freeze_end": 0.4,
                             "zoom": [{"src_at": round(ds["t"], 3), "to": 1.35, "in": 0.3, "focus": [0.5, 0.22]}]})
            first_src = next((s["in"] for s in segs if s["type"] == "source"), 0)
            gap = top["t"] - first_src
            label = f"{max(1, round(gap / 60))} MINUTE{'S' if round(gap / 60) > 1 else ''} EARLIER" if gap >= 75 \
                else "EARLIER..."
            a_rewind = self.pick(["time_skip"], ["whoosh", "stinger"], categories=["sfx_meme", "sfx_ui"])
            if a_rewind:
                sfx.append({"asset": a_rewind["id"], "seg": segs[0]["id"], "rel": 0.0, "dur": 1.2})
            overlays.append({"type": "motion", "template": "time_card", "vars": {"text": label},
                             "seg": segs[0]["id"], "rel": 0.0})
            sfx.append(self._sfx_for(["shock", "panic"], ["hit", "stinger"], "cold-1", top["t"], "peak"))
        segs = lead + segs
        sfx = [x for x in sfx if x]

        # ---- intro title + outro CTA
        title = self.pj.get("title") or self.slug
        first_main = next(s for s in segs if not s["id"].startswith("cold"))
        overlays.append({"type": "motion", "template": "title_card",
                         "vars": {"title": title.upper()[:40], "subtitle": self.brand.get("channel_name", "")},
                         "seg": first_main["id"], "rel": 1.9 if lead else 0.4})
        if duration > 45:                                # subscribe CTA in a CALM stretch - never on a joke or a panic
            t, calm = 0.0, None
            for s in segs:
                d = seg_duration(s, lambda i: A.get(i))
                strong = any(s["type"] == "source" and s["in"] <= b["t"] < s["out"] and b["score"] >= 3 for b in beats)
                if (s["type"] == "source" and not s["id"].startswith("cold") and s.get("mode") == self.base_mode
                        and not strong and d >= 3.5 and 0.35 * duration <= t <= 0.75 * duration):
                    calm = s
                    break
                t += d
            if calm:
                overlays.append({"type": "motion", "template": "subscribe",
                                 "vars": {"channel_name": self.brand.get("channel_name", "")},
                                 "seg": calm["id"], "rel": 0.3})
                self.caption_hides.append({"seg": calm["id"], "rel": 0.3, "dur": 3.5})
        # (mode stingers are a manual tool now - automatic colour flashes were distracting)

        edl = {"version": 1, "project": self.slug, "title": title, "mode": self.base_mode,
               "generator": "autoplan", "segments": segs, "overlays": overlays, "text": texts,
               "audio": {"sfx": sfx, "bleeps": [], "music": []},
               "captions": {"enabled": True, "emphasis_words": sorted(emphasis)[:20], "hide": self.caption_hides}}
        wm = self.brand.get("watermark", {})
        if wm.get("enabled"):
            edl["watermark"] = {"text": wm.get("text", ""), "opacity": wm.get("opacity", 0.55)}
        engage(edl, self.words, self.modes)
        self.music(edl)
        for x in edl["audio"]["sfx"]:
            x.pop("_beat", None)
        return edl

# Minecraft Channel: automated editing studio

This folder contains:
- `Editing Pack/`: the unified asset pack. It combines the original pack with the v2 archives, deduplicated and organised into `Sound Effects/`, `Music/`, `Meme Videos/`, `Green Screen/`, `Overlays & VFX/`, `Transitions/`, `Animations/`, `Backgrounds/`, `Images/`, `Fonts/` and a few more (the full tree is in `catalog/taxonomy.json` → `folders`).
  - Asset ids are content-stable (`catalog/identity.json`), so files can move without breaking tags or edits.
  - Ids of merged-away duplicates are mapped in `catalog/redirects.json`.
  - Every move is logged in `catalog/moves.jsonl`; undo with `python studio/catalog/organize.py undo`.
  - Quarantined duplicates sit in `_Duplicates (review, then delete)/`.
- `Stock Library/`: the creator's own footage (B-roll, stock, memes, music). Index it with `uv run mcs library scan`, then tag it.
- `studio/`: the editing assembly line (Python package `mcstudio`, CLI `mcs`, uv project pinned to Python 3.12).
  - `catalog/`: the asset database pipeline. `build_catalog.py` (technical scan) → `tags/*.json` (LLM semantic tags, see `TAGGING.md`) → `merge_catalog.py` → `assets.db`. The vocabulary lives in `taxonomy.json`. Hand corrections go in `overrides.json` (`{"<asset id>": {field: value}}`), and they win over the tags.
  - `projects/<slug>/`: one folder per episode. `project.json` (sources), `edit.json` (the EDL), `work/` (transcript, signals, renders cache), `out/` (videos).
  - `style.json`: channel look (caption font and colours, text styles, audio levels, pacing targets, encoders).
  - `docs/TOOLS.md`: tool research and roadmap.
  - `ui/` + `mcstudio/server.py`: the local web UI (`uv run mcs ui`).
- `studio/modes.json` (mood modes), `studio/looks.json` (colour presets), `studio/brand/` (channel identity and narrator avatar), `studio/motion/` (HyperFrames motion-graphics templates).
- `.claude/skills/mc-edit/`: the editing skill. **Use it for any editing request.**

Adding a new asset pack (zips anywhere):
1. `python studio/catalog/extract_archives.py "<pack>" "<pack>/_extracted"` (nested zips are handled)
2. `uv run studio/catalog/dedupe.py "Editing Pack/<relevant folders>" "<pack>/_extracted" --out studio/catalog/dedupe_<n>.json`
3. `python studio/catalog/organize.py stage "<pack>/_extracted" studio/catalog/dedupe_<n>.json` (unique files go to `Editing Pack/_Incoming/<pack>/`)
4. `uv run studio/catalog/build_catalog.py`, then `uv run python studio/catalog/deep_analyze.py` (transcripts and 8-frame strips)
5. `uv run python studio/catalog/make_review_batches.py`, then tag the batches with parallel agents (TAGGING.md, "Review pass")
6. `python studio/catalog/organize.py plan && python studio/catalog/organize.py apply`, then build_catalog, `rebuild_redirects.py` and merge_catalog

Removing a class of content: `python studio/catalog/remove_content.py indian --dry-run` (moves to `_Removed (review, then delete)/`, never deletes).

Conventions:
- Run commands from `studio/` with `uv run mcs ...`. ffmpeg 9 is on PATH.
- No NVIDIA GPU: keep heavy ML on CPU (int8) or hosted APIs.
- Never auto-use assets rated `banned`. The finder and `mcs check` enforce this.
- Image/GIF overlays must go through the `movie=` source filter (looped image inputs deadlock ffmpeg 9's scheduler). render.py already does this.

- [MC Studio project](mc-studio-project.md) — automated Minecraft edit pipeline, skill, UI; CPU-only machine
- [Editing feedback](feedback-editing-style.md) — SFX under voice, no clipped words, short meme beats, subtle looks, lots of zooms

content.content:
repeat call costs nothing. `--preview` renders 960x540 / 540x960 at 30fps. A full render is 1920x1080 /
1080x1920 at 60fps, supersampled 2x from the same layout, so previews and finals line up exactly.
`--force` re-renders.

## Templates

| Template | Length | Kind | Vars (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title_card` | 2.5s | card/overlay | `title` ("I DUG TO BEDROCK"), `subtitle` ("EPISODE 1", empty = none), `accent` (brand gold) |
| `chapter` | 2.0s | overlay | `chapter` ("CHAPTER 2"), `name` ("THE DEEP DARK"), `accent` (gold) |
| `time_card` | 1.8s | overlay/card | `text` ("3 HOURS LATER"), `accent` (gold) |
| `lower_third` | 3.0s, stretchable >=1.4s | overlay | `text` ("STEVE"), `sub` ("PROFESSIONAL CAVE GOBLIN", empty = none), `icon` (first letter of `text`), `accent` (grass) |
| `subscribe` | 3.5s | overlay | `channel_name` (brand), `label` ("SUBSCRIBE"), `done_label` ("SUBSCRIBED"), `accent` (redstone) |
| `counter` | 2.0s | overlay | `label` ("DAY"), `from` (1), `to` (100), `prefix` (""), `suffix` (""), `accent` (diamond) |
| `hook_banner` | 3.0s, stretchable >=1s | overlay, vertical-first | `text` (`*word*` = highlighted word), `accent` (redstone), `badge` ("!", empty = none) |
| `end_screen` | 10s, stretchable >=5s | overlay/card | `channel_name`, `tagline` (brand), `left_label` ("WATCH NEXT"), `right_label` ("BEST VIDEO"), `accent` (gold), `scrim` (0.62 background dim) |
| `mode_stinger` | 0.6s | transition | `color` (amethyst), `label` ("" = none, e.g. "MEANWHILE") |

All templates also accept `opaque` (set it with `opaque=True` / `--opaque`, not `--var`).

Behaviour notes:
- **title_card**: blocks rain in and stack into a plinth (0 to 0.9s). The title slams onto it at 0.95s with a screen shake and a burst of dust, the subtitle tag pops at 1.3s, and everything clears in the last 0.3s.
- **chapter**: an ink band with a gold under-stripe and stepped pixel edges wipes in from the left, the chapter name types in letter by letter, then the band wipes out to the right in the last 0.4s.
- **lower_third**: sits lower-left (landscape) or at 66% height (vertical, above the Shorts UI). It exits over the last 0.42s. `--duration` lengthens the hold.
- **subscribe**: a cursor clicks the stone button at 1.05s (it turns `accent` and reads SUBSCRIBED), then rings the bell at 1.86s. It exits at 3.2s.
- **counter**: the value ticks from 0.24s to 1.39s with a power2 in-out ease, then punches and flashes `accent`. Values are rounded integers.
- **hook_banner**: pops in at the top (8.5% from the top on vertical, clear of the Shorts header) and stays until the end with no exit. To keep it longer, use `--duration`, or let the renderer hold the last frame.
- **end_screen**: the video rectangles are left empty (transparent) and the borders sit outside them. In 1920x1080 output pixels: left video `x=100 y=360 w=760 h=428`, right video `x=1060 y=360 w=760 h=428`, subscribe circle `x=840 y=820 d=240`. The same rectangles are in `templates/end_screen/template.json` under `layout_1920x1080`. Place the YouTube end-screen elements on them. The vertical version stacks the frames.
- **mode_stinger**: the frame is **fully covered from 0.26s to 0.32s**, so cut the underlying footage at **0.29s** (`cut_at` in template.json). The label colour switches automatically between paper and ink for contrast.

## EDL snippets
- **Narration avatar** ("Blocky", in `studio/brand/avatar/`): appears automatically in narration mode, or set
  `"avatar": true` per segment.
  - The expression follows the mode; override it with `avatar_mood`.
  - To use the creator's own skin: `mcs avatar build --skin <png>`.
- **Motion graphics** (`studio/motion/`, built with HyperFrames):
  - Overlay: `{"type":"motion","template":"time_card","vars":{"text":"3 HOURS LATER"}}`
  - Card: `{"type":"card","template":"title_card","vars":{...}}`
  - Templates: title_card, chapter, time_card, lower_third, subscribe, counter, hook_banner, end_screen, mode_stinger.
  - For mode_stinger, cut the footage underneath at 0.29 s.
- **Stock and B-roll**: the creator's `Stock Library/` is in the same database (`--category broll stock`).
  - Use B-roll as full-frame `video` overlays with `"audio": false` while the voice continues.
- **Engagement**: `mcs engage <slug>` adds attention zooms (punch-ins on stressed words, 1.0x/1.1x reframes across
  jump cuts) so something changes every few seconds.
  - Auto zooms are marked `"auto": true` and are replaced on each re-run.

- **Favourites**: the creator stars assets (UI ★ or `mcs assets fav <id>`). Starred assets get a finder bonus,
  so prefer them when they fit. Use `--favorites` to list them, and ask "use my favourites" on request.
- **Spoken content**: memes and sounds are transcribed (`speech` column, full-text searchable). Search by quote,
  e.g. `mcs assets find --text "I can do this all day"`, and use word timings (`use_window`) to cut to the punchline.

## Copyright (creator policy)

import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel")
T = ROOT / "studio" / "motion" / "templates"
NEW = ["word_slam", "callout_arrow", "speech_bubble", "emoji_burst", "versus_card", "ranking_number",
       "advancement_toast", "boss_bar", "xp_level_up", "chat_message", "mc_title", "hotbar_select",
       "pixel_wipe", "block_break_wipe", "location_tag", "countdown", "progress_tracker", "question_card"]


def fmt(v):
    if v is None:
        return "brand"
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return f'"{v}"' if len(v) < 40 else f'"{v[:37]}..."'
    return json.dumps(v)


rows = []
for n in NEW:
    m = json.loads((T / n / "template.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    dur = f'{m.get("duration")}s' + (f', {m["duration_rule"]}' if m.get("duration_rule") else "") \
        + (", stretchable" if m.get("stretchable") else "")
    vs = ", ".join(f"`{k}` ({'brand' if 'brand' in s else fmt(s.get('default'))})"
                   for k, s in m.get("vars", {}).items() if k != "opaque")
    rows.append(f"| `{n}` | {dur} | {m.get('kind', 'overlay')} | {vs} |")

readme = T.parent / "README.md"
s = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
anchor = '| `mode_stinger` | 0.6s | transition | `color` (amethyst), `label` ("" = none, e.g. "MEANWHILE") |'
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
s = s.replace(anchor, anchor + "\n" + "\n".join(rows))
notes_anchor = "## EDL snippets" if "## EDL snippets" in s else None
extra = """
More behaviour notes (newer templates):
- **pixel_wipe / block_break_wipe**: full-frame block transitions. Fully covered at 0.37-0.48s / 0.30-0.52s, so cut the footage at **0.42s** (`cut_at` in template.json). `style` picks the block texture.
- **countdown**: one second per number plus GO!. The duration follows `from` automatically (`from + 1`).
- **advancement_toast / hotbar_select / location_tag `icon`**: a built-in icon name, a data URI, a URL, or a local image path (motion.py inlines local files).
- **chat_message**: `lines` separated by `|`; `<Name> text` = player chat, otherwise yellow system text; `&a` colour codes work.
- **question_card**: side-by-side on landscape, stacked on vertical.
- Vertical layouts keep clear of the Shorts header (top ~10%) and the caption/buttons zone (bottom ~26%).
"""
if "More behaviour notes (newer templates)" not in s:
    i = s.find("\n## ", s.find("Behaviour notes:"))
    s = s[:i] + "\n" + extra + s[i:] if i > 0 else s + extra
readme.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")

sk = ROOT / ".claude" / "skills" / "mc-edit" / "SKILL.md"
s = sk.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = "  - Templates: title_card, chapter, time_card, lower_third, subscribe, counter, hook_banner, end_screen, mode_stinger.\n  - For mode_stinger, cut the footage underneath at 0.29 s."
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, """  - Templates (27, previews in the UI under Motion graphics; vars in `studio/motion/README.md`):
    - Channel: title_card, chapter, time_card, lower_third, subscribe, counter, hook_banner, end_screen
    - Comedy callouts: word_slam (BONK/OOF impact word), callout_arrow ("THAT'S ME" pointer), speech_bubble,
      emoji_burst, versus_card, ranking_number
    - Minecraft UI: advancement_toast, boss_bar, xp_level_up, chat_message, mc_title, hotbar_select
    - Info: location_tag, countdown, progress_tracker ("DIAMONDS 3/10"), question_card (would-you-rather)
    - Transitions: mode_stinger (cut at 0.29 s), pixel_wipe and block_break_wipe (cut at 0.42 s)
  - Use them where they literally fit the moment, and sparingly: one game-UI graphic per beat, never stacked
    with a meme or green screen on the same line. autoplan already places advancement_toast (diamonds, max 2),
    location_tag (named places, max 2) and boss_bar (named bosses, max 1).""")
sk.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")
print("docs ok", len(rows))

"""Cut the Crodie brand sheets into individual transparent PNGs (rembg + connected components)."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from rembg import new_session, remove
from scipy import ndimage

SRC = Path(r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\Crodie")
OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
sess = new_session("isnet-general-use")

# (name, file, box) - panels of the sheets; header strips excluded
PANELS = [
    ("char", "assets.png", (0, 62, 768, 515)),
    ("logo", "assets.png", (770, 62, 1536, 515)),
    ("emote", "assets.png", (0, 575, 522, 1024)),
    ("scene", "assets.png", (524, 575, 1076, 1024)),
    ("lower", "assets.png", (1078, 575, 1536, 1024)),
    ("skin", "mc skin.png", (0, 60, 820, 640)),
    ("hero", "mc skin.png", (770, 0, 1254, 640)),
    ("head", "mc skin.png", (425, 700, 1240, 870)),
    ("pfp", "profile pic.png", (0, 0, 1254, 1254)),
]
index = []
for name, f, box in PANELS:
    im = Image.open(SRC / f).convert("RGB").crop(box)
    up = 2 if im.width < 1000 else 1
    big = im.resize((im.width * up, im.height * up), Image.LANCZOS)
    cut = remove(big, session=sess, post_process_mask=True)
    cut.save(OUT / f"_{name}_panel.png")
    a = np.array(cut)[:, :, 3]
    if name in ("hero", "pfp"):
        labels, n = (a > 40).astype(int), 1
    else:
        mask = ndimage.binary_dilation(a > 60, iterations=6 * up)
        labels, n = ndimage.label(mask)
    for k, sl in enumerate(ndimage.find_objects(labels), 1):
        if sl is None:
            continue
        h, w = sl[0].stop - sl[0].start, sl[1].stop - sl[1].start
        if h * w < (40 * up) ** 2:
            continue
        piece = cut.crop((sl[1].start, sl[0].start, sl[1].stop, sl[0].stop))
        pa = np.array(piece)
        lab = labels[sl] == k
        pa[:, :, 3] = np.where(lab, pa[:, :, 3], 0)
        p = f"{name}_{len([i for i in index if i['set'] == name]) + 1:02d}.png"
        Image.fromarray(pa).save(OUT / p)
        index.append({"file": p, "set": name, "x": sl[1].start // up + box[0], "y": sl[0].start // up + box[1],
                      "w": w // up, "h": h // up, "px": [w, h]})
    print(name, sum(1 for i in index if i["set"] == name), flush=True)
(OUT / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1))

# contact sheets per set, labelled
for s in sorted({i["set"] for i in index}):
    items = [i for i in index if i["set"] == s]
    cell = 170
    cols = 8
    rows = (len(items) + cols - 1) // cols
    sh = Image.new("RGB", (cols * cell, rows * (cell + 16)), (60, 60, 70))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(sh)
    for j, it in enumerate(items):
        im = Image.open(OUT / it["file"])
        im.thumbnail((cell - 8, cell - 8))
        x, y = (j % cols) * cell, (j // cols) * (cell + 16)
        sh.paste(im, (x + 4, y + 4), im)
        d.text((x + 4, y + cell), f"{it['file']} {it['w']}x{it['h']}", fill=(255, 255, 0))
    sh.save(OUT / f"sheet_{s}.png")
print("done", len(index))

input.content:
"""Slice the creator's transparent brand sheets (Crodie/*.png) into one PNG per sticker.

    uv run python brand/slice_sheets.py            # -> brand/crodie/<sheet>/<sheet>_NN.png + index.json + sheet_*.png

Pieces are found from the sheet's real alpha: opaque blobs, slightly dilated so sparkles / hearts / "zzz" stay
attached to their sticker, tiny leftovers merged into the nearest big piece. Named later via names.json.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage

STUDIO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = STUDIO.parent / "Crodie"
OUT = STUDIO / "brand" / "crodie"
SHEETS = {"emotes": "emotes.png", "characters": "character renders.png", "logos": "logos and text.png",
          "overlays": "overlays.png", "cta": "other overlays.png"}
DILATE = {"emotes": 4, "characters": 5, "logos": 4, "overlays": 5, "cta": 6}


def slice_sheet(key: str, fname: str) -> list[dict]:
    im = Image.open(SRC / fname).convert("RGBA")
    rgba = np.array(im)
    a = rgba[:, :, 3]
    solid = a > 24
    lab, n = ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_dilation(solid, iterations=DILATE[key]))
    objs = ndimage.find_objects(lab)
    areas = ndimage.sum(solid, lab, range(1, n + 1))
    big = [i for i in range(n) if areas[i] >= 1500]
    small = [i for i in range(n) if 0 < areas[i] < 1500]
    centre = lambda sl: ((sl[0].start + sl[0].stop) / 2, (sl[1].start + sl[1].stop) / 2)  # noqa: E731
    owner = {i: i for i in big}
    for i in small:                      # sparkle / note / tear -> nearest big sticker (if close)
        cy, cx = centre(objs[i])
        best = min(big, key=lambda j: (centre(objs[j])[0] - cy) ** 2 + (centre(objs[j])[1] - cx) ** 2)
        by, bx = centre(objs[best])
        if abs(by - cy) < 140 and abs(bx - cx) < 160:
            owner[i] = best
    groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    for i, o in owner.items():
        groups.setdefault(o, []).append(i)
    pieces = []
    for o, members in groups.items():
        mask = np.isin(lab, [m + 1 for m in members]) & (a > 0)
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask)
        y0, y1, x0, x1 = ys.min(), ys.max() + 1, xs.min(), xs.max() + 1
        pieces.append((y0, x0, y1, x1, mask))
    # reading order: rows (by centre y bands), then x
    pieces.sort(key=lambda p: (round(((p[0] + p[2]) / 2) / 120), p[1]))
    d = OUT / key
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for f in d.glob(f"{key}_*.png"):
        f.unlink()                       # our own generated slices only
    out = []
    for k, (y0, x0, y1, x1, mask) in enumerate(pieces, 1):
        crop = rgba[y0:y1, x0:x1].copy()
        crop[:, :, 3] = np.where(mask[y0:y1, x0:x1], crop[:, :, 3], 0)
        name = f"{key}_{k:02d}.png"
        Image.fromarray(crop).save(d / name)
        out.append({"file": f"{key}/{name}", "sheet": key, "box": [int(x0), int(y0), int(x1), int(y1)],
                    "w": int(x1 - x0), "h": int(y1 - y0)})
    return out


def contact(items: list[dict], path: Path):
    cell, cols = 190, 8
    rows = (len(items) + cols - 1) // cols
    sh = Image.new("RGB", (cols * cell, rows * (cell + 18)), (90, 90, 106))
    dr = ImageDraw.Draw(sh)
    for j, it in enumerate(items):
        im = Image.open(OUT / it["file"])
        im.thumbnail((cell - 10, cell - 10))

    uv run python brand/slice_sheets.py            # -> brand/crodie/<sheet>/<sheet>_NN.png + index.json + sheet_*.png

Pieces are found from the sheet's real alpha: opaque blobs, slightly dilated so sparkles / hearts / "zzz" stay
attached to their sticker, tiny leftovers merged into the nearest big piece. Named later via names.json.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage

STUDIO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = STUDIO.parent / "Crodie"
OUT = STUDIO / "brand" / "crodie"
SHEETS = {"emotes": "emotes.png", "characters": "character renders.png", "logos": "logos and text.png",
          "overlays": "overlays.png", "cta": "other overlays.png"}
DILATE = {"emotes": 4, "characters": 5, "logos": 4, "overlays": 5, "cta": 6}


def slice_sheet(key: str, fname: str) -> list[dict]:
    im = Image.open(SRC / fname).convert("RGBA")
    rgba = np.array(im)
    a = rgba[:, :, 3]
    solid = a > 24
    lab, n = ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_dilation(solid, iterations=DILATE[key]))
    objs = ndimage.find_objects(lab)
    areas = ndimage.sum(solid, lab, range(1, n + 1))
    big = [i for i in range(n) if areas[i] >= 1500]
    small = [i for i in range(n) if 0 < areas[i] < 1500]
    centre = lambda sl: ((sl[0].start + sl[0].stop) / 2, (sl[1].start + sl[1].stop) / 2)  # noqa: E731
    owner = {i: i for i in big}
    for i in small:                      # sparkle / note / tear -> nearest big sticker (if close)
        cy, cx = centre(objs[i])
        best = min(big, key=lambda j: (centre(objs[j])[0] - cy) ** 2 + (centre(objs[j])[1] - cx) ** 2)
        by, bx = centre(objs[best])
        if abs(by - cy) < 140 and abs(bx - cx) < 160:
            owner[i] = best
    groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
    for i, o in owner.items():
        groups.setdefault(o, []).append(i)
    pieces = []
    for o, members in groups.items():
        mask = np.isin(lab, [m + 1 for m in members]) & (a > 0)
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask)
        y0, y1, x0, x1 = ys.min(), ys.max() + 1, xs.min(), xs.max() + 1
        pieces.append((y0, x0, y1, x1, mask))
    # reading order: rows (by centre y bands), then x
    pieces.sort(key=lambda p: (round(((p[0] + p[2]) / 2) / 120), p[1]))
    d = OUT / key
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for f in d.glob(f"{key}_*.png"):
        f.unlink()                       # our own generated slices only
    out = []
    for k, (y0, x0, y1, x1, mask) in enumerate(pieces, 1):
        crop = rgba[y0:y1, x0:x1].copy()
        crop[:, :, 3] = np.where(mask[y0:y1, x0:x1], crop[:, :, 3], 0)
        name = f"{key}_{k:02d}.png"
        Image.fromarray(crop).save(d / name)

    return out

    rows = (len(items) + cols - 1) // cols

        im = Image.open(OUT / it["file"])
        im.thumbnail((cell - 10, cell - 10))
        x, y = (j % cols) * cell, (j // cols) * (cell + 18)
        sh.paste(im, (x + 5, y + 5), im)
        dr.text((x + 5, y + cell), f"{Path(it['file']).stem}  {it['w']}x{it['h']}", fill=(255, 255, 0))
    sh.save(path)


def main():
    index = []
    for key, f in SHEETS.items():
        items = slice_sheet(key, f)
        contact(items, OUT / f"_sheet_{key}.png")
        index += items
        print(f"{key}: {len(items)} pieces")
    (OUT / "slices.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    uv run python brand/slice_sheets.py            # -> brand/crodie/<sheet>/<sheet>_NN.png + index.json + sheet_*.png

Pieces are found from the sheet's real alpha: opaque blobs, slightly dilated so sparkles / hearts / "zzz" stay
attached to their sticker, tiny leftovers merged into the nearest big piece. Named later via names.json.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage

STUDIO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = STUDIO.parent / "Crodie"
OUT = STUDIO / "brand" / "crodie"
SHEETS = {"emotes": "emotes.png", "characters": "character renders.png", "logos": "logos and text.png",
          "overlays": "overlays.png", "cta": "other overlays.png"}
ERODE = {"emotes": 3, "characters": 3, "logos": 3, "overlays": 3, "cta": 4}


def slice_sheet(key: str, fname: str) -> list[dict]:
    im = Image.open(SRC / fname).convert("RGBA")
    rgba = np.array(im)
    a = rgba[:, :, 3]
    solid = ndimage.binary_erosion(a > 200, iterations=ERODE[key])     # cores: glow halos don't bridge
    lab, n = ndimage.label(solid)
    objs = ndimage.find_objects(lab)
    areas = ndimage.sum(solid, lab, range(1, n + 1))
    big = [i for i in range(n) if areas[i] >= 2500]
    centre = lambda sl: ((sl[0].start + sl[0].stop) / 2, (sl[1].start + sl[1].stop) / 2)  # noqa: E731
    keep = np.zeros(n + 1, int)
    for i in big:
        keep[i + 1] = i + 1
    for i in range(n):                   # sparkle / note / tear core -> nearest big sticker if close
        if keep[i + 1] or not objs[i]:
            continue
        cy, cx = centre(objs[i])
        best = min(big, key=lambda j: (centre(objs[j])[0] - cy) ** 2 + (centre(objs[j])[1] - cx) ** 2)
        by, bx = centre(objs[best])
        bh = objs[best][0].stop - objs[best][0].start
        bw = objs[best][1].stop - objs[best][1].start
        if abs(by - cy) < bh * 0.85 and abs(bx - cx) < bw * 0.85:
            keep[i + 1] = best + 1
    lab = keep[lab]
    # every visible pixel (glow, outline) belongs to the nearest core
    _, (iy, ix) = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(lab == 0, return_indices=True)
    near = lab[iy, ix]
    dist = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(lab == 0)
    owned = np.where((a > 0) & (dist < 40), near, 0)
    pieces = []
    for o in sorted(set(np.unique(owned)) - {0}):
        mask = owned == o
        ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask)
        y0, y1, x0, x1 = ys.min(), ys.max() + 1, xs.min(), xs.max() + 1
        pieces.append((y0, x0, y1, x1, mask))
    # reading order: rows (by centre y bands), then x
    pieces.sort(key=lambda p: (round(((p[0] + p[2]) / 2) / 120), p[1]))
    d = OUT / key
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for f in d.glob(f"{key}_*.png"):
        f.unlink()                       # our own generated slices only
    out = []
    for k, (y0, x0, y1, x1, mask) in enumerate(pieces, 1):
        crop = rgba[y0:y1, x0:x1].copy()
        crop[:, :, 3] = np.where(mask[y0:y1, x0:x1], crop[:, :, 3], 0)
        name = f"{key}_{k:02d}.png"
        Image.fromarray(crop).save(d / name)
        out.append({"file": f"{key}/{name}", "sheet": key, "box": [int(x0), int(y0), int(x1), int(y1)],
                    "w": int(x1 - x0), "h": int(y1 - y0)})
    return out


def contact(items: list[dict], path: Path):
    cell, cols = 190, 8
    rows = (len(items) + cols - 1) // cols
    sh = Image.new("RGB", (cols * cell, rows * (cell + 18)), (90, 90, 106))
    dr = ImageDraw.Draw(sh)
    for j, it in enumerate(items):
        im = Image.open(OUT / it["file"])
        im.thumbnail((cell - 10, cell - 10))
        x, y = (j % cols) * cell, (j // cols) * (cell + 18)
        sh.paste(im, (x + 5, y + 5), im)
        dr.text((x + 5, y + cell), f"{Path(it['file']).stem}  {it['w']}x{it['h']}", fill=(255, 255, 0))
    sh.save(path)


def main():
    index = []
    for key, f in SHEETS.items():
        items = slice_sheet(key, f)
        contact(items, OUT / f"_sheet_{key}.png")
        index += items
        print(f"{key}: {len(items)} pieces")
    (OUT / "slices.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

       "overlays": "facecam frames, stream scenes, alerts",
       "cta": "call-to-action banner: subscribe / like / comment prompts (sticker_pop, calm stretches only)"}


def main():

            out.append({"id": f"crodie.{prefix}{name}", "set": key, "file": f"brand/crodie/{key}/{dst.name}",

    (D / "stickers.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(len(out), "stickers named")


if __name__ == "__main__":

input.prompt: Build ONE new HyperFrames motion-graphics template named `sticker_pop` for the Minecraft channel "Crodie" studio at `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\motion\`. Context: templates live in `studio/motion/templates//` with `template.json`, `markup.html`, `template.css`, `template.js`; `mcstudio/motion.py` generates `landscape/` and `vertical/` HyperFrames projects from them (`uv run python -c "from mcstudio import motion as M; M.build('sticker_pop')"`) and renders with `M.render(name, vars, orientation, preview=True)` -> ProRes 4444 alpha .mov in motion/cache. Study 2-3 existing templates first (e.g. `emoji_burst`, `advancement_toast`, `word_slam`, `location_tag`) plus `studio/motion/README.md` and the shared files in `studio/motion/shared/` to copy the conventions exactly (manifest fields, brand vars, `opaque`, vertical safe zones, determinism, `npx hyperframes check`). Load the `hyperframes` skill domain guidance if needed (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`). Do NOT modify motion.py, shared/, or other templates. What sticker_pop does: shows ONE transparent PNG sticker (the channel mascot's emotes, logos, CTA banners) with a punchy, cartoon "sticker" animation, for reaction beats in edits. Vars: - `image` (string): the sticker. motion.py already converts a local file path to a data: URI before rendering, so in the page treat it as an . Default: a real Crodie emote as a data URI is too big for the manifest — instead default to the relative path of a file you copy INTO the template folder, e.g. `templates/sticker_pop/default.png` copied from `studio/brand/crodie/emotes/shocked_exclaim.png` (check how markup/projects resolve asset paths; if a relative default can't load in the generated projects, make motion.py-free fallback: empty image = draw nothing, and document that the caller must pass `image`). dups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
for r in scan:
    if r.get("duplicate_of"):

# what is actually SAID in each clip (catalog/deep_analyze.py), keyed by content hash
_an_p = OUT / "analysis.json"

jsonl = []
n_tagged = 0
for r in scan:
    if r.get("duplicate_of"):
        continue
    t = tags.get(r["id"], {})
    n_tagged += bool(t)
    a = r.get("audio_analysis") or {}
    v = r.get("video") or {}
    im = r.get("image") or {}
    uw = t.get("use_window") or [None, None]
    row = {
        "id": r["id"], "root": r.get("root", "Editing Pack"), "path": r["path"], "category": r["category"],
        "subfolder": r["subfolder"],
        "kind": r["kind"], "title": r["title"], "duration_s": r.get("duration_s"),
        "width": v.get("width") or im.get("width"), "height": v.get("height") or im.get("height"),
        "fps": v.get("fps"), "has_audio": int(bool(r.get("has_audio"))),

        "roles": json.dumps(t.get("roles") or []), "tags": json.dumps(t.get("tags") or [], ensure_ascii=False),

        "content_rating": t.get("content_rating"),

        "copyright_risk": t.get("copyright_risk"), "risk_level": RISK_ORDER.get(t.get("copyright_risk"), 1),
        "placement": t.get("placement"), "use_in": uw[0], "use_out": uw[1],
        "volume_db": t.get("volume_db") or 0, "frequency": t.get("frequency"), "notes": t.get("notes"),
        "thumb": r.get("thumb"), "duplicates": json.dumps(dups.get(r["id"], []), ensure_ascii=False),
        "tagged": int(bool(t)),
        # webm side-data alpha can't be decoded by this ffmpeg build -> hidden from the finder until converted

        "favorite": int(r["id"] in favorites),

    if r.get("text"):

        row["id"], row["title"], row["description"] or "", " ".join(t.get("tags") or []),

def build_overlays(ctx: Ctx, spans) -> tuple[list[list], list[str], str, list[dict]]:
    W, H, FPS = ctx.W, ctx.H, ctx.FPS
    inputs, chains, overlay_audio = [], [], []
    cur = "[0:v]"
    for k, ev in enumerate(ctx.edl.get("overlays", [])):
        label = f"overlay[{k}] {ev.get('asset') or ev.get('file')}"
        at = resolve_time(ev, spans, ctx.warnings, label)
        if at is None:
            continue
        if ev.get("template"):
            ev = {**ev, "file": str(motion_file(ctx, ev)), "placement": ev.get("placement", "fullscreen"),
                  "key_mode": "alpha", "audio": False}
            ev.setdefault("dur", motion_duration(ev["template"], ev.get("vars")))
        a = ctx.asset(ev["asset"]) if ev.get("asset") else {}
        path = ctx.media_path(ev)
        typ = ev["type"]
        mode = ev.get("key_mode", a.get("key_mode"))
        if mode == "alpha" and path.suffix.lower() == ".webm":
            ctx.warnings.append(f"{label}: webm side-data alpha can't be decoded by this ffmpeg build; "
                                "convert once with `mcs prep-alpha` or use a ProRes/PNG version")
        src_in = ev.get("in", a.get("use_in") or 0.0)
        if typ == "image":
            dur = ev.get("dur", 1.2)
        else:
            dur = ev.get("dur") or ((ev.get("out") or a.get("use_out") or a.get("duration_s") or 2.0) - src_in)
        if typ == "transition":
            cover = ev.get("cover_s", dur / 2)
            at = max(0.0, at - cover)
        if typ == "image":
            # Looped-image *inputs* stall ffmpeg 9's scheduler once they hit EOF before the main stream,
            # so stills/GIFs come in through the movie= source filter instead (staged to a short
            # relative path to dodge filtergraph escaping of Windows paths).
            stage = ctx.work / "stage"
            stage.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            staged = stage / f"img{k:03d}{path.suffix.lower()}"
            if not staged.exists() or staged.stat().st_size != path.stat().st_size:
                shutil.copyfile(path, staged)
            src_pad = f"movie=stage/{staged.name}:loop=0,setpts=N/{FPS}/TB,trim=duration={dur:.3f},"
        else:
            n = len(inputs) + 1
            inputs.append(["-ss", f"{src_in:.3f}", "-t", f"{dur:.3f}", "-i", path])
            src_pad = f"[{n}:v]setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,"
        placement = ev.get("placement") or a.get("placement") or "overlay_center"
        if typ == "transition" or placement == "fullscreen":
            size = f"scale={W}:{H}"
            x, y = "0", "0"
        else:
            sc = ev.get("scale", 0.45 if typ != "image" else 0.3)
            hpx = int(H * sc) // 2 * 2
            if ev.get("anim", "pop" if typ == "image" else None) == "pop":
                size = f"scale=w=-2:h='trunc({hpx}*{POP}/2)*2':eval=frame"
            else:
                size = f"scale=-2:{hpx}"
            cx, cy = ev.get("x", 0.5), ev.get("y", 0.5)
            x = f"{W * cx:.1f}-overlay_w/2"
            y = f"{H * cy:.1f}-overlay_h/2"
        flip = ",hflip" if ev.get("flip") else ""
        rot = f",rotate={ev['rotate']}*PI/180:c=none:ow=rotw(iw):oh=roth(ih)" if ev.get("rotate") else ""
        kf = key_filter(mode, a.get("key_color") if ev.get("key_color") is None else ev["key_color"], ev)
        op = f",colorchannelmixer=aa={ev['opacity']}" if "opacity" in ev else ""
        chains.append(f"{src_pad}fps={FPS},{kf},{size}{flip}{rot}{op},"
                      f"setpts=PTS+{at:.4f}/TB[ov{k}]")
        nxt = f"[v{k}]"
        chains.append(f"{cur}[ov{k}]overlay=x='{x}':y='{y}':enable='between(t,{at:.4f},{at + dur:.4f})':"
                      f"eof_action=pass{nxt}")
        cur = nxt
        if typ != "image" and ev.get("audio", True) and a.get("has_audio", 1):
            vol = ctx.matched_db(a, ctx.style["audio"]["mix"]["overlay_rel_db"],
                                 ctx.style["audio"]["sfx_db"] + (a.get("volume_db") or 0)) + ev.get("volume_db", 0)
            overlay_audio.append({"path": path, "at": at, "in": src_in, "dur": dur, "vol": vol})
    cur = avatar_overlays(ctx, spans, cur, chains)
    return inputs, chains, cur, overlay_audio

def render(slug: str, preview: bool = False, record: bool = True) -> Path:

content.text:
I added a **Brand library** to the studio UI. It's in the sidebar as **◆ Brand library** at `http://localhost:8765/#/brandlib`, and the server has been restarted, so it's live now.

**What's on the page:**
- **Header:** the main Crodie logo and your colour swatches. Click a swatch to copy its hex code.
- **Seven tabs:**
  - Emotes (56)
  - Characters (35)
  - Logos & icons (37)
  - CTA banners (12)
  - Stream overlays (29)
  - Narrator avatar (the 5 mood faces plus every talking state)
  - Channel art (your original banners, profile pic and sheets)
- **Search and favourites:** search by name or moment ("cry", "gg", "death") and filter to your favourites.
- **On every sticker card:**
  - **★ Favourite**: the auto-editor prefers starred stickers.
  - **▶ Animate**: renders the actual pop, slide or stamp animation in about 10 seconds.
  - **⧉ EDL**: copies a ready-made overlay snippet for an edit.
  - **⤓**: downloads the PNG.
- **Emotes** have an "avatar…" menu to set any emote as the narrator's face for a mood. The avatar rebuilds right away.
- **Logos** have a "use as…" menu to make any logo the watermark, main logo, icon or badge.

**What I tested:** the page loads all tabs with no broken images. I clicked Animate on the crying emote, and the preview rendered with Crodie popping in correctly. Starring a sticker saves and shows up as a favourite. I didn't click through the avatar and logo menus.

**Also done since last time:**
- **Animated sticker:** the sticker animation (pop for emotes, slide for banners, stamp for GG/W/L badges) is finished.
- **Stray bits removed:** the stray gem under the shocked emote and similar leftovers on four other stickers are gone.
- **Editing skill:** it now explains how to place Crodie stickers in an edit.

The test edit I promised isn't rendered yet; that's the next step.

p = r"C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\mcstudio\autoplan.py"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
i = s.index("    def sticker_beat(")
j = s.index("    def motion_beat(")
s = s[:i] + '''    def sticker_beat(self, b: dict, s: dict, overlays: list, busy: bool, duration: float) -> None:
        """The channel mascot reacts: a Crodie emote pops in a corner on a big beat (crying on a death, screaming
        on a jumpscare, heart eyes on loot). Sparse: strong beats only, >=25 s apart, ~1 per 40 s, never on a beat
        that already got a meme / green screen / game-UI graphic. A death screen is the payoff: it always gets the
        crying reaction, and the panic right before it stays clean so the two don't stack."""
        if busy or b["score"] < 4 or b["moment"] not in self.STICKER_MOMENTS:
            return
        deaths = [d["t"] for d in self.sig.get("death_screens", [])]
        if not b.get("death_screen") and any(0 < d - b["t"] < 15 for d in deaths):
            return                                       # leave the build-up clean for the death payoff
        ts = self.mg_used.setdefault("sticker_pop", [])
        if not b.get("death_screen") and (len(ts) >= max(1, min(5, int(duration / 40)))
                                          or any(abs(b["t"] - t) < 25 for t in ts)):
            return
        q = A.Query(moments=[b["moment"]], roles=["emotes"], categories=["brand_sticker"], project=self.slug,
                    exclude=self.used, limit=8, seed=self.rng.randint(0, 10 ** 6))
        res = [a for a in A.find(q) if b["moment"] in (a.get("moments") or [])]
        made_for = [a for a in res if a["moments"][0] == b["moment"]]   # emotes drawn FOR this moment first
        pool = (made_for or res)[:3]
        if not pool:
            return
        a = pool[0] if len(pool) == 1 or self.rng.random() < 0.6 else self.rng.choice(pool)
        self.used.append(a["id"])
        ts.append(b["t"])
        badge = a["id"].startswith("crodie.badge_")
        at = b["t"] + 0.6 if b.get("death_screen") else b["end"] + 0.1
        overlays.append({"type": "motion", "template": "sticker_pop", "seg": s["id"], "src_at": round(at, 3),
                         "vars": {"image": a["path"],                     # studio-relative (brand/crodie/...)
                                  "position": "center" if badge else ("top-right" if len(ts) % 2 else "top-left"),
                                  "style": "stamp" if badge else "pop"},
                         **({"dur": 2.2} if b.get("death_screen") else {})})

''' + s[j:]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
print("ok")
