"""Batch demo videos: the same test recording edited in every mode + a motion-graphics / Crodie sticker reel.

    uv run python demos.py [names...]        # default: all; renders 1080p60 finals one after another

Each mode demo is a fresh project cloned from projects/auto-dig (same sources, transcript, signals), auto-planned
with that base mode, rendered to projects/<slug>/out/<slug>.mp4 and copied to ../Demos/.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

STUDIO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PROJ = STUDIO / "projects"
DEMOS = STUDIO.parent / "Demos"
BASE = "auto-dig"

MODES = {
    "demo-crodie-narration": ("narration", "Crodie narrates: I dug to bedrock"),
    "demo-crodie-scary": ("scary", "Scary mode: the cave that got me"),
    "demo-crodie-hype": ("exciting", "Hype mode: digging to bedrock"),
    "demo-crodie-sad": ("sad", "Sad mode: I just wanted diamonds"),
    "demo-crodie-pov": ("pov", "POV: you dig straight down"),
    "demo-crodie-angry": ("angry", "Rage mode: this game hates me"),
}


def sh(*args: str) -> None:
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "mcstudio.cli", *args], cwd=STUDIO, check=True)


def clone(slug: str, title: str) -> Path:
    src, dst = PROJ / BASE, PROJ / slug
    (dst / "work").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pj = json.loads((src / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    pj.update({"slug": slug, "title": title})
    (dst / "project.json").write_text(json.dumps(pj, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    for f in ("transcript.json", "transcript.md", "signals.json", "signals.md", "levels.json"):
        if (src / "work" / f).exists():
            shutil.copyfile(src / "work" / f, dst / "work" / f)
    return dst


def mode_demo(slug: str) -> Path:
    mode, title = MODES[slug]
    clone(slug, title)
    sh("autoplan", slug, "--mode", mode)
    sh("render", slug)
    return PROJ / slug / "out" / f"{slug}.mp4"


def motion_reel(slug: str = "demo-crodie-motion-reel") -> Path:
    """Every motion template + a handful of Crodie stickers, one after another over gameplay, labelled."""
    sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDIO))
    from mcstudio import motion as M
    d = clone(slug, "Crodie motion graphics library")
    pj = json.loads((d / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    total = pj.get("duration_s") or 140
    items = []
    for t in M.list_templates():
        if t["name"] in ("sticker_pop", "end_screen"):
            continue
        dur = min(float(t.get("duration", 2.5)), 4.0)
        items.append({"type": "motion", "template": t["name"], "vars": {}, "dur": dur, "label": t["name"]})
    for img, style, pos in [("emotes/crying_waterfall.png", "pop", "top-right"),
                            ("emotes/screaming_panic.png", "pop", "top-left"),
                            ("emotes/heart_eyes.png", "pop", "top-right"),
                            ("emotes/badge_gg.png", "stamp", "center"),
                            ("emotes/badge_w.png", "stamp", "center"),
                            ("cta/cta_subscribe.png", "slide", "bottom-left"),
                            ("cta/cta_like.png", "slide", "bottom-right")]:
        items.append({"type": "motion", "template": "sticker_pop", "dur": 1.8, "label": "crodie sticker",
                      "vars": {"image": f"brand/crodie/{img}", "style": style, "position": pos}})
    gap = 0.4
    length = sum(i["dur"] + gap for i in items) + 1.0
    start = 20.0 if total > length + 25 else 0.0
    segs = [{"id": "reel", "type": "source", "in": start, "out": round(start + length, 2)}]
    overlays, texts, t = [], [], 0.5
    for i in items:
        label = i.pop("label")
        overlays.append({**i, "at": round(t, 2)})
        texts.append({"text": label.replace("_", " ").upper(), "at": round(t, 2), "dur": i["dur"],
                      "style": "label", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.94})
        t += i["dur"] + gap
    edl = {"version": 1, "project": slug, "title": "Motion graphics library", "mode": "funny",
           "segments": segs, "overlays": overlays, "text": texts,
           "audio": {"sfx": [], "bleeps": [], "music": []},
           "captions": {"enabled": False}}
    b = json.loads((STUDIO / "brand" / "brand.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if b.get("watermark", {}).get("image"):
        edl["watermark"] = {"image": b["watermark"]["image"], "opacity": b["watermark"].get("opacity", 0.85)}
    (d / "edit.json").write_text(json.dumps(edl, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    sh("render", slug)
    return d / "out" / f"{slug}.mp4"


def main():
    names = sys.argv[1:] or [*MODES, "demo-crodie-motion-reel"]
    DEMOS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for n in names:
        try:
            out = motion_reel(n) if n == "demo-crodie-motion-reel" else mode_demo(n)
            shutil.copyfile(out, DEMOS / out.name)
            print(f"[demo] {n} -> {DEMOS / out.name}", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep going with the other demos
            print(f"[demo] {n} FAILED: {e}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            continue

    return ";\n".join(out)

        ks = [int(x) for x in a[4:].split(",")]
        fc = FC
        for k in ks:
            fc = drop(fc, k)
        run(a, fc)

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

def run(name, fc, out=("-f", "null", "-"), extra=(), timeout=240):

    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-v", "error", "-y"]

            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-r", "60", "-c:a", "aac", *extra, "-t", "105.74", *out]
    t = time.time()
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=W, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        print(f"{name}: exit {r.returncode} in {time.time() - t:.0f}s {r.stderr[-300:]}", flush=True)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/F", "/IM", "ffmpeg.exe"], capture_output=True)
        print(f"{name}: HANG (>{timeout}s)", flush=True)


def drop(fc, k):
    """Replace overlay k with a passthrough."""
    lines = fc.strip().split(";\n")
    out = []
    for ln in lines:
        if re.match(rf"^\[{k + 1}:v\]", ln):
            out.append(f"[{k + 1}:v]nullsink")
            continue
        m = re.match(rf"^(\[[^\]]+\])\[ov{k}\]overlay=.*(\[v{k}\])$", ln)
        if m:
            out.append(f"{m.group(1)}null{m.group(2)}")
            continue
        out.append(ln)
    return ";\n".join(out)

Build 6 new Crodie-branded HyperFrames motion-graphics templates for the Minecraft YouTube channel "Crodie" studio at `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\motion\`. Another agent is building a different set in parallel — only create folders with the names below; do not edit motion.py, shared/, or any other template (except adding your rows to `studio/motion/README.md` at the very end).

Context to read first:
- `studio/motion/README.md`, and 3 existing templates as reference for conventions: `sticker_pop` (uses an image var — study exactly how it loads a data-URI image, sizes by aspect, and handles vertical safe zones), `lower_third`, `title_card`. Also `studio/motion/shared/`.
- `mcstudio/motion.py`: `resolve_vars` inlines any image var whose value is a local path (absolute, studio-relative like `brand/crodie/emotes/x.png`, or channel-relative) into a data: URI, so image vars can DEFAULT to studio-relative brand paths. `build(name)` generates landscape/ + vertical/ projects; `render(name, vars, orientation, preview=True)` renders ProRes 4444 alpha .mov to motion/cache.
- Brand: `studio/brand/brand.json` (CRODIE; colours lime #92AE22, leaf #437420, orange #EF7718 (key "gold"), cream #FCDFB5, olive #313B20, ink, paper; fonts Minecraft Ten / Luckiest Guy / Minecraft). Brand art (transparent PNGs): `studio/brand/crodie/stickers.json` lists all 169 (emotes/, characters/, logos/, overlays/, cta/). Look at a few with the Read tool to know what they look like. Useful ones: logos/logo_grass_main.png, logos/icon_c_grass_orange.png, logos/badge_wood_crown.png, logos/badge_wood.png, characters/char_reach_closeup.png, char_jump_cheer.png, char_peek_pillar.png, char_head_smile.png, char_head_shocked.png, emotes/*, cta/cta_subscribe.png, cta/cta_like.png, cta/cta_notifications.png, overlays/frame_facecam_wave.png.
- The source art is ~150-650px; avoid scaling stickers beyond ~1.8x their native size in full 1080p renders (they get soft) — design layouts accordingly.

Templates to build (each landscape + vertical, transparent, first & last frame fully transparent, `opaque` var like the others, sensible vertical safe zones: clear of top ~10% and bottom ~26%):
1. `crodie_intro` (~2.5s): channel logo sting — Crodie (char_reach_closeup) bursts up from the bottom, the grass-block CRODIE logo slams in with a block-dust burst and screen shake, small sparkles, exits. Vars: `logo` (image, default logo_grass_main), `mascot` (image), `tagline` (text, default brand tagline, "" = none).
2. `crodie_subscribe` (~3.5s): Crodie CTA — the cta_subscribe banner slides in, a Minecraft-style cursor clicks it (button press squash, banner swaps to a "SUBSCRIBED ✓" state drawn in CSS over it or a tint), a bell (cta_notifications or CSS pixel bell) rings, Crodie emote (thumbs_up) pops beside. Vars: `banner` (image), `emote` (image), `done_text`.
3. `crodie_peek` (~2.5s, stretchable): Crodie peeks in from a screen edge (char_peek_pillar or emotes/peek_grass_block), wiggles, ducks back. Vars: `image`, `side` (left|right|bottom), `text` (optional speech-bubble text, "" = none, e.g. "psst...").
4. `crodie_lower_third` (~3.5s, stretchable): name/info lower third on a wooden sign (badge_wood or a CSS wood plank in the brand style) with Crodie's head (char_head_smile) popping on the left, title + subtitle text. Vars: `title`, `subtitle`, `head` (image).
5. `crodie_chapter` (~2.2s): chapter card — wooden sign drops in on two chains/vines, "CHAPTER 2" small + big chapter name, a Crodie emote peeks over the sign's top edge. Vars: `chapter`, `name`, `emote` (image).
6. `crodie_reacts` (~2.5s, stretchable): "CRODIE REACTS" corner reaction cam — the frame_facecam_wave frame (or a CSS vine frame) pops in at a corner holding a Crodie emote that changes/bounces, with a small label. Vars: `emote` (image, default emotes/screaming_panic), `label` (default "CRODIE:"), `position` (corner).

For each: `npx hyperframes check` passes (0 errors) for both generated projects; render previews (preview=True) in both orientations; extract mid-animation frames composited over gray AND over a gameplay frame (e.g. any frame from `studio/projects/auto-dig/work/full/base.mkv` via ffmpeg -ss 30) and LOOK at them (Read the PNGs) — fix layout/sharpness/timing issues you see; verify first/last frame alpha 0. Don't run full 60fps renders except one spot-check. CPU is shared with other render jobs: render sequentially, not in parallel.
Finally add table rows + brief behaviour notes for your 6 templates to `studio/motion/README.md`, and report: template names, durations, vars + defaults, anything the caller must know.

def stage_clip(ctx: Ctx, path: Path, src_in: float, dur: float, fps: int) -> Path:
    """Cut an overlay clip's used window to a clean, video-only, constant-fps lossless file (cached).

    Feeding pack clips straight in with -ss/-t made ffmpeg 9 hang at the very end of the final pass for some
    files (24 fps clips with a non-zero start time, e.g. 'Patrick Stewart Epic Facepalm', the anime speed
    lines): every frame got written, the mp4 was never finalised. Pre-cut inputs avoid it, and the final pass
    gets cheaper. ProRes/alpha sources stay ProRes 4444 so their alpha survives."""
    import hashlib as _h
    st = path.stat()
    key = _h.sha1(f"{path}|{st.st_mtime_ns}|{st.st_size}|{src_in:.3f}|{dur:.3f}|{fps}".encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    alpha = path.suffix.lower() == ".mov"
    out = ctx.work / "stage" / f"clip_{key}.{'mov' if alpha else 'mkv'}"
    if not out.exists():
        out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        codec = ["-c:v", "prores_ks", "-profile:v", "4444", "-pix_fmt", "yuva444p10le"] if alpha \
            else ["-c:v", "ffv1", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p"]
        tmp = out.with_name(out.stem + ".tmp" + out.suffix)
        run_ff(["-ss", f"{src_in:.3f}", "-t", f"{dur:.3f}", "-i", path, "-an", "-sn", "-dn",
                "-vf", f"fps={fps},setpts=PTS-STARTPTS", *codec, tmp], ctx.work, ctx.log)
        os.replace(tmp, out)
    return out

    uv run python demos.py [names...]        # default: all; renders 1080p60 finals one after another

Each mode demo is a fresh project cloned from projects/auto-dig (same sources, transcript, signals), auto-planned
with that base mode, rendered to projects/<slug>/out/<slug>.mp4 and copied to ../Demos/.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

STUDIO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PROJ = STUDIO / "projects"
DEMOS = STUDIO.parent / "Demos"
BASE = "auto-dig"

MODES = {
    "demo-crodie-narration": ("narration", "Crodie narrates: I dug to bedrock"),
    "demo-crodie-scary": ("scary", "Scary mode: the cave that got me"),
    "demo-crodie-hype": ("exciting", "Hype mode: digging to bedrock"),
    "demo-crodie-sad": ("sad", "Sad mode: I just wanted diamonds"),
    "demo-crodie-pov": ("pov", "POV: you dig straight down"),
    "demo-crodie-angry": ("angry", "Rage mode: this game hates me"),
}


def sh(*args: str) -> None:
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "mcstudio.cli", *args], cwd=STUDIO, check=True)


def clone(slug: str, title: str) -> Path:
    src, dst = PROJ / BASE, PROJ / slug
    (dst / "work").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pj = json.loads((src / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    pj.update({"slug": slug, "title": title})
    (dst / "project.json").write_text(json.dumps(pj, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    for f in ("transcript.json", "transcript.md", "signals.json", "signals.md", "levels.json"):
        if (src / "work" / f).exists():
            shutil.copyfile(src / "work" / f, dst / "work" / f)
    return dst


def mode_demo(slug: str) -> Path:
    mode, title = MODES[slug]
    clone(slug, title)
    sh("autoplan", slug, "--mode", mode)
    sh("render", slug)
    return PROJ / slug / "out" / f"{slug}.mp4"


def motion_reel(slug: str = "demo-crodie-motion-reel") -> Path:
    """Every motion template + a handful of Crodie stickers, one after another over gameplay, labelled."""
    sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDIO))
    from mcstudio import motion as M
    d = clone(slug, "Crodie motion graphics library")
    pj = json.loads((d / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    total = pj.get("duration_s") or 140
    items = []
    for t in M.list_templates():
        if t["name"] in ("sticker_pop", "end_screen"):
            continue
        dur = min(float(t.get("duration", 2.5)), 4.0)
        items.append({"type": "motion", "template": t["name"], "vars": {}, "dur": dur, "label": t["name"]})
    for img, style, pos in [("emotes/crying_waterfall.png", "pop", "top-right"),
                            ("emotes/screaming_panic.png", "pop", "top-left"),
                            ("emotes/heart_eyes.png", "pop", "top-right"),
                            ("emotes/badge_gg.png", "stamp", "center"),
                            ("emotes/badge_w.png", "stamp", "center"),
                            ("cta/cta_subscribe.png", "slide", "bottom-left"),
                            ("cta/cta_like.png", "slide", "bottom-right")]:
        items.append({"type": "motion", "template": "sticker_pop", "dur": 1.8, "label": "crodie sticker",
                      "vars": {"image": f"brand/crodie/{img}", "style": style, "position": pos}})
    gap = 0.4
    length = sum(i["dur"] + gap for i in items) + 1.0
    start = 20.0 if total > length + 25 else 0.0
    segs = [{"id": "reel", "type": "source", "in": start, "out": round(start + length, 2)}]
    overlays, texts, t = [], [], 0.5
    for i in items:
        label = i.pop("label")
        overlays.append({**i, "at": round(t, 2)})
        texts.append({"text": label.replace("_", " ").upper(), "at": round(t, 2), "dur": i["dur"],
                      "style": "label", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.94})
        t += i["dur"] + gap
    edl = {"version": 1, "project": slug, "title": "Motion graphics library", "mode": "funny",
           "segments": segs, "overlays": overlays, "text": texts,
           "audio": {"sfx": [], "bleeps": [], "music": []},
           "captions": {"enabled": False}}
    b = json.loads((STUDIO / "brand" / "brand.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if b.get("watermark", {}).get("image"):
        edl["watermark"] = {"image": b["watermark"]["image"], "opacity": b["watermark"].get("opacity", 0.85)}
    (d / "edit.json").write_text(json.dumps(edl, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    sh("render", slug)
    return d / "out" / f"{slug}.mp4"


def main():
    names = sys.argv[1:] or [*MODES, "demo-crodie-motion-reel"]
    DEMOS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for n in names:
        try:
            out = motion_reel(n) if n == "demo-crodie-motion-reel" else mode_demo(n)
            shutil.copyfile(out, DEMOS / out.name)
            print(f"[demo] {n} -> {DEMOS / out.name}", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep going with the other demos
            print(f"[demo] {n} FAILED: {e}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

I've sent the corrected versions of the six mode demos, replacing the copies in `Demos/`. I checked a frame from the POV demo, and captions now stay off the title card. These re-renders also picked up the new Crodie subscribe prompt.

**Everything finished since your last messages:**
- **Green screens in the test edit:** smug emoji at 1:03, Eddy Wally's "wow" at 1:35, speed lines at 1:40. Every green screen now renders reliably.
- **Seven demos:** narration, scary, hype, sad, POV, rage, and the motion graphics reel.
- **12 new Crodie motion graphics**, taking the library to 41:
  - intro sting, subscribe click, peek-in, lower third, chapter card
  - "Crodie reacts" cam, wipe transition, W/L/GG verdict stamp
  - day counter, end card, thought bubble, loot reveal
- **Publishing workflow** (sidebar → Publishing):
  - A board with Editing, Awaiting upload, Uploaded, Scheduled and Published columns.
  - Each episode's Publish tab has a title (5 options), description with chapters, tags and hashtags.
  - It also has ChatGPT thumbnail prompts centred on Crodie, in 16:9 with text, without text, and a 9:16 Shorts cover.
  - Every field has a Copy button, plus a "Copy all".
  - Copy is ready for the bedrock episode and its 3 Shorts.

**Things to know:**
- The `claude` command isn't installed on this PC, so the publishing copy comes from a rule-based writer. It reads well, but install Claude Code's CLI and the Regenerate button will use it instead.
- The board tracks status only; it doesn't upload to YouTube for you. You upload in YouTube Studio, then move the card or paste the link, and it moves to Scheduled or Published on its own.
- The publishing check flagged the bedrock episode's background music as "unknown licence". It's a possible Content ID claim, so swap it before you upload.
- The test edit (`auto-dig.mp4`) still has the caption-over-title overlap, because I hand-placed its green screens rather than re-running the auto-editor. I can patch that and re-render it whenever you like.

]

]

(dst/"edit.json").write_text(json.dumps(edl,indent=2),encoding="utf-8")

input.prompt:
Add a complete, central **feature settings system with on/off toggles** to the "MC Studio" automated Minecraft editing app for the channel Crodie, at `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\` (Python package `mcstudio`; FastAPI `mcstudio/server.py`; vanilla-JS UI `ui/index.html`, `ui/app.js`, `ui/style.css`; run Python with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe` from `studio/`). Read `../CLAUDE.md`, `../.claude/skills/mc-edit/SKILL.md` and `references/edl.md` first. The UI server on :8765 is managed by the parent session — don't start/stop it; tell the parent to restart it.

The creator asked (verbatim): "I want you to expand the ui with all of the features that we have added with the ability to turn certain things off, for example if i want to turn off filters, all filters, specific filters, etc. for all settings"

## 1. Inventory every feature
Read `mcstudio/autoplan.py` (Planner.plan, LEXICON/TREAT, cold open, title_card, crodie_subscribe CTA, time_card, running_gags counters, meme cutaways, green screens, motion_beat (advancement_toast / location_tag / boss_bar), sticker_beat (Crodie emote sticker_pop), engage() zooms, music(), modes/assign_modes, brighten, speed montage, freeze frames, shakes, text pops, caption_hides, watermark), `mcstudio/render.py` (looks/colour grades via `looks.json` + per-mode looks in `modes.json`, brighten effect, zoom/shake, guard_cuts cut guard + fades, avatar_overlays narrator avatar, watermark logo bug, overlay audio, SFX bus/ducking/speech gate, loudness), `mcstudio/captions.py` (captions, emphasis words, POV header, text pops), `mcstudio/shorts.py` (hook banner, short windows), `mcstudio/scaffold.py` (dead-air removal), `style.json`, `modes.json`, `looks.json`, `brand/brand.json`, `studio/motion/templates/*/template.json` (41 templates). Build the settings around what actually exists in code — don't invent features that aren't implemented.

## 2. Settings model — `studio/settings.json` + `mcstudio/settings.py`
- One JSON with sensible defaults = current behaviour (nothing changes unless the user toggles). Grouped sections, e.g.:
  - `looks`: `enabled` (master: all filters/colour grading off → neutral), `default_look`, `allowed` per look (clean/vivid/warm/cool/cinematic/shader/…; disabled looks are never applied — fall back to `none`/clean), `mode_looks` (let moods change the grade), `brighten_dark` (auto-brighten caves), `intensity` (0–1 multiplier if the grade code can scale it cleanly; skip if not feasible).
  - `modes`: `auto_story_modes` on/off, per-mode allowed (scary/sad/… ; disabled → base mode).
  - `captions`: enabled, emphasis colours on/off, POV header, text pops (impact/minecraft text), running-gag counters ("STICKS x3").
  - `audio`: sfx enabled, per-role toggles (hit, whoosh, riser, voice_line, reaction, laugh, stinger, ui, literal, ambience…), sfx volume offset dB, max SFX per minute, music beds on/off + music volume offset, overlay (meme/green screen) audio on/off, bleeps on/off, ducking/speech gate.
  - `memes`: meme cutaways on/off + max per minute; green screens on/off + max per minute + allowed placements; favourites-only option (finder has `favorites_only`).
  - `camera`: beat zooms, engagement zooms (`engage`), shakes, freeze frames, speed montage (x4 speed), cold open.
  - `motion`: title card, time card, subscribe CTA, game-UI graphics (advancement_toast, location_tag, boss_bar individually), Crodie sticker reactions, plus a per-template `disabled` list (any of the 41 templates can be blocked from auto use AND from render — render skips a disabled template overlay with a warning).
  - `brand`: watermark on/off, narrator avatar on/off (narration mode), mascot stickers on/off.
  - `editing`: cut guard (never clip words) on/off, dead-air removal, cut fades.
  - `shorts`: hook banner, number of shorts, min/max length (whatever shorts.py takes).
- `settings.py`: `load(slug=None)` deep-merges defaults ← `settings.json` ← per-episode overrides in `projects/<slug>/settings.json` (only changed keys stored; value `null` = inherit). `save_global(patch)`, `save_project(slug, patch)`. A schema/metadata structure describing every setting (label, help text, type: bool/number/select/multi, min/max/step, options, section, `applies`: "plan" | "render" | "both") that the UI renders generically — so adding a setting later = one schema entry.
## 3. Wire it in (so toggles really work)
- **Plan-time** (autoplan, engage, music, shorts, scaffold): skip placing disabled things; respect caps.
- **Render-time kill switches** (render.py / captions.py) so toggles also apply to EXISTING edit.json files without re-planning: looks master off / disallowed looks → neutral grade; brighten off; captions off; text pops off; sfx off / per-role off / volume offset; music off; overlay audio off; watermark off; avatar off; zoom/shake off; disabled templates skipped; meme cutaways / green screens off (skip those segments/overlays cleanly — cutaway segments must be removed from the timeline without breaking span math, so do that at EDL-load time before build_spans, with a warning in render_report); cut guard off.
  Make render-cache keys include the relevant settings (segments are cached by hash + RENDER_VERSION — if a look/zoom setting changes a segment's pixels, it must change the segment hash; check how the hash is built in render.py).
- Add CLI: `mcs settings show [--slug]`, `mcs settings set <dotted.key> <value> [--slug]`.
- Another session may edit `autoplan.py`/`render.py` lightly; keep your changes surgical and clearly marked, re-read files right before editing.

## 4. UI
- New sidebar page **"Settings"** (#/settings) placed near Brand & modes: sections as collapsible cards with a master toggle per section (e.g. "Filters & colour" master switch greys out its children), toggle switches (styled checkbox switches), sliders with live value, selects, multi-select chip lists (looks, modes, SFX roles, the 41 motion templates with their preview poster thumbnails from `/api/motion` and a search box), help text per setting, an "applies at: plan / render" badge, "Reset section to defaults" and "Reset all", autosave (debounced PATCH) with a toast, and a search bar that filters settings across sections.
- Episode page: a **"Settings"** tab showing the same schema in override mode: each control has a tri-state (Inherit · On · Off / or a custom value) with the inherited global value shown faintly; "Re-plan with these settings" (runs autoplan job) and "Re-render preview" buttons (use existing job endpoints/patterns in server.py — check what exists for autoplan/render jobs).
- Endpoints: `GET /api/settings/schema`, `GET/PATCH /api/settings`, `GET/PATCH /api/projects/{slug}/settings`, `POST /api/settings/reset` (section optional).
- Match existing UI style/helpers (`api`, `toast`, `esc`, `$`, `$$`, `view`, `store`, `pollers`, `[hidden]` rule, `.card`, `.chip`, `.btn`). `node --check ui/app.js` must pass.

## 5. Verify
- Unit-ish checks with the FastAPI TestClient for the endpoints.
- Prove toggles work end to end on the existing project `auto-dig` WITHOUT overwriting its edit.json (it has hand-placed green screens): copy it to a scratch project `settings-test` (copy project.json + work/transcript.json, signals.json, levels.json + edit.json), set overrides there (e.g. looks off, sfx off, captions off, watermark off, one template disabled), run `mcs render settings-test --preview`, extract frames / check audio (e.g. ffmpeg volumedetect or astats) to confirm each switch took effect, then reset. Also run `mcs autoplan settings-test` with e.g. stickers + green screens + memes disabled and confirm the plan has none.
- Report: settings list (sections + keys), files changed, endpoints, what is plan-time vs render-time, and anything that couldn't be made toggleable and why.

content.text:
Not literally. I can't retrain myself on videos, but I can study them and turn what I find into rules the auto-editor follows. In practice that gets you most of what "training" would.

**What studying a video would look like** (a `mcs learn <video>` command):

1. **Measure the editing.** From each reference video I'd pull hard numbers:
   - shot length and cuts per minute
   - how often the frame zooms or punches in, and how hard
   - sound effects per minute and how loud they sit under the voice
   - how often meme cutaways and green screens appear, and how long they last
   - caption style: words on screen at once, colours, position
   - music changes and how fast the cold open hooks
   
   The tools for most of this are already in the project.
2. **Look at it.** I'd pull frames at every edit point and review them myself, the same way I check our renders. That way I learn the patterns, not just the numbers: what they do on a death, how they set up a punchline, when they hold a moment with no effects.
3. **Line edits up with speech.** Matching the transcript to the edit points shows when they cut relative to the joke, such as SFX right after the punchline word or a zoom on stressed words.
4. **Save a style profile.** You could pick it in Settings (e.g. "fast-paced like Channel X", "calm storytelling"), and it would retune the auto-editor's pacing, densities and rules.

**Learning from you** is the most valuable part. If you fix one of my edits in the timeline, I can compare it with what I made: what you cut, moved, made quieter or deleted. Those differences then update your channel's own style. Your feedback on SFX volume, clipped words and overused filters already works this way; this would make it automatic.

**Limits:**
- You'd need to give me the video files; I shouldn't download from YouTube for you.
- Videos are only studied, never reused in your edits.
- It learns style and pacing, not taste. It still won't know why something is funny the way a person does, which is why your feedback stays in the loop.

Want me to build it? If so, which 2–3 creators' videos would you want me to learn from? Start with a few you'd like Crodie's edits to feel like.

content.text:
The Settings page is live in the UI (sidebar → **Settings**). I restarted the server, checked the page loads, and switched filters off and back on through it; it saved both ways. Everything is at defaults, so nothing changes until you flip something.

It has 10 sections, each with its own on/off switches:
- **Filters & colour** (master switch): all filters off in one click, or block specific looks (vivid, warm, cinematic…). There's also a filter strength slider, whether moods change the colour, cave auto-brighten, and each effect (flash, black-and-white, deep-fry, vignette…).
- **Moods:** the automatic scary and sad sections on or off, and any single mood blocked.
- **Captions:** captions, emphasis colours, text pops, the "STICKS ×3" counters, the POV header, "x4 SPEED" labels.
- **Audio:** all sound effects or each of the 11 types separately (hits, whooshes, stingers…), SFX volume, SFX per minute, music and its volume, meme and green-screen audio, bleeps, ducking.
- **Memes & green screens:** each on or off, how many per minute, corner or fullscreen, favourites only.
- **Camera:** beat zooms, engagement zooms, zoom strength, shakes, freeze frames, speed-ups, cold open.
- **Motion graphics** (master switch): title card, subscribe prompt, time card, achievement toast, location tag, boss bar. Each of the 40 templates can be blocked from a searchable grid with preview pictures.
- **Brand:** watermark, Crodie narrator, Crodie sticker reactions.
- **Editing:** the cut guard that keeps words from being clipped, cut fades, dead-air removal, longest pause kept.
- **Shorts:** on or off, how many, min and max length, hook banner.

Every episode also has a **Settings tab**. Each option there can follow the global setting or be forced on or off for that episode alone, and there are buttons to re-plan and re-render a preview with those choices.

**When changes apply:**
- Turning things off (filters, SFX, captions, watermark, memes, zooms, specific templates) applies straight to existing edits on the next render.
- Caps, favourites-only, mood sections and speed-ups need a re-plan.
- Each setting shows a small "plan" or "render" badge so you can tell which is which.

The agent tested each switch on a copy of the bedrock episode. For example, with filters, sound effects, captions, watermark, title card and memes all off, the render came out exactly as expected, and your real episode wasn't touched. That copy is still on your Episodes list as **settings-test** if you want to try the switches yourself; tell me if you'd like it removed.

The video-learning feature from your last question is still yours to decide: tell me which 2–3 creators' videos you'd like me to study and I'll build it.

- hyperframes: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.
- hyperframes-audio: Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), or automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter. Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.
- hyperframes-cli: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.
- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.
- hyperframes-creative: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.
- hyperframes-keyframes: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
- hyperframes-registry: Install, discover, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).
- media-use: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal.
- motion-graphics: A short, design-led motion graphic where motion is the message — kinetic typography, stat count-up, chart/data-viz hit, logo sting / brand lockup, lower-third / callout / social overlay, animated map (highlight regions, connect places, zoom to a location), animated tweet / news-article / headline, webpage / UI animation (scroll, cursor, callouts), or fusing a real image's geometry into a chart. Usually under 10s (up to ~30s), no narration or live-action subject; renders to MP4 or transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / multi-scene → /general-video. Unclear → /hyperframes.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: Always use this skill when the user wants to create a new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file. You MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call.
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. # Handoff: Creator Program sponsorship promo (game server hosting)

Paste this whole file into a new Claude Code session (desktop app, Code tab) as the first message.

---

## 1. The goal

Make a **30–40 second promotional video** for our **game server hosting website's creator program**. YouTubers drop it into their videos as a **sponsored segment**. It shows how easy our service is, from picking a game to managing a running server, and pushes viewers to use the **creator's code for a discount**.

It's built by **splicing my screen recordings and screenshots with custom motion graphics** in our brand identity.

## 2. Story / storyboard (target ~36 s at 60 fps)

| # | Time | Beat | Footage / graphic |
|---|------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | 0.0–2.5 | **Hook + logo sting.** Brand logo slams in, tagline ("Your server. Live in 60 seconds." or similar, confirm with me). | Custom motion graphic (logo sting) |
| 2 | 2.5–6.0 | **Pick a game.** Animated **collage / wall of game cover art** (all games we offer) scrolling or tiling, then one cover gets "selected" and zooms toward camera. | Custom motion graphic built from the cover images I supply |
| 3 | 6.0–9.5 | **Choose a server region.** | Screen recording/screenshot + animated map pin / region highlight callout |
| 4 | 9.5–13.5 | **Enter the creator code → discount.** Code typed into the field, price strikes through, discount badge pops ("-XX%"). **The code must be a variable** so each creator gets their own render. | Screen recording + motion overlay (typing, price strike, badge) |
| 5 | 13.5–16.5 | **Checkout / pay.** Quick, clean, no real card details visible. | Screen recording, blur/mask anything sensitive |
| 6 | 16.5–20.5 | **Watch it deploy.** Progress / console lines, then a "Server online ✓" moment. | Screen recording + motion graphic (progress ring / deploy stamp) |
| 7 | 20.5–24.0 | **Dashboard tour.** Glide across the game server dashboard. | Screen recording with smooth punch-ins / reframes |
| 8 | 24.0–26.5 | **Settings.** | Recording + callout labels |
| 9 | 26.5–29.0 | **One-click mod installs.** Click → installed badge. | Recording + click ripple + "1-click" callout |
| 10 | 29.0–31.5 | **Resource usage.** CPU/RAM graphs. | Recording + animated stat highlights |
| 11 | 31.5–34.0 | **One-click resource upgrade.** RAM bumps up, graph relaxes. | Recording + upgrade burst graphic |
| 12 | 34.0–38.0 | **CTA end card.** Logo, URL, "Use code **{CODE}** for **{XX}% off**", platform badges. | Custom motion graphic (end card) |

Pacing: fast and punchy, a cut or move every 1–3 s. Each beat gets one clear on-screen label ("Pick your game", "Choose a region", "Use code CRODIE", "Deploy in seconds", "1-click mods", "Upgrade instantly"). Keep text big enough to read on phones.

## 3. What I will supply

I'll put everything in one folder. Suggested: `Desktop\Server Promo\` with these subfolders:
- `brand/`: logo (SVG or transparent PNG preferred), brand colours, fonts (or font names), tagline if we have one
- `covers/`: game cover images for the collage, one file per game, named by game
- `recordings/`: screen recordings of each step (deploy flow, dashboard, settings, mods, resources, upgrade)
- `screenshots/`: stills for any step without a clean recording
- `audio/` (optional): music bed / SFX / voiceover if I have them

Ask me for anything missing:
- website URL
- discount % and example creator code
- tagline
- whether there's a voiceover
- which disclosure wording to use
- the target aspect ratios

## 4. Deliverables

1. **Master promo** 16:9, 1920×1080 @ 60 fps MP4 (H.264, AAC), ~36 s.
2. **Vertical cut** 9:16 1080×1920 for Shorts/TikTok creators (same beats, re-laid-out, not just cropped).
3. **Per-creator renders**: the creator code (and optionally creator name/handle) is a single variable. One command renders a new version per code, e.g. `render --code CRODIE --discount 20`.
4. **Transparent overlays** (ProRes 4444 .mov with alpha) of the key motion graphics: logo sting, code/discount badge, end card. Creators can place them over their own footage.
5. A **project folder + README** explaining how to re-render with new codes, swap footage, and change copy.
6. (Nice to have) a short "how to use this sponsorship" note for creators, and a still thumbnail/end-frame PNG.

## 5. Tools and approach that worked in the previous session (reuse them)

Machine:
- Windows 11.
- AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 / Radeon 890M. **No NVIDIA/CUDA, and Vulkan GPU compute paths failed**, so treat it as **CPU-only**.
- 31 GB RAM.
- **ffmpeg 9** on PATH, **Node 24**, **uv** (Python 3.12).
- Shells: PowerShell is primary, Git Bash is also available.

**Motion graphics: HyperFrames** (HTML → video, GSAP animations, seekable, deterministic):
- Start with the `hyperframes` skill. It routes to `/motion-graphics` for short brand graphics and `/general-video` for the full promo. Load `/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes` (punch-ins, reframes, camera moves on screen recordings), `/hyperframes-cli` and `/media-use` as needed.
- Render overlays as **ProRes 4444 `.mov` with alpha** (`--format mov`) and composite them in ffmpeg, or build the whole promo as one HyperFrames composition with the recordings as clips. Pick whichever keeps per-creator re-renders simplest.
- Always run `npx hyperframes check` (0 errors) on every composition.
- Render **previews** (540p/30) while iterating; render full 1080p60 only at the end. Full renders are CPU-heavy, so run them **one at a time**.
- **Images inside HyperFrames pages:** the render page is served over http, so local `C:\...` paths don't load. Inline them as `data:` URIs (or serve them from the project folder).
- Make the creator code / discount / URL **composition variables**, so per-creator renders are just a variable swap.
- Design rules that worked:
  - First and last frame fully transparent for overlays.
  - Vertical layouts keep clear of the top ~10% and bottom ~26%, where the platform UI sits.
  - Don't upscale raster art beyond ~1.8× native (it goes soft).
  - Pixel-snap text sizes.

**ffmpeg gotchas learned the hard way (ffmpeg 9 on this machine):**
- **Looped image inputs (`-loop 1 -i x.png`) deadlock ffmpeg 9's scheduler.** Bring stills in through the `movie=` source filter instead. For a static image held for the whole video, use a single frame plus `overlay=...:eof_action=repeat`, never `loop=0`.
- **Feeding clips straight in with `-ss/-t` can hang the final pass at the very end** (all frames written, mp4 never finalised). It happened with 24 fps clips that have a non-zero start time. Fix: **pre-cut each clip first** to a clean constant-fps intermediate (`-ss in -t dur -i src -an -vf fps=60,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS -c:v ffv1`, or ProRes 4444 for alpha), then use those.
- WebM VP8/VP9 alpha can't be decoded by this build. Use ProRes 4444 or PNG sequences for alpha.
- libass needs the font's *name-table family name* (e.g. "Pricedown Black"). Pass `fontsdir=`.
- Use `-/filter_complex <file>` for long filtergraphs. On Windows, copy media to short relative paths to avoid escaping issues.

**Verification habit (do it every time):**
- After each render, extract frames at every beat with `ffmpeg -ss <t> -i out.mp4 -frames:v 1 f.png` and actually look at them.
- Check text is readable, nothing sensitive is visible (card numbers, emails, IPs, passwords), overlays are aligned and the alpha is clean.
- Check the first and last frames.

**Working style:**
- Run independent pieces in parallel with sub-agents, e.g. one agent per motion graphic. Keep renders sequential.
- Keep edits reversible and the project re-renderable from source + a config file.

## 6. Custom motion graphics to design (brand identity from `brand/`)

1. **Logo sting** (2–2.5 s): logo build/slam, light particles or a server-rack/pixel motif, tagline.
2. **Game collage** (3–4 s): wall/grid/marquee of all covers with parallax and depth, a highlight sweep, then one cover selected and zoomed in. Must accept any number of covers.
3. **Region picker callout**: stylised world map with region pins and a selected-region pulse.
4. **Creator code + discount**: code typing into a field, a price strike-through, and a "-XX%" badge burst. The code, % and prices are variables.
5. **Deploy progress**: progress ring / console lines → "ONLINE ✓" stamp.

| 5 | 13.5–16.5 | **Checkout / pay.** Quick, clean, no real card details visible. | Screen recording, blur/mask anything sensitive |
| 6 | 16.5–20.5 | **Watch it deploy.** Progress / console lines, then a "Server online ✓" moment. | Screen recording + motion graphic (progress ring / deploy stamp) |
| 7 | 20.5–24.0 | **Dashboard tour.** Glide across the game server dashboard. | Screen recording with smooth punch-ins / reframes |
| 8 | 24.0–26.5 | **Settings.** | Recording + callout labels |
| 9 | 26.5–29.0 | **One-click mod installs.** Click → installed badge. | Recording + click ripple + "1-click" callout |
| 10 | 29.0–31.5 | **Resource usage.** CPU/RAM graphs. | Recording + animated stat highlights |
| 11 | 31.5–34.0 | **One-click resource upgrade.** RAM bumps up, graph relaxes. | Recording + upgrade burst graphic |
| 12 | 34.0–38.0 | **CTA end card.** Logo, URL, "Use code **{CODE}** for **{XX}% off**", platform badges. | Custom motion graphic (end card) |

Pacing: fast and punchy, a cut or move every 1–3 s. Each beat gets one clear on-screen label ("Pick your game", "Choose a region", "Use code CRODIE", "Deploy in seconds", "1-click mods", "Upgrade instantly"). Keep text big enough to read on phones.

I'll put everything in one folder. Suggested: `Desktop\Server Promo\` with these subfolders:

5. A **project folder + README** explaining how to re-render with new codes, swap footage, and change copy.
6. (Nice to have) a short "how to use this sponsorship" note for creators, and a still thumbnail/end-frame PNG.

## 5. Tools and approach that worked in the previous session (reuse them)

Machine:
- Windows 11.
- AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 / Radeon 890M. **No NVIDIA/CUDA, and Vulkan GPU compute paths failed**, so treat it as **CPU-only**.
- 31 GB RAM.
- **ffmpeg 9** on PATH, **Node 24**, **uv** (Python 3.12).
- Shells: PowerShell is primary, Git Bash is also available.

**Motion graphics: HyperFrames** (HTML → video, GSAP animations, seekable, deterministic):

  - First and last frame fully transparent for overlays.

  - Pixel-snap text sizes.

- Check text is readable, nothing sensitive is visible (card numbers, emails, IPs, passwords), overlays are aligned and the alpha is clean.
- Check the first and last frames.

- Run independent pieces in parallel with sub-agents, e.g. one agent per motion graphic. Keep renders sequential.

content.text:
Left and right are nearly identical, and the side signal (L−R) is about 27 dB quieter. So the audio is effectively mono duplicated to both ears, and there's no stereo trick that would separate mic from desktop.

**What I found:** one stereo track, with mic and desktop audio already mixed. Since I can't separate them after the fact, a single track records everything together.

**To get separate tracks next time, in OBS:**
1. **Settings → Output → Output Mode: Advanced**, then the **Recording** tab.
2. Set **Type: Standard** and **Recording Format: Matroska (.mkv)** or **Fragmented MP4**. Plain MP4 can hold multiple tracks too, but a crash loses the whole file, while MKV survives a crash.
3. Under **Audio Track**, tick **1 and 2**. This is the same place you'd also tick 3+ for extra sources.
4. **Edit → Advanced Audio Properties**, or the cog next to each source in the mixer.
5. Untick every track for **Mic/Aux**, and tick only **Track 1** for Desktop Audio.
6. Then tick only **Track 2** for Mic/Aux.

Then the file has Track 1 = desktop and Track 2 = mic. My pipeline already understands multiple tracks, so it can take them separately with no extra setup.

**Why this helps your sponsor promo:** for screen recordings with your own voice or game audio, separate tracks mean I can duck the desktop audio under your mic, drop one entirely, or remove keyboard noise without touching your voice. Everything stays easier to edit.

If you've already recorded things you can't redo, I can still reduce the desktop noise under your voice with a speech-focused filter, but it won't be as clean as separate tracks. Which are you recording?

You're recording in **Simple** output mode, and that's the cause. I read your OBS profile: `Mode=Simple`, `RecFormat2=mp4`, `RecTracks=1`. Simple mode can only record one audio track, so everything gets mixed into it. You haven't done anything wrong; it's OBS's default.

**How to set it up (about 2 minutes):**

1. Click **Settings** (bottom right of OBS), then **Output**.
2. Change **Output Mode** from Simple to **Advanced**.
3. Open the **Recording** tab and set:
   - **Type:** Standard
   - **Recording Path:** keep `C:\Users\edmem\Videos\OBS\Screen`
   - **Recording Format:** Matroska Video (.mkv) is the safest, because a crash won't lose the file. Your current MP4 setting also works, but a crash can corrupt it.
   - **Video Encoder:** the same one you use now (x264, or a hardware encoder if you prefer)
   - **Audio Track:** tick **1, 2 and 3**. This is the most important step.
4. Click **Apply**, then **OK**.
5. In the main window, open **Edit → Advanced Audio Properties**. It lists each source (Desktop Audio, Mic/Aux) with six track checkboxes (1–6). Set them like this:

   | Source | Track 1 | Track 2 | Track 3 |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | **Desktop Audio** | ✔ | ✔ | ☐ |
   | **Mic/Aux** | ✔ | ☐ | ✔ |

   So Track 1 is everything mixed (what any video player plays), Track 2 is desktop only, and Track 3 is mic only. This is slightly better than the two-track setup I described earlier: any player still sounds normal, and I get both clean tracks for editing.

## Flashback Mod Overview

Flashback allows you to record your Minecraft gameplay, play it back and create stunning cinematic shots. The mod was created by Moulberry and the Flashback Team.

## Export and Video Features

Flashback supports keyframes for camera movements, with interpolation that uses realtime instead of ticks, so that if you modify the speed of the replay in the middle of a camera movement, the camera movement itself won't speed up or slow down.

The mod also supports various export-related features through extensions like Flashback Extras: Export Presets adds built-in presets for common output targets, such as YouTube 1440p, and lets you create your own presets so you can save the settings you use again and again instead of rebuilding them every time.

## Additional Tools

FlashbackTurbo is a Fabric addon for Flashback that drastically speeds up video export by replacing Flashback's PNG-sequence encoder with a parallel pipeline (N-1 threads), configurable zlib compression level, and color-type-2 output when transparency is off.

content.text:
Yes, you can automate this almost completely. The trick is to stop shooting live.

**Why those four mods feel manual:** CMD-Cam, Freecam and Motion Capture are camera tools that you have to drive yourself, with commands, coordinates and shot setup. A different kind of mod removes that work: **Replay Mod** and **Flashback** record everything that happens while you play, then let you film it from any camera angle later. They're [Replay Mod](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/replay-mod-fabric-and-forge), which can record every session automatically once the setting is on, and [Flashback](https://www.mado-hosting.com/en/minecraft-mods/flashback), which offers the same idea with keyframed camera paths on newer Minecraft versions. Which one you need depends on your Minecraft version.

**The pipeline I'd build:**
1. **Capture (zero effort):** you play normally. OBS records your screen as usual, and the replay mod quietly records the world in the background.
2. **Shoot (automatic, after the session):**
   - I'd detect the good moments: the diamond and loot callouts, deaths, panic, explosions, new places. The studio already pulls these from your voice and the game.
   - For each moment I'd generate a camera move: orbit, drone pull-up, push-in or fly-by.
   - The mod renders them overnight into a folder.
3. **Edit:** the clips go into your `Stock Library/Minecraft B-Roll/` folder. The studio already tags that category, and the auto-editor cuts to them at the right beats.

So all you supply is the gameplay and the replay file.

**Other automatic options:**
- [Cinematic Cameraman](https://vpesports.com/minecraft/mods/cinematic-cameraman/) is a Paper server plugin where a second account acts as an automatic camera operator (orbits, fly-bys, cranes, tracking shots). It's fully live, but you'd need a second Minecraft account and two game clients running at once, which is heavy on your PC.
- [AFK Cinematic](https://www.modpackindex.com/mod/98082/afk-cinematic) and [Ambient Camera](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/ambient-camera) start cinematic shots when you go idle, but only then.

**What I haven't verified yet:** I can't yet confirm that I can write camera paths into a replay file from a script and start the render without clicking. That decides whether the shooting step is fully hands-off or needs one click. I'd test it on one short replay before building anything bigger.

**Limits to expect:**
- Replays contain only what your game loaded, so shots are limited to areas near where you played.
- Rendering takes real time, and your PC has no dedicated GPU, so shaders will be slow.
- Automatic camera paths sometimes clip into terrain. I'd review preview frames and discard the bad ones.

**To start, tell me:**
1. Your Minecraft version and mod loader (Fabric, Forge or NeoForge).
2. Whether you play single-player or on a server (your own, or hosted).
3. Whether you use shaders.

content.text: Flashback ships a built-in compatibility patch aimed specifically at Replay Mod's recorder. That suggests the two don't simply run side by side, so I'm checking what the patch does:

input.command:
cd "$TEMP" && "/c/Users/edmem/OneDrive/Desktop/Minecraft Channel/studio/.venv/Scripts/python.exe" - <<'EOF'
import zipfile, os, re
mods=os.path.expandvars(r"%APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods")

b=fz.read("com/moulberry/flashback/mixin/compat/replaymod/MixinReplayModRecording.class")
print("strings:",sorted(set(m.group(0).decode() for m in re.finditer(rb"[\x20-\x7e]{6,}",b)))[:40])
# where else does Flashback mention replay mod / its settings or kill-switch
for n in fz.namelist():
    if n.endswith(".class") and "bytedeco" not in n:
        d=fz.read(n)
        for m in re.finditer(rb"[\x20-\x7e]{0,50}(replaymod)[\x20-\x7e]{0,60}",d,re.I):

            if "compat/replaymod" not in s: print(n.split("/")[-1],"|",s[:140]); break
EOF

content.text:
**The red badge** is Replay Mod's "Recording Indicator". It only shows on screen while you play, and it isn't stored in the replay itself. It will appear in your OBS footage, though. To turn it off:

- **In game:** go to the main menu → **Replay Viewer** → **Settings** → **Recording** → set **Recording Indicator** to off. I'm going from memory on that path, and I haven't seen your menus.
- **Or in the file:** with the game closed, I can change `"indicator": true` to `false` in `config/replaymod.json`. Want me to?

Pressing F1 also hides it, but that hides your hotbar and everything else too.

**Are both recording right now? Yes.** I checked your folders a few seconds ago, and both were growing at that moment:

| Mod | Live file | Size | Last written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay Mod | `replay_recordings\recording\2026_10_10_14_22_15.mcpr.tmp\…\recording.tmcpr` | 27.9 MB | 14:25:05 |
| Flashback | `flashback\temp\recording\…\level_chunk_caches\0` | 22 MB | 14:25:04 |

Together that's roughly 16 MB a minute, which is small.

**How to tell without me:**
- **Replay Mod:** the red badge itself means it's recording. If you turn the badge off, you lose that cue. Your settings have chat notifications on, so you'll still get a message when it starts.
- **Flashback:** it shows no badge. It pops up a "Started recording" toast in the top right when you join, if toasts are on. While you're in a world, pressing **Esc** also shows its buttons, which say "Pause/Finish Recording" when it's recording or "Start Recording" when it isn't.

**When you finish:**
- **Disconnect from the server normally** instead of closing the game window. Replay Mod will then ask you to name the replay and save it into `replay_recordings`.
- If the game crashes, Flashback will offer to recover the recording next launch, but up to 5 minutes at the end can be lost.

**A correction to my earlier advice:** I told you to run only one of the two mods. That was a precaution, and both are in fact recording fine together. For this first test I'd keep both, because it lets me compare how each stores a recording and decide which one is easier to automate. Afterwards you can drop one.

When you're done playing, send me a note, and I'll look at what each mod saved.

Recording Indicator now shows **OFF**, so that's done. Click **Done** at the bottom so the settings save.

**Replay Mod, from your screenshot:**

| Setting | Set to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rename Dialog | **OFF** | Replays save on their own with a timestamp name, with no popup each time you quit. |
| Show Chat | **OFF** | It controls whether recorded chat appears in replays and renders. Server chat can show other players' names and messages, which you don't want in B-roll. |
| Enable Notifications | **OFF**, once you're sure it records | The popups can show up in your OBS footage. |

Everything else is right for you: both recording options ON, Automatic Recording ON, Camera Classic, Catmull-Rom (smooth camera paths) and Full Brightness Gamma.

**Flashback:** these come from the options list inside the mod. I haven't seen your menus, and I can't see which defaults are currently set. Look for a Flashback options (cog) button next to its recording buttons when you press **Esc** in game. If you can't find it, send me a screenshot of the Esc menu.

| Setting | Set to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Automatically Start | **ON** | It's already recording, so keep it. |
| Automatically Finish | **ON** | The recording saves when you leave the server, with nothing to press. |
| Quicksave | **ON** | Saves with default settings and no save screen. |
| Show Recording Toasts | **OFF** | The top-right popups would appear in your OBS footage. |
| Mark Dimension Changes | **ON** | It marks each time you enter the Nether or End, which helps me find good shots. |
| First-person Updates | **60** | This is how often your own character's position and view are saved. Flashback's own text says to raise it to the framerate you'll export at. At a low rate, your character can look jerky in shots that follow you. |
| Record Voice Chat | **OFF** (keep it) | It would record other players' voices if your server uses voice chat. |

Leave Record Hotbar and Record Bobby Chunks alone. Exporting, Keyframes, Editor Movement and Marker only matter later, when we render shots.

Keep both mods recording for the test. Once I've seen what each one saves, I'll tell you which to keep.
